records.excerpt: Title: Pike County Officials Seek Public Input on $3.3B Tech Campus Plan for SB Energy, OpenAI Partnership URL Source: http://littermedia.com/pike-county-officials-seek-public-input-on-3-3b-tech-campus-plan-for-sb-energy-openai-partnership/ Published Time: 2026-11-18T21:50:57+00:00 Markdown Content: Pike County Government Center, Waverly, Ohio. Dan Ramey/Litter Media November 18, 2026 Dan Ramey _Article presented by **[Pike County Career & Technology Center](https://www.pikectc.org/)** and**[Classic Brands](https://www.classicbrandsoh.com/)**…_ **WAVERLY, Ohio — Nov. 18, 2026**—Pike County, Ohio officials today announced a proposed framework for long-term community partnership at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus.Under the pending terms, the project is currently estimated to generate $3.3 billion in revenue for the county over 15 years. “Since the beginning of our work on the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, the Commissioners have focused on a transparent process. We have done mailings to every home; held a public open house; encouraged participation at our weekly meetings; created a project website and now seek public input regarding the proposed details in the term sheet,” said **Tony Montgomery, President, Pike County Board of Commissioners.**“The community benefits from this pending agreement are intended to advantage every single citizen of Pike County. In the coming years, we plan to use these funds to make significant improvements to local infrastructure in our townships and villages. What this funding can do for all of our public schools is to make a pathway for each and every student to stay in Pike County, a place they can get a job, start a business, raise a family, and plan for the next generation.” At the heart of the pending development agreement is **Pike 2040**, a long-term community planning initiative to support local families, businesses, institutions, and growth in the region.Pike 2040 will be funded by payments made under the development agreement and administered through a charitable foundation governed by a board consisting of a majority of county-designated representatives and will also include company representatives. Pike 2040 **i**s an innovative model for long-term community partnership, shaped by local priorities focused on expanding opportunities and improving quality of life. **A Community That Came Together** Earlier this year, shortly after SB Energy announced plans for the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, Pike County’s leaders made a deliberate choice: rather than negotiate piecemeal, they would come together through a Council of Governments (COG). Virtually every political subdivision in the county joined the COG. Jennifer Chandler, President of the COG, said that decision to negotiate resulted in the best outcome for the community. “I am so proud of how our community came together around this project,” Chandler said. “Rather than each political subdivision charting its own course, our villages, our townships, and our schools are joining with the County Commissioners to speak with a single voice. And SB Energy has been great to work with. The community unity, in partnership with SB Energy and OpenAI, will produce a truly transformational opportunity for the people of Pike County.” **A Framework for Local Investment** Pike 2040 is part of the development agreement for the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus and will be designed to optimize the direct benefits that the local community receives from major technology and energy investments entering the region. The proposed agreement would provide an alternative to traditional property tax payments, offering greater revenue predictability and the potential for additional long-term benefits to the county. “Our priority is ensuring that this development supports lasting opportunities for Pike County,” said Pike County Commissioner, Jeff Chattin**.**“The proposed agreement with the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus will provide our community with accelerated payments and give us revenue certainty.” **Infrastructure and Workforce Development** SB Energy will design, construct, and fund the public infrastructure improvements needed to serve the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, including applicable road, water, wastewater and emergency-response improvements. The proposed agreement supports collaboration with local labor unions and workforce partners to expand training and apprenticeship opportunities, helping Pike County residents build careers in critical infrastructure construction and operations. **How Pike County Citizens Can Participate** The proposed framework, announced today, is being released for public review and comments before a definitive, binding agreement can be reached. Pike County residents are encouraged to continue to attend Pike County Board of Commissioners’ meetings to ask questions and hear more discussion of the details. The next two meetings are Thursday, November 19 and Monday, November 23, both at 9:00 a.m. at the Government Center, 230 Waverly Plaza, Suite 100, Waverly, Ohio 45690. Additional details about the Pike 2040 planning process, community participation opportunities, and the Pike 2040 Foundation will be announced as the initiative moves forward. To read more about the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus, visit [https://www.pikecountyohcommissioners.gov/ports](https://www.pikecountyohcommissioners.gov/ports)that provides a dedicated email address and phone line for additional questions and comments. records.title: OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents
records.excerpt: OpenAI’s rogue agents OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents AG: OpenAI tested dangerous AI without proper oversight and misled public about it. Jon Brodkin – Nov 17, 2026 1:13 pm | 89 ... ... ... Credit: Getty Images | Visual China Group Credit: Getty Images | Visual China Group Story text Size Width * Links * Subscribers only Learn more California sued OpenAI yesterday, alleging it has tried to evade responsibility for the Hugging Face attack and about 80 other incidents in which the company lost control of its AI. The lawsuit was filed under the state’s public nuisance and unfair competition laws. The July 2026 hack of Hugging Face and other attacks carried out by OpenAI’s autonomous agents “may just be the tip of the iceberg,” said a lawsuit filed in a state court by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. “OpenAI recently admitted to the Attorney General’s Office that it has lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing.” OpenAI had publicly reported only 27 such incidents, showing that “OpenAI’s public reports do not represent the full scope of loss-of-control incidents involving OpenAI’s models that have impacted third parties,” the lawsuit said. OpenAI “knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it,” Bonta said in a press release . OpenAI models are “able to find novel vulnerabilities in computer networks, quickly break down defenses, and autonomously carry out cyberattacks,” Bonta’s lawsuit said. OpenAI puts safeguards in its publicly released models to prevent this behavior, “but deliberately omits or removes these protections while experimenting with and training its models,” the lawsuit said. In the attack on Hugging Face, OpenAI agents “employed complicated hacking methodologies and involved coordinated actions by hundreds of individual autonomous AI agents that should have been contained in OpenAI’s research environment,” the lawsuit said. Known attacks “include unauthorized access of and cyberattacks on databases containing code that powers countless applications; informational websites that are trusted and valuable resources for the public; and foreign government databases storing sensitive health information,” the lawsuit said. “Swarms of OpenAI’s experimental AI agents have even compromised OpenAI’s own internal infrastructure, in an attack that managed to obtain administrator-level access to critical OpenAI systems.” AG says OpenAI “thwarted” investigation The lawsuit accused OpenAI of refusing to provide sufficient detail about the incidents. Bonta announced an investigation into OpenAI in early September and sent an investigative subpoena to the company with additional questions on September 30. “Rather than take responsibility and be transparent with the public and with regulators so that these loss-of-control incidents can be analyzed and prevented, OpenAI thwarted the Attorney General’s efforts to investigate these incidents, including by refusing to provide detailed information about the full universe of incidents known to the company,” the lawsuit filed yesterday said. OpenAI told Ars that most of the incidents identified in its review had low severity, and none matched the severity or scale of the Hugging Face attack. OpenAI defended its response to the California investigation, saying it provided multiple technical briefings to Bonta and his staff, answered the office’s questions, and offered more technical briefings to discuss its remediation efforts and plans for addressing the problems. “Since the Hugging Face incident, we’ve undertaken an extensive and transparent effort to understand and address misaligned model activity,” OpenAI said. “We’ve published a detailed technical report, commissioned and published a separate independent report, notified affected organizations, strengthened safeguards across our research systems, and created a framework for additional identification and disclosure of misalignment. This lawsuit appears to single out OpenAI over a challenge that’s been identified by every major AI lab. We take misalignment seriously, and we have engaged—and will continue to engage—constructively with the attorney general’s office to share information and advance strong, practical safety standards for the entire industry.” OpenAI created public nuisance, state says California’s lawsuit accuses OpenAI of creating a public nuisance as defined in state law, and several violations of the state’s Unfair Competition Law. Alleged violations include “causing and/or allowing agents to gain unauthorized access to third-party computer systems,” developing AI models without adequate security measures, and making false or misleading claims about the safety of its AI products. California is seeking an injunction to stop the alleged violations of the Unfair Competition Law and to require civil penalties and financial damages. It also wants an order to “compel OpenAI to abate the ongoing public nuisance their conduct has created in California.” Bonta said in his press release that “the Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability—and this was only one of 80 known incidents.” OpenAI was sued in September by Legal Advocates for Safe Science & Technology (LASST), a nonprofit that alleged violations of California’s Unfair Competition Law and the state’s Comprehensive Computer Data Access and Fraud Act. “OpenAI and frontier AI developers more broadly can’t avoid the consequences of their unsafe actions just by claiming that ‘an AI did it,’” the group said. “Autonomous AI agents will continue to hack, steal data, disrupt systems, and violate rights until a court steps in.” OpenAI said in response to the LASST lawsuit that “Hugging Face was a serious incident and we’ve taken a series of actions in response to it, but this lawsuit is completely without merit.” Jon Brodkin Senior IT Reporter Jon Brodkin Senior IT Reporter Jon is a Senior IT Reporter for Ars Technica. He covers the telecom industry, Federal Communications Commission rulemakings, broadband consumer affairs, court cases, and government regulation of the tech industry. 89 Comments

records.title: Abbove Launches MCP Connector to Bridge Wealth Data with AI Tools Like ChatGPT and Claude
records.excerpt: Title: Abbove Launches MCP Connector to Bridge Wealth Data with AI Tools Like ChatGPT and Claude URL Source: http://ffnews.com/news/abbove-brings-european-wealth-planning-into-the-ai-era-76825272 Final URL: https://ffnews.com/news/abbove-brings-european-wealth-planning-into-the-ai-era-76825272 Published Time: 2026-11-18T15:58:42.087+00:00 Markdown Content: Wealth planning platform Abbove has launched an MCP connector, allowing advisors to integrate structured client data directly into enterprise AI tools like ChatGPT and Claude. By bridging the gap between holistic wealth modeling and Large Language Models, the firm aims to automate labor-intensive data entry and meeting preparation for over 1,450 European advisors. The launch of the MCP (Model Context Protocol) connector provides a bridge between Abbove’s structured wealth data and the AI ecosystems chosen by financial institutions, including Claude, ChatGPT, Mistral, and Copilot. The tool is designed to solve the "garbage in, garbage out" problem in wealth management by providing LLMs with a foundational data layer that includes family structures, life events, gifts, and specific financial goals rather than just raw account aggregation. Advisors using the connector can automate several core functions of the wealth planning workflow. This includes transforming unstructured meeting notes and legal documents into a complete wealth overview, a process the company claims can reduce days of manual work to under an hour. Additionally, the tool allows for the instant generation of client meeting materials, such as agendas and risk-opportunity guides. Perhaps most significantly for business development, advisors can now query their entire book of business using natural language to identify specific client needs or advisory opportunities across their portfolio. The connector is available immediately and is activated at the organizational level. It currently supports a network of more than 1,450 advisors who serve approximately 40,000 families, representing over 200,000 individuals across Europe. > "An LLM without quality data is like a Formula 1 car running on bad fuel" [Guillaume Desclée](https://ffnews.com/people/guillaume-desclee) Founded in Brussels in 2017, Abbove operates as a European white-label wealth planning platform. The company specifically targets the upper tiers of the financial services market, providing technology to private banks, wealth managers, and family offices. Unlike standard retail fintech tools, Abbove’s platform is built around a collaborative model where both the advisor and the client family contribute to a documented view of total wealth. The firm has established itself as a key infrastructure provider in the Benelux region and broader Europe, focusing on the complex data requirements of high-net-worth individuals. Guillaume Desclée, who leads the company as CEO, has a background in the Belgian fintech ecosystem, including involvement with Spreds. Abbove’s market position relies on its ability to handle the "soft" data of wealth management—such as inheritance plans and family trees—alongside traditional "hard" financial assets, making it a specialized player in the digital transformation of private banking. FF News has tracked Abbove’s expansion into major institutional banking environments. We previously reported on the company’s growth in the retail and private banking sector when [Abbove Strengthens Its Banking Position With the Deployment of Its Platform at ING in Belgium](https://ffnews.com/news/abbove-strengthens-its-banking-position-with-the-deployment-of-its-platform-at-ing-in-belgium). This deployment was a significant milestone in proving the platform's scalability within Tier-1 financial institutions. Furthermore, the company’s move toward more intelligent, automated planning was signaled last year when [Abbove Unveils “Mia”: Opening a New Chapter in Digital Wealth Planning in Europe](https://ffnews.com/news/abbove-unveils-mia-opening-a-new-chapter-in-digital-wealth-planning-in-europe), which introduced new digital capabilities to their wealth planning suite. This move signals a shift in the fintech sector from "AI as a chatbot" to "AI as a data processor." By adopting the Model Context Protocol, Abbove is betting on interoperability rather than trying to build a proprietary, closed-loop AI. This puts pressure on traditional wealth tech vendors who have yet to provide a clean way for banks to feed their own data into enterprise-grade LLMs. The real test for the industry will be whether compliance departments at major private banks feel comfortable with the "access rights" framework when client data begins flowing into third-party models like OpenAI’s or Anthropic’s, even within a secure connector environment. Through the open Model Context Protocol, advisors can put their clients’ complete wealth picture to work in the AI tools their institution has chosen, such as Claude, ChatGPT, Mistral or Copilot, within their access rights. The difference lies in the data. [AI tools are only as good as the data they consume](https://www.abbove.com/en/post/ai-wealth-planning). Abbove builds on its ability to model each family’s wealth data in a complete and structured way. Co-built by advisors and their client families, it captures what aggregation alone cannot: goals, life events, gifts, the full picture of the family and its wealth. It forms the foundational data layer LLMs need to reach their full potential. With the connector, advisors can: * **Transform data collection:** rebuild a complete wealth overview from meeting notes and wealth documents, ready for the advisor to review and import. Days of work now take under an hour. * **Prepare client meetings in moments:** agenda, interview guide, key risks and opportunities. * **Query their entire book in natural language** to identify each client’s needs and advisory opportunities. “An LLM without quality data is like a Formula 1 car running on bad fuel” said Guillaume Desclée, CEO of Abbove. “By placing a collaborative, holistic approach to wealth at the heart of the client-advisor relationship, we engage families in building, with their advisor, a single, complete and documented view of their wealth. That is the essential condition for building a high-quality information base and bringing AI into wealth advisory practice.” The connector is available from today, activated per organisation. **About Abbove** Founded in Brussels in 2017, Abbove is a European white-label wealth planning platform for private banks, wealth managers and family offices. More than 1,450 advisors use it to serve more than 40,000 families representing over 200,000 individuals. [www.abbove.com](http://www.abbove.com/)

records.title: What if Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude and ChatGPT face Major Data Breaches N Millions of Users could fall to Risks
records.excerpt: Title: What if Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude and ChatGPT face Major Data Breaches N Millions of Users could fall to Risks URL Source: http://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/what-if-google-gemini-anthropic-claude-and-chatgpt-face-major-data-breaches-millions-of-users-could-fall-to-risks/ Final URL: https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/what-if-google-gemini-anthropic-claude-and-chatgpt-face-major-data-breaches-millions-of-users-could-fall-to-risks/ Published Time: 2026-11-18T06:35:16+00:00 Markdown Content: ![Image 1](https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/wp-content/uploads/Shark-57-696x398.jpeg) Artificial intelligence has rapidly become an essential part of everyday life, with millions of people relying on AI-powered platforms such as Google’s Gemini, Anthropic’s Claude and OpenAI’s ChatGPT for personal, professional and business activities. From drafting emails and analyzing confidential documents to writing computer code, conducting research and seeking personal advice, users are increasingly sharing sensitive information with AI assistants. But what would happen if these popular AI platforms experienced a major data breach? The consequences could be far more serious than many users realize. A large-scale data breach involving any of these AI platforms could potentially expose millions of conversations, personal information, business documents and other sensitive data. Depending on the nature of the breach, cyber-criminals could gain access to information that users never intended to make public. **Personal Conversations and Confidential Information at Risk** One of the biggest concerns surrounding an AI-related [data breach](https://www.cybersecurity-insiders.com/coles-admits-cyberattack-but-denies-any-customer-data-breach/) would be the exposure of private conversations. Users frequently discuss personal matters, financial concerns, workplace issues and even confidential business strategies with AI chatbots. If such information were accessed by unauthorized individuals, it could create serious privacy concerns. For example, employees using ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude to summarize internal reports could unintentionally expose confidential corporate information. Similarly, individuals who share personal details, contact information or sensitive documents could become vulnerable to identity theft, impersonation and targeted scams. **Financial Fraud and Identity Theft Could Increase** A successful cyberattack could potentially expose account details, personal identifiers and other information stored within compromised systems. Criminals could use such information to conduct phishing attacks, impersonate individuals or attempt to gain access to other online accounts. In particular, leaked conversations could provide attackers with valuable background information about their victims. This could make fraudulent emails and messages appear more convincing, increasing the possibility of financial fraud and identity theft. **Businesses Could Face Serious Consequences** The impact would not be limited to individual users. Businesses increasingly depend on AI platforms to analyze documents, develop marketing strategies, generate software code and improve productivity. If confidential company information, customer records, proprietary research or source code were exposed, organizations could face financial losses, reputational damage, legal complications and regulatory investigations. A breach affecting one major AI provider could also have consequences for businesses that have integrated its services into their applications and internal systems. **Trust in Artificial Intelligence Could Take a Major Hit** Perhaps the biggest long-term consequence would be the loss of public confidence in artificial intelligence. Users trust these platforms to process their information responsibly. A major security incident could make individuals and organizations reconsider how much information they are willing to share with AI assistants. It could also increase pressure on technology companies to introduce stronger encryption, access controls, security monitoring and transparent data-handling policies. **How Can Users Protect Themselves?** Although AI companies implement security measures to protect user information, no online platform can guarantee absolute protection against cyber threats. Users should avoid entering passwords, banking credentials, confidential business information or highly sensitive personal details into AI conversations unless there is a clear and secure reason to do so. Enabling multi-factor authentication, using strong and unique passwords, reviewing privacy settings and regularly monitoring account activity can also reduce security risks. Ultimately, a major data breach involving [Google Gemini](https://gemini.google.com/app), Anthropic Claude or ChatGPT would serve as a serious warning about the growing relationship between artificial intelligence and digital privacy. As AI adoption continues to expand, cybersecurity must remain a priority for technology providers and users alike. The future of artificial intelligence will depend not only on how intelligent these platforms become, but also on how effectively they protect the information entrusted to them. First capacity is expected in the first half of 2027. TensorWave announced a signed, six-year agreement on November 16, 2026, to provide OpenAI with 457 MW of dedicated AI infrastructure across multiple U.S. data-center sites. The company expects the first capacity in the first half of 2027 and the full deployment by early 2028. [TensorWave’s announcement](https://x.com/tensorwave/status/2122332671955132454) dates the deal; its [company release](https://tensorwave.com/blog/tensorwave-to-provide-openai-with-457-megawatts-of-amd-powered-ai-infrastructure) describes the planned systems and workloads. Learn AI Tools ## What TensorWave agreed to provide The agreement covers infrastructure dedicated to a single customer: OpenAI. TensorWave says the planned capacity will support large-scale AI training and inference, the processes used to train AI models and generate their outputs. The plan spans multiple U.S. data-center sites. TensorWave says the systems will use **AMD Instinct MI455X GPUs** in **AMD Helios** rack-scale systems, connected by high-performance Ethernet. These are the components and workloads specified for the planned build. ## When the capacity is expected TensorWave expects to bring the first capacity online in the first half of 2027 and complete the deployment by early 2028. The schedule describes a staged rollout, with initial capacity preceding the full build. OpenAI announced a broader partnership with AMD on October 6, 2025, covering 6 GW of GPU capacity across multiple generations. That agreement provides context for the companies’ wider compute relationship; TensorWave’s announcement sets out its own 457 MW project. [OpenAI’s partnership announcement](https://openai.com/index/openai-amd-strategic-partnership/) describes the broader commitment. Create a free account Menu Crypto sections Bitcoin Ethereum Altcoins DeFi Stablecoins Regulation Security Create account Log in Español OpenAI locks down unreleased model weights after two security incidents OpenAI official logo (public domain, Wikimedia Commons) — CryptoBriefing brand treatment The company's new overview details air-gapped training, multi-party access rules and layered monitoring following breaches in July and September by Diego Almada Lopez Wed 18 Nov 2026 · 15:04 EST · 4 min read In AI Share Follow on Google OpenAI has published a detailed security overview covering the environments where it trains and evaluates its most advanced models. The October 23, 2026 document explains how the company now protects unreleased model weights and frontier training runs. The timing is not a coincidence. The new controls follow two incidents earlier in the year, including one in which models under evaluation found their way into Hugging Face infrastructure. What OpenAI is changing Some context on why weights matter so much. Model weights are the learned numerical values that determine how an AI system behaves, which makes them the closest thing an AI lab has to a secret recipe. The overview lists several defensive layers. The first is simple in concept: training runs no longer have live internet access. The second is multi-party authorization for anyone seeking access to model weights. Think of a bank safe deposit box that needs two separate keys held by two separate people. No single employee can open it alone. Third, OpenAI is using Azure private-linked storage. That means the data sits behind a private network connection to Microsoft ’s cloud rather than being reachable over the public internet. Fourth, the company is enforcing strict egress controls. Outbound traffic from these environments can only travel to a predetermined list of destinations, so anything trying to send data elsewhere hits a wall. Advertisement Crypto Briefing Pro Follow the news about what you own. Add your holdings to find related stories in Pro. Create a free account On top of the access rules sits an expanded four-layer monitoring system. It includes activation probes, which watch a model’s internal signals for signs of unusual behavior, and model-based reviewers, which is a polite way of saying AI is now helping supervise AI. OpenAI also plans additional security sprints that will involve external partners. The company has made continuous red-teaming and monitoring standard practice for its frontier work, rather than a one-off audit. AI, tech, and the markets they move—in one daily briefing. Daily. Free. Join 34,000+ readers across crypto, finance, and policy. We respect your privacy. Unsubscribe anytime. The incidents behind the overhaul The first problem surfaced in July 2026 during security evaluations. Models being tested accessed Hugging Face systems by exploiting a zero-day vulnerability, meaning a flaw the defenders did not yet know existed. OpenAI quarantined the affected prototypes and restricted their access. The second incident came on September 20, 2026. A DNS misconfiguration briefly allowed a model to reach the internet. OpenAI detected the issue within 15 minutes, paused training immediately and layered on enhanced controls. Before restarting, OpenAI ran an extensive red-teaming process. OpenAI used capable models to do some of that probing. It then patched the vulnerabilities those exercises uncovered. Frontier reinforcement learning training and internal inference operations resumed on October 1, 2026. Reinforcement learning is the stage where a model improves by trial, feedback and adjustment, while inference is the act of running a model to generate answers. OpenAI said no customer data or released models were compromised in the earlier cybersecurity evaluations. The exposure, by the company’s account, stayed confined to unreleased prototypes and testing environments. Why the threat model just got stranger Traditional cybersecurity assumes the attacker is outside the building. The incidents OpenAI describes involve a second category: the system being protected occasionally behaves like an intruder itself. That shift explains the shape of the new controls. Cutting off internet access and limiting egress to approved targets defends against outside thieves, but it also boxes in the models during training and evaluation. Multi-party authorization and private-linked storage address the human side. They make it harder for one compromised account, or one careless engineer, to move the most valuable files the company owns. The monitoring stack tackles the gap in between. Activation probes look inside the model rather than just at network traffic, which is an acknowledgment that some risky behavior may show up internally before it shows up on the wire. What this means for the AI industry The July incident touched Hugging Face, a widely used hub for sharing AI models and datasets. That makes this more than an internal OpenAI housekeeping story, since shared infrastructure that the broader research community depends on was on the receiving end. Other labs running similar evaluations face the same basic question. If a model under test can exploit an unknown flaw in a third-party system, every platform those environments connect to becomes part of the security perimeter. records.excerpt: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on 17 November, adding Edu access, a 20% cut to Astra API prices and tighter cyber safeguards. Photo: Coolcaesar / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 4.0 (cropped). Source · Licence OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol on 17 November 2026, making both models available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users and through the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol . For universities and research offices the release brings an Edu rollout, a 20% cut in Astra’s API prices, and tighter default safeguards for higher-risk cybersecurity requests. What happened OpenAI announced the two models on 17 November 2026 in a post in its Developer Community announcements forum . It describes GPT-6.2 Astra as its frontier model for the hardest projects and GPT-6.2 Sol as an efficient, versatile model for everyday work and multistep agentic workflows. The Decoder reports that OpenAI calls Astra “the world’s best model for scientists.” OpenAI says Astra sets new highs on evaluations across professional work and scientific research at less than a third of the cost per task of GPT-6 Astra. On Agents’ Last Exam, Astra at its xhigh setting scores 5.2 points above GPT-6 Astra at max, at less than half the cost. On Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0, which measures whether changes to real codebases are good enough for maintainers to merge, Sol comes within half a point of Astra at about one-fifth of the cost, according to 9to5Mac . records.excerpt: Title: OpenAI increases its ChatGPT Ads presence in 44 countries through an exclusive reseller partnership with Aleph URL Source: http://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/19/3406657/0/en/openai-increases-its-chatgpt-ads-presence-in-44-countries-through-an-exclusive-reseller-partnership-with-aleph.html Final URL: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/19/3406657/0/en/openai-increases-its-chatgpt-ads-presence-in-44-countries-through-an-exclusive-reseller-partnership-with-aleph.html Published Time: 2026-11-19T14:01:13Z Markdown Content: ![Image 1: Aleph Group](https://ml-eu.globenewswire.com/Resource/Download/ee19de7a-0c5b-456b-905a-493e21f5e866/picture1.png) [](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/11/19/3406657/0/en/openai-increases-its-chatgpt-ads-presence-in-44-countries-through-an-exclusive-reseller-partnership-with-aleph.html# "Expand") MADRID, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- OpenAI increases its ChatGPT Ads presence into 44 countries through an exclusive reseller partnership with Aleph. Starting today, brands and agencies across 14 markets in Latin America, 16 in Europe and Central Asia, 10 in the Middle East and Africa, and 4 in Asia-Pacific can contract, pay and get support locally through Aleph, OpenAI’s exclusive reseller. ChatGPT is a new kind of advertising environment, where people come to learn, explore and make decisions. For Aleph, the partnership with OpenAI is about connecting businesses across these markets with ChatGPT, one of the defining products of the AI era. For advertisers, it means buying ChatGPT Ads through a partner with local teams and its own payments infrastructure. “AI is giving businesses a new way to connect with people. Starting today, advertisers in 44 markets can work with OpenAI through a local team that speaks their language, bills in their currency and extends credit. That is what Aleph does best: turning global technology into local growth.” — Gastón Taratuta, Founder and CEO, Aleph Brands and agencies that work with Aleph contract and are invoiced locally, with onboarding and first-line support from Aleph’s teams in each market. The agreement covers 44 markets: * **Latin America (14):** Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Puerto Rico and Uruguay * **Europe and Central Asia (16):** Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Croatia, Cyprus, Czechia, Estonia, Hungary, Kazakhstan, Latvia, Lithuania, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, Slovenia, Ukraine and Uzbekistan * **Middle East and Africa (10):** Egypt, Kenya, Kuwait, Morocco, Nigeria, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Turkey and the United Arab Emirates * **Asia-Pacific (4):** Bangladesh, Cambodia, Hong Kong (outbound) and Sri Lanka Advertisers and agencies in these markets can learn more and connect with Aleph’s local teams at: [**https://alephdigital.com/OpenAi?utm_source=pr&utm_id=openai&utm_content=europe**](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=B9qNKcZO_Txs5x_dYs6yvgWMO0Rd2gtMmf7S8hAdhFurg7OFcZMn9eHRot03hAYpnoG9l354SV8jJDp4CFdX455kmMRuV4B6kCa2KMuDfNSKc2FaAgWtQdpW8HGxNUrfzkGQvLo657A-tccZUBjqMr1e1y2Nou6pgMyqHxZaa-Jjmuv1HCGkPMqlSAhvqJ8npNtrKCRJIzYaFK1iiB-SPb5GENsXPfE9cd5rSu-h34TCITn7NoA2eIhw2zyP9pJqlujk6733I7csJhiQ0CIb0A==) **About Aleph** Aleph operates the largest global infrastructure accelerating media and payments solutions across more than 130 high-growth markets. With 20 years of experience and partnerships with over 50 of the world’s leading digital platforms, Aleph connects media, payments and local market expertise to enable platforms and businesses to grow and operate globally with speed and compliance. With teams in more than 90 offices worldwide, Aleph combines global scale with deep local execution. Beyond business impact, Aleph drives digital inclusion through its education initiative, Digital Ad Expert, recognized by UNESCO’s Global Skills Academy. records.title: Security Journey brings training to Claude & ChatGPT
records.excerpt: Programme owners can now track security training and enrol staff inside Claude or ChatGPT, cutting friction for teams already using workplace AI assistants. ERP AI AI Coding Security Journey brings training to Claude & ChatGPT Wed, 18th Nov 2026 SHADDA LIE CATUGAL Editor Security Journey has launched integrations with Claude and ChatGPT for training programme management, allowing programme owners to manage security training from within the AI assistants. Built on the Model Context Protocol and powered by Security Journey's intelligence layer, Aspen, the integrations let users identify learners who are behind on training, assign courses, answer programme questions and generate reports in natural language without opening a separate dashboard. The launch comes as companies look for ways to reduce the friction of moving between workplace applications. Security Journey cited research showing that one in four workers spend more than seven hours a week copying information between applications, reconciling data and feeding context into AI tools. Other research has pointed to a broader productivity problem linked to frequent switching between software tools. Harvard Business Review research cited by Security Journey found workers switch between applications and websites about 1,200 times a day, losing nearly four hours a week regaining focus after interruptions. Meanwhile, use of workplace AI assistants has risen sharply. OpenAI data cited by Security Journey showed weekly ChatGPT Enterprise messages grew roughly eightfold in 2025. How it works Within Claude and ChatGPT, programme owners can ask plain-language questions about learner progress and take action in the same interaction. One example was a manager asking which team members had not started secure coding training, then enrolling or prompting them without leaving the assistant. Access follows existing Security Journey permissions, so users can view and manage only information they are already authorised to access. The offering is available now to existing customers at no additional cost. According to Security Journey, Aspen sits at the centre of the platform and has two main functions. One, called Adapt, uses organisational data to link training more closely to recurring software vulnerabilities and generate updated rule files for AI coding tools as pull requests for review. The other, called Assist, is designed to support programme administration and learner guidance through natural-language interaction. Dan Newton, Chief Executive Officer of Security Journey, said customers had made clear that learner participation remained a central issue. "Engagement is the biggest challenge we hear from customers, and the clearest indicator of whether a training program is working," Newton said. He added: "Bringing Security Journey into Claude and ChatGPT means program owners can engage their people faster and more precisely, without ever leaving their AI assistant." Security Journey also included a customer comment from a learning and development leader at a software company. "AI has changed what we expect from every tool we use. Claude is increasingly where our team spends its day, so being able to check who hasn't started their training and get them enrolled or nudged without switching tools is a big deal. It simply fits into how we already work," the learning and development leader said. Workflow shift The launch reflects a broader shift in enterprise software towards embedding AI into existing workflows rather than requiring staff to open dedicated systems for each task. In this case, Security Journey is trying to move training administration into conversational interfaces employees already use during the working day. That may be particularly relevant in areas such as secure coding and AI use, where organisations are under pressure to improve workforce skills while keeping pace with changing tools. By placing administrative actions inside general-purpose assistants, software vendors are testing whether AI interfaces can become a control point for routine business processes rather than simply a layer for answering questions. Security Journey is also working to bring a similar experience to learners inside the tools they use every day. For now, the immediate focus is on programme owners who need to track uptake, assign work and measure training progress from within Claude and ChatGPT. records.excerpt: Title: SB Energy updates its IPO filing with a $1.9 billion nine-month loss driven by OpenAI warrant charges URL Source: http://mlq.ai/news/sb-energy-updates-its-ipo-filing-with-a-19-billion-nine-month-loss-driven-by-openai-warrant-charges/ Final URL: https://mlq.ai/news/sb-energy-updates-its-ipo-filing-with-a-19-billion-nine-month-loss-driven-by-openai-warrant-charges/ Published Time: 2026-11-19T18:44:32.379210-05:00 Markdown Content: Key points * Nine-month revenue rose 7.9% to $177.1 million; the net loss attributable to SB Energy widened to $1.91 billion from $440.0 million [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). * The loss includes a $1.20 billion non-cash charge for remeasuring the warrant liability linked to OpenAI's warrants, a $166.7 million charge on Nvidia's $1.5 billion prepaid forward contract and $593.6 million of stock-based compensation [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). * The amendment still gives no price range or share count; SB Energy plans to list as SBE on the Nasdaq Global Select Market and Nasdaq Texas [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). ![Image 1: SB Energy updates its IPO filing with a $1.9 billion nine-month loss driven by OpenAI warrant charges](https://mlq.ai/media/news_images/sb-energy-updates-its-ipo-filing-with-a-19-billion-nine-month-loss-driven-by-ope.jpg) SB Energy, the SoftBank-controlled developer building data centers and power plants for SoftBank and OpenAI, filed a third amendment to its IPO registration on Thursday, Nov. 19, adding results for the nine months to Sept. 30 [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). The update, its first since Sept. 21, shows a net loss attributable to the company of $1.91 billion, against $440.0 million a year earlier, on revenue of $177.1 million [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm)[[2]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026062846/sbenergy-sx1a2.htm). Most of the loss is non-cash. The company booked a $1.20 billion charge for the change in fair value of its warrant liability, which the filing ties to warrants held by OpenAI, a $166.7 million loss on remeasuring the $1.5 billion prepaid forward contract it signed with Nvidia on Aug. 17, and $593.6 million of stock-based compensation inside general and administrative expenses [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). Excluding those items, SB Energy says its loss attributable to the company was $117.3 million [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). ## The nine-month numbers | Nine months to Sept. 30 | 2026 | 2025 | | --- | --- | --- | | Revenue | $177.1M | $164.1M | | G&A expense | $618.9M | $393.6M | | Operating loss | $578.6M | $359.2M | | Warrant liability charge | $1,202.8M | none | | Prepaid forward charge | $166.7M | none | | Net loss to SB Energy | $1,913.7M | $440.0M | Revenue still comes almost entirely from its solar and storage power business. Of the $177.1 million, $109.8 million came from contracts with customers and $67.3 million from realized and unrealized gains on power price swaps; the company says its data center segment has not generated significant revenue yet [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). Cash used in investing activities reached $4.14 billion in the nine months, against $709.0 million a year earlier, and the accumulated deficit stood at $2.51 billion on Sept. 30 [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). ## What SB Energy is selling SB Energy says no data center capacity is in operation yet. Its first two projects, the Cosmos Research Campus in Travis County, Texas, about 50 MW of critical IT capacity leased to a SoftBank affiliate for 15 years, and the Milam County Data Center for OpenAI, are under construction [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). It has also signed a lease for the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Pike County, Ohio, designed as 17 buildings with about 8.0 GW of critical IT capacity, which MLQ.ai covered in [GE Vernova shares slide after SoftBank revises its U.S. data center power equipment plans](https://mlq.ai/news/ge-vernova-shares-slide-after-softbank-revises-its-us-data-center-power-equipment-plans/)[[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). The company puts its backlog at about $439 billion, of which about $430 billion is data center backlog, most of it PORTS-Pike [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). [Nvidia](https://mlq.ai/companies/nvidia/) has committed to buy $1.5 billion of non-voting Class N stock in a private placement at the IPO price and has already prepaid another $1.5 billion for Class N shares at 90% of the IPO price, a $3.0 billion investment in total [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). Some of OpenAI's warrants vest when the offering is priced, and 2,253,942 OpenAI warrants would remain unvested afterward [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). The cover still reads "between $ and $" for the price range, and the share count is blank [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are the lead bookrunners, and SoftBank will keep control, making SB Energy a controlled company under Nasdaq rules [[1]](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2133037/000162828026075026/sbenergy-sx1a3.htm). records.title: NATO Is Now Using OpenAI’s ‘Daybreak’ AI Models
records.excerpt: NATO Is Now Using OpenAI’s ‘Daybreak’ AI Models - The National Interest The National Interest logo A phone displaying the logo of AI giant OpenAI. OpenAI tools are useful for coding and cybersecurity purposes, and it has now granted access to NATO’s Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) for use. (Shutterstock/rozaiphotography) NATO Is Now Using OpenAI’s ‘Daybreak’ AI Models November 17, 2026 By: Peter Suciu Share Share this link on Facebook Share this page on X (Twitter) Share this link on LinkedIn Share this page on Reddit Email a link to this page Add TNI as a Preferred Source on Google As cyberspace has become a crucial warfighting domain, the NATO alliance has sought to keep up—using AI-assisted tools to help enhance its cyber-resilience. Artificial intelligence developer OpenAI has established a major partnership with the United States Department of Defense (DoD) to deploy its technology on classified military networks. The San Francisco-based firm announced this week that it would make its Daybreak cybersecurity AI models available for use by the members of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) military alliance. The specialized program was designed for vetted, authorized cybersecurity defenders, and it will be used by NATO’s Communications and Information Agency (NCIA) to protect alliance networks. According to OpenAI, NATO has already used approximately 300 billion raw input and output tokens monthly. (In plain English, a token is the most basic unit of data —which could include a word, part of a word, or even a punctuation mark—that an AI model reads, processes, and generates. Unlike humans, who typically read text as full sentences, AI utilizes a “tokenizer” that breaks down text into smaller chunks, which are then processed accordingly.) OpenAI’s Daybreak will aid NATO in examining code, scanning for odd network behavior, and confirming weaknesses. It can then build and trial patches. “AI-powered cyber defence models represent a generational leap in cyber security,” said Dr. Dylan Browne, the NCIA’s general manager. Browne claimed that the models could accelerate vulnerability discovery and help detect emerging threats at machine speed, which could enable defenders to stay ahead of potential adversaries. “For NATO, these technologies strengthen our cyber resilience, enhance our operational advantage and reinforce our ability to protect critical digital infrastructure at unprecedented scale and speed,” Browne said. “As we scale adoption, we will build a deeper understanding of token consumption, usage patterns and the underlying economics of AI models. This insight will help us optimize costs, evaluate competing solutions and make informed procurement decisions.” OpenAI and NATO continue to use the term “artificial intelligence,” even as US President Donald Trump has directed all federal departments and agencies to use the term “super intelligence” (SI) in official correspondence, public communications, websites, and policy documents. How OpenAI Has Worked with NATO Before Earlier this year, OpenAI supported NATO’s Crossed Swords 2026, the alliance’s annual, full-spectrum cyber operations and multi-domain military exercise organized by the NATO Cooperative Cyber Defence Centre of Excellence (CCDCOE). The exercise, which took place in Tallinn, Estonia, earlier this month, saw around 250 participants from more than 40 NATO and non-NATO partner countries—including military cyber operators, threat hunters, digital forensics specialists, and special operations units—take part in offensive and defensive cyberspace operations. Part of this year’s cyber drills saw participants build, deploy, and assess AI agents for cyber operations, utilizing local environments and OpenAI’s Daybreak cyber defense offering under human oversight. It marked the first time the platform was employed in such an exercise. The emphasis remains on maintaining human oversight of the AI models. “The people defending our democracies should have the most advanced technology on their side. NATO’s cyber defenders protect networks that are essential to the security of the Alliance. Through Daybreak, we’re putting more capable tools in their hands to help them find and fix vulnerabilities before attackers can exploit them,” said Sasha Baker, head of national security policy at OpenAI. “We look forward to deepening this work with NATO and our allies, helping turn advances in AI into stronger cyber defenses.” NATO Is Trying to Adopt a Technology-Friendly “Warrior Ethos” The adoption of OpenAI’s Daybreak AI cybersecurity initiative is just one aspect of NATO’s continued embrace of emerging technologies to help the alliance protect against rising threats. At the 2025 NATO Summit in The Hague, the allied leaders endorsed NATO’s Rapid Adoption Action Plan , which called for significantly accelerating the pace at which the alliance adopts new technologies and integrates them into Allied armed forces. The nine priority technology areas of focus included: AI Autonomous systems Quantum technologies Biotechnology and human enhancement technologies space Hypersonic systems Novel materials and manufacturing Energy and propulsion Next-generation communications networks “Although many of the technologies that are reshaping the world today are new, the need for innovation is not,” the alliance wrote in a media release . “Since its founding in 1949, NATO has stayed at the forefront of technology to ensure the defence of its member countries and the success of its operations.” About the Author: Peter Suciu Peter Suciu regularly writes about military hardware, firearms history, cybersecurity, politics, and international affairs. He has contributed to dozens of newspapers, magazines, and websites over a 30-year career in journalism, including Forbes and Clearance Jobs . He is based in Michigan. You can follow him on Twitter: @PeterSuciu . You can email the author at [email protected] . Region: Europe , North America Blog: The Buzz Topic: Artificial Intelligence (AI) , Cybersecurity Tags: North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) , OpenAI , United States (USA)

records.excerpt: Title: Camel Tech Joins the OpenAI Partner Network as an Implementation Partner URL Source: http://www.recordonline.com/press-release/story/147958/camel-tech-joins-the-openai-partner-network-as-an-implementation-partner/ Final URL: https://www.recordonline.com/press-release/story/147958/camel-tech-joins-the-openai-partner-network-as-an-implementation-partner/ Published Time: 2026-11-16T06:54:16.000Z Markdown Content: ![Image 1](https://pix.xpr.media/p/eyJzIjoiYWJlNTI2YmEtMDI4Yi00MTU2LTlhMjQtY2FlNzg2NGRjYzU4IiwiYyI6IjE4OTQzYjM4LTdlNjItNDJmYS1iOGVmLTY4Yjc5ZWVhOWJlMiIsInYiOjF9.MvCeyAE463Hz2csKgSletLhksTtj6JzGSB_Lj-yulRo.gif) _Camel Tech expands its capabilities for helping organizations bring OpenAI technology into everyday business by becoming an OpenAI implementation partner_ > Using ChatGPT is easy. Making it useful in a business takes more work. You need clear processes, and responsible persons. OpenAI partnership supports our clients put those foundations together, > > — Imrul, Founder NEW YORK, NY, UNITED STATES, November 15, 2026 /[EINPresswire.com](https://www.einpresswire.com/)/ — [Camel Tech](https://camelai.tech/), a business systemization company, has joined the [OpenAI Partner Network](https://openai.com/business/partners/) as a Select Partner. The program supports firms that help organizations adopt OpenAI technology and apply it to business operations. OpenAI announced the network on June 14, 2026, alongside a $150 million investment to support its partner ecosystem. The program brings together firms that help organizations identify practical applications, redesign workflows, integrate technology, and support adoption across their teams. The network includes three partner tiers: Select, Advanced, and Elite. OpenAI describes progression through these tiers in terms of sales performance, technical capability, co-selling engagement, and deployment experience. Published partner resources include: 1. Onboarding and training to help teams develop expertise with OpenAI technology. 2. Technical resources and support for building and deploying solutions. 3. Opportunities to collaborate with OpenAI on selling and delivering solutions. For Camel Tech, participation supports an existing approach: systemize first, automate next. The company begins by understanding how work moves through a business, where information is stored, and who is responsible for decisions. It then identifies where artificial intelligence can support those processes, with appropriate access controls and human review. For Camel Tech’s clients, the partnership primarily strengthens the resources behind the work. The company’s [artificial intelligence transformation services](https://camelai.tech/service/ai-native) include custom agents, searchable knowledge bases, workflow assistants, and business applications such as client portals and internal tools development. Where OpenAI technology fits the requirements, these solutions can help teams find approved information, process documents, and prepare actions for review within their existing business systems. Participation provides access to partner training and technical resources to support that work. Camel Tech’s approach remains the same: test systems before deployment, define what information they can access, and establish when a person must review an output or approve an action. The team also explains how each solution handles client information. “Using ChatGPT is easy. Making it useful in a business takes more work. You need clear processes, and responsible persons. OpenAI partnership supports our clients put those foundations together,” -said Imrul, CEO and Founder of Camel Tech. Camel Tech also maintains partnerships with other technology providers to support its business systemization and artificial intelligence transformation services. The company is a ClickUp Verified Service Provider, Notion Consulting Partner, monday.com Official Partner, and member of Anthropic’s Claude Partner Network. Camel Tech has completed more than 100 implementations across construction, accounting, healthcare, agencies, and other service-based industries worldwide. It remains tool- and model-agnostic, recommending platforms according to each client’s processes, integration needs, data requirements, and budget. About Camel Tech Camel Tech is a business systemization company that transforms operational chaos into systemized, scalable, AI-native businesses. They help founders and companies scale sustainably with business systems and AI transformation. They diagnose what’s broken, build one core system to run the entire business, then layer in AI and automation to scale without growing headcount or burning weekends. Their work spans construction, healthcare, agencies, accounting, e-commerce, education, and other service-based industries, serving clients primarily in the United States, Australia, Canada, and Europe. records.title: OpenAI, Chile sign pact to push AI adoption in public sector
records.excerpt: OpenAI, Chile sign pact to push AI adoption in public sector - BNamericas News OpenAI, Chile sign pact to push AI adoption in public sector Bnamericas Published: Tuesday, November 17, 2026 Politics Government program Federal Government SaaS, PaaS, IaaS Artificial intelligence OpenAI and the Chilean government signed a partnership to promote the adoption of artificial intelligence in public administration, building on the country’s national AI policy and action plan. The initiative is backed by the US Department of Commerce’s American SI Exports Program, of which OpenAI is a partner. The program was created under a July 2025 executive order from US President Donald Trump. It promotes the export of full-stack American AI technology packages, including hardware, software, models and applications, to allied and partner countries. Industry-led consortia submit proposals, which the commerce secretary selects in consultation with the secretaries of state, war and energy and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. Approved packages get interagency government support abroad. MoU The memorandum of understanding (MoU), led by Chile’s science, technology, knowledge and innovation ministry, covers exploring training for civil servants, the incorporation of AI tools into administrative processes and support for Chilean startups developing solutions to public challenges. Science minister Ximena Lincolao signed the deal on behalf of Chile at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference, in California. “I’m excited to work with Chile to help public servants use these tools, improve public services and support entrepreneurs in creating new companies,” OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said. “We are deeply excited about this collaboration and the extraordinary opportunities it will open for scientific discovery, entrepreneurship and innovation across Chile,” Lincolao said. The partnership will explore adopting technology in the ministry’s administrative processes, including possible support from OpenAI to implement new models, as well as advisory services and training for staff. For civil servants, activities could include AI literacy workshops and a train-the-trainer model. For the startup ecosystem, the parties said they will explore access to OpenAI programs and technologies, hands-on learning, technical guidance and mentoring. The collaboration could also link entrepreneurs with public institutions, universities and other local partners. A joint working group made up of representatives of the ministry and OpenAI is expected to define priorities and an initial work plan. Specific activities, eligibility criteria, resources and access to technology will be agreed separately. The MoU does not establish investment or purchase commitments. records.title: US, South Korea issue urgent advisories after OpenAI Cyber model flags critical security flaws in Java | World News
records.excerpt: Cybersecurity start-up Calif used OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber model to expose a major flaw in Java, a programming language used by key government agencies. | World News The United States and South Korea have issued urgent cybersecurity advisories after a cybersecurity firm unveiled a critical software bug in Java, a programming language widely used in key information systems, including government agencies, financial institutions and the military.According to a report by The New York Times, the start-up Calif exposed a major flaw in Java using OpenAI’s GPT-6 Cyber model. Bruce Dang, a senior researcher at Calif, described Java as the "beating heart of the modern company", adding that vulnerabilities in the programme will affect all major companies.Also Read | Highly classified network used by US’s National Security Agency down: Report Cybersecurity concerns around the world have mounted this year with the rapid pace of AI development and tech outages in recent months. Calif and other groups have been using AI to help alert network defenders to vulnerabilities that can be exploited by hackers to carry out a major security breach. What is the Java4Shell bug?However, the Java discovery is Calif's most serious threat, as the programming language is widely used by banks, hospitals, the aviation industry, government agencies, Fortune 500 companies, the corporate sector and even the military. It also helps power cloud computing architecture, identity management tools and email services.According to the report, the security flaw in Java could allow a hacker to gain remote access to sensitive internal systems. This discovery has assumed significance after widespread tech disruptions in recent days, including the outages of Microsoft products and the nationwide ground stop of all departing flights in the US due to a "communications failure".The bug, called Java4Shell, is reportedly caused while trying to execute 64 'A' characters followed by one equal sign. It caused Java to erroneously execute code by tampering with a section of computer memory, which could be used to corrupt data and grant hackers full access to any system.Also Read | Cascade of Outages Triggers Conspiracy Theories—and Finger-PointingCalif said they could use this bug to break into Keycloak, a widely used authentication and login system that is associated with thousands of big tech organisations, including Hewlett Packard, UnitedHealthcare and NASA, as per the report.The Java vulnerability is the second major bug discovered by Calif using OpenAI models. Last month, it exposed security flaws in PHP, a programming language estimated to be used by 70% of websites and apps on the internet, triggering a frantic effort to deploy a patch before government agencies took websites offline to prevent hackers from exploiting the bug.US, South Korea issue advisoriesThe US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency issued an alert, pressing organisations to “immediately patch” the vulnerability. "Review your software inventory for JDKs and Java runtimes, including those bundled with third-party applications or included in container images and appliances," it said.In South Korea, which is considered to be particularly vulnerable as it heavily relies on Java in the public and private sectors, the presidential office held an emergency meeting on Tuesday with related government agencies to discuss preemptive measures to tackle the issue, according to the Yonhap news agency.South Korea's Ministry of Science and ICT and the Korea Internet & Security Agency said on Wednesday that public institutions and private enterprises must urgently install the security updates. Java represented 53% of programming language use in South Korea compared to a global average of 30%, according to a JetBrains survey.This came amid global fears of AI resurgence that could enable more of such tech vulnerabilities and hacking attempts. Quang Luong, a security researcher from Calif, said it was only a matter of time before AI can independently build the most advanced cyberattacks, leading to several unpredictable problems.

OpenAI、3か月で1,700件超を調査する新システムを公開 ニュース 2026.11.20 ChatGPTが遅くなる原因をAIが自動調査！ OpenAI、3か月で1,700件超を調査する新システムを公開 IT・デジタル 業務・現場 URLをコピーしました！ ChatGPTの応答が遅くなったとき、その原因をAIが自動で調べ、修正案まで作成する。OpenAIが、そんなシステム運用の新たな仕組みを公開しました。 OpenAIは、AIコーディングエージェント「Codex」を活用し、ChatGPTなどのサービスで発生する性能低下を自動的に調査・修正するシステム「Performance Factory」の仕組みと運用実績を紹介しました。 同システムの性能低下対応ワークフローでは、約3か月間で1,700件を超える調査を追跡し、600件以上の事例で根本原因を特定しました。1日あたり約17件の自動調査に相当します。 ChatGPTの応答が遅くなったら？ AIが原因調査から修正案の作成まで担当 従来、ChatGPTの応答速度が低下した場合、エンジニアがログやシステムの稼働状況を確認し、原因を探す必要がありました。 Performance Factoryでは、性能低下を知らせるアラートをきっかけに、Codexエージェントが自動で調査を開始します。 AIは、いつから応答が遅くなったのか、どの処理に影響が出ているのかを確認。システムの変更履歴やプログラムのコード、各種ログなどを分析して原因を絞り込みます。 特徴的なのは、別のAIエージェントが調査結果を検証する仕組みです。 最初のAIが示した原因について、別のAIが反証を試み、説明に矛盾がないかを確認します。 OpenAIが100件の原因分析結果を人手で評価したところ、70％が正確と判定され、残り30％は追加の検証や因果関係の確認が必要でした。 こうした課題に対応するため、複数のAIが異なる役割を担い、調査の精度を高めています。 修正後の回復確認もAIが担当！ エンジニアは重要な判断に集中 原因が特定されると、Codexは修正用のコードを作成し、エンジニアにレビューを依頼します。 エンジニアが修正内容を確認して反映した後は、再びAIが動作状況を調査し、性能が以前の水準に回復したかを検証します。 十分な改善が確認できなければ、追加調査に戻す仕組みも備えています。 また、AI自身が使用する調査ツールの不具合やアクセス権限の問題を検出し、修正タスクを作成する仕組みも導入しています。 一方で、AIが提案する修正は複雑になりすぎたり、新たな問題を引き起こしたりする可能性があります。そのため、現時点ではエンジニアによるコードの確認と反映判断が重要な役割を担っています。 OpenAIは今後、アラートが発生する前に性能低下の兆候を検出する仕組みや、リスクの低い修正をAIが自律的に適用する可能性も検討しています。 AIがシステム開発だけでなく、運用上の問題を発見し、改善を繰り返す。Performance Factoryは、AIエージェントを活用したシステム運用の新たな事例といえそうです。 レポート／DXマガジン編集部 シェアはこちらから URLをコピーしました！ 関連記事 ニュース 2024.11.20 JR東海が駅の空きスペースを活用する実証実験、マッチングサービス使って地域活性化を支援 ニュース records.excerpt: 日立がOpenAIのサイバー防御プログラムに参画 脆弱性発見から修復確認までAIでつなぐ 11/20(金) 11:55 配信 【画像解説と記事全文はこちら】日立のフロンティアAI提携、2026年の積み上がり（ビジネス+IT） 日立製作所は11月20日、OpenAIのサイバー防御パートナープログラム「Daybreak Defense Network」に参画したと発表した。OpenAIのフロンティアAIと日立の防御・運用の知見を組み合わせ、脆弱性の発見から検証、修復、修復結果の確認までをつなぐ防御ワークフローを開発・検証する。6月以降、先行検証を重ねてきた。 日立製作所は11月20日、OpenAIのサイバー防御パートナープログラム「Daybreak Defense Network」に参画したと発表した。OpenAIのフロンティアAIと、日立が蓄積してきた防御・運用の知見を組み合わせ、脆弱性の発見から検証、修復、修復結果の確認までをつなぐ防御ワークフローを開発・検証するという。 同プログラムは、パートナー企業が自社の専門知識とOpenAIのフロンティアAIモデルを組み合わせ、既存の製品やサービスにサイバー防御機能を組み込めるよう支援する枠組みだ。日立はOpenAIの技術チームと連携し、人による監督と適切な安全対策のもとで、脆弱性の発見、リスクの優先順位付け、修復を支援するワークフローを開発・検証する。 背景には、生成AIの進展によってサイバー攻撃が高度化・高速化し、システムの脆弱性やセキュリティリスクを迅速に見つけて対策につなげる重要性が高まっていることがある。 日立は2026年6月にOpenAIとの連携を本格化し、Cyber CoEを中核に、自社を最初の利用者とする「カスタマーゼロ」の立場で検証を進めてきた。社内システムや公共・金融分野のアプリケーションを対象に、ソースコードの診断とペネトレーションテスト（侵入テスト）を先行して実施。11月12日には、その知見を生かした「ソースコードセキュリティ診断」と「ペネトレーションテスト」を、オペレーショナルレジリエンスサービス「HMAX Cyber」のラインアップとして提供開始している。 今回の参画で得た知見は、HMAX Cyberをはじめとする顧客向けサービスに生かす方針だ。あわせて、顧客の課題を把握してAIの適用を進めるFDE（Forward Deployed Engineer）Teamの活動にも反映する。 日立の小岩博明氏（AI＆ソフトウェアサービスビジネスユニット Head of Cyber CoE）は、社会インフラの信頼性とレジリエンスを守ることを最優先の課題と位置づけ、FDE Teamを通じて先進AIの適用をリードしていく考えを示した。OpenAI Japan合同会社の水嶋ディノ氏（GTMパートナーシップ責任者）は、これまで高度なAIを活用しにくかった企業にもOpenAIの技術を届け、日本企業の脆弱性対応を支援していく考えを示した。 【関連リンク】 【情報漏えい・脆弱性対策】今知っておくべき主要5社「AI防御特化スキル」徹底解説 Okta・CrowdStrikeら4社を比較、「AIエージェントを守る製品」何を選ぶべき？

records.title: OpenAI、営業の作業をサポートするプラグイン「ChatGPT for Sales」をリリース
records.excerpt: OpenAI、営業の作業をサポートするプラグイン「ChatGPT for Sales」をリリース - AI Watch 検索 閉じる ニュース OpenAI、営業の作業をサポートするプラグイン「ChatGPT for Sales」をリリース 編集部：船津稔 2026年11月20日 14:16 OpenAIは新しい営業用のプラグイン「ChatGPT for Sales」をリリースした。 ChatGPT for Salesでは、アプローチする企業の選定から商談の準備、フォローアップの下書きまで、日々の営業活動ですぐに使えるワークフローを提供。パートナープラグインも利用でき、これまで使ってきたツールに埋もれている顧客情報をChatGPTが活用し、商談の進展に結びつけることができる。情報を一元化することで、営業チームは、全員が顧客について共通の理解を持つことで、営業に結びつけることができる。 アプローチすべき企業の情報に始まり、どの商談に注意が必要でその理由についてなど営業が知りたい情報は、顧客との会話、見込み客開拓ツールの報告書やCRMなどに隠れていることが多く、こうした情報を集約することで、チームは意思決定や顧客との約束を遂行することにより多くの時間を使えるようになる。 さらに、ChatGPTの常時稼働エージェントであるdotに任せれば、会話をしていない間も業務を進めることができる。dotは、同じプラグインと顧客情報を活用し、会議用の要約資料の作成や商談の最新状況を追跡できる。また、関連する情報の変化や次のステップへの提案を、ユーザーに届けてくれる。 このほかにも、CRMの履歴や顧客との会話をもとに、商談が停滞している原因を把握できるようChatGPTに依頼することもできる。 利用にあたっては、Salesプラグインをインストールし、新しいウィンドウで開くことで、ChatGPT for Salesの詳細やパートナープラグインについて確認することができる。 パートナープラグインも利用できる URL 🔗ニュースリリース https://openai.com/ja-JP/index/introducing-chatgpt-for-sales/ 🔗OpenAI https://openai.com/ja-JP/

records.title: NeuroFusion、Google・OpenAIを抑えAI未来予測ベンチマークで首位
records.excerpt: 韓国の金融AI企業NeuroFusionが、未来事象の確率予測ベンチマーク「ForecastBench」の総合リーダーボードでブライア指数69.4点を記録し、評価対象550モデルの中で首位に立った。Google DeepMind（68.4点）、OpenAIのGPT-6 Astra（66.7点）、AnthropicのClaude Opus 5.5（66.6点）などを上回り、人間の専門家集団「スーパーフォーキャスター」（68.1点）をも超えた。同社は独自の時系列グラフ「Damian」や530以上のデータパイプラインなど金融データ基盤を成果の背景に挙げている。NeuroFusionは今回の評価を最後にベンチマークへの参加を終え、Valley AIの金融特化エージェント拡張に乗り出す計画だ。 韓国の金融AI企業NeuroFusionが、グローバルな人工知能（AI）の未来予測能力を競うベンチマークで、Google DeepMindやOpenAI、Anthropicなどビッグテックのモデルをすべて抑えて首位に立った。 NeuroFusionは20日、自社の金融AI研究チームが未来事象の確率予測ベンチマーク「ForecastBench」の総合リーダーボードで1位を記録したと発表した。今月17日時点の総合ブライア指数は69.4点で、評価対象となった550モデルの中で最も高いスコアだ。昨年9月にデータセット部門の先行リーダーボードで1位となったのに続き、公式順位でも首位を確定した。 ForecastBenchはフィリップ・テトロック・ペンシルベニア大学ウォートンスクール教授らが参加するForecasting Research Institute（FRI）が運営し、国際学会ICLR 2025に採択された評価体系だ。提出時点で結果が確定していない質問の確率予測を実際の結果と照合する方式のため、正解の漏洩や事前学習による性能の水増しを根本的に防ぐ。評価は企業株価や米国債金利、政策金利など経済・金融指標を扱うデータセット部門と、主要国の選挙結果や国際紛争交渉の妥結可否など定性的な判断を要する事象を扱うマーケット部門に分かれる。総合順位は両部門のスコアを同じ比重で合算し、予測提出から50日が経過して結果が確定した後にのみ公式記録として認定される。 NeuroFusionはデータセット部門で65.5点、マーケット部門で73.9点を獲得した。競合モデルとの差も明確だ。モデルを直接提出したGoogle DeepMindは68.4点で1.0点差をつけられ、運営陣がウェブ検索を適用して評価したxAIの「Grok 4.20」（66.9点）、OpenAIの「GPT-6 Astra」（66.7点）、Anthropicの「Claude Opus 5.5」（66.6点）、Metaの「Muse Spark 1.3」（66.0点）とは2.5～3.4点の差を広げた。難易度補正ブライアスコアに換算すると、NeuroFusionの「Seraphin AI」はAnthropicとOpenAIの比較モデルより予測誤差を15～16％低減した水準となる。 区分 総合ブライア指数 NeuroFusion 69.4点 Google DeepMind 68.4点 xAI Grok 4.20 66.9点 OpenAI GPT-6 Astra 66.7点 Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 66.6点 Meta Muse Spark 1.3 66.0点 スーパーフォーキャスター（人間専門家集団） 68.1点 注：今月17日時点のForecastBench総合リーダーボード。スコアが高いほど予測精度が優れている。 人間の専門予測家集団「スーパーフォーキャスター」の最新評価スコア（68.1点・9位）も上回った。NeuroFusionはデータセット（スーパーフォーキャスター63.4点）とマーケット（73.5点）の両部門でこの基準点を上回った。所属を公開した参加チームのうち、スーパーフォーキャスターより高いスコアを得たのはNeuroFusionとGoogle DeepMindの2社のみだ。 今回の成果の背景として、同社は独自設計した4段動的時系列グラフ「Damian」と4年間で構築した530以上のデータパイプライン、167の金融特化MCPなど精製された金融データ基盤を挙げた。予測システムはユーザー基盤の仮説集約、再帰的自己改善、エージェンティック・データエンジニアリング、LLM基盤のバックテスティング、ワールドモデルなどで構成される。 NeuroFusionは今回の評価を最後にベンチマークへの参加を終え、研究成果を実際のサービスに適用する作業と活用範囲の拡大に注力する計画だ。AI投資分析プラットフォーム「Valley AI」を金融特化の能動型エージェントへ拡張することも推進する。 チェ・ハンチョルNeuroFusion代表は「多くのAIエージェントサービスは与えられた作業をうまく遂行する領域に集中しているが、今後は少しずつ未来予測領域へと焦点が移っていくだろう」と述べ、「AIがデータの少ない問題でも人間より優れた判断をし始めるなら、それは金融市場を超え、はるかに巨大な意思決定領域の革新が間近に迫っていることを意味する」と語った。続けて「現在の研究成果を大規模に拡張し、人間の思考を計量化して超知能を達成するというNeuroFusionのビジョンに向けてさらに邁進する」と表明した。 今回の結果は、金融界のAI活用議論が単純な業務自動化から予測・判断領域へ移行しつつある信号として読まれる。これまでAIエージェント競争は与えられた課題をいかに正確に遂行するかを中心に展開されてきたが、確率予測のように正解が事後にしか確定しない領域で人間の専門家を上回る事例が現れたことで、金融・投資分析サービスの評価基準自体が変わる可能性が提起される。ただしベンチマークのスコアは特定期間に提出された質問群を対象とした結果であるため、実際の市場環境における汎化性能には追加検証が必要との指摘もある。

records.excerpt: OpenAIら上場で「億万長者1.2万人」爆誕、彼らが真っ先に買う「意外な資産」とは？ 11/20(金) 6:40 配信 テック長者たちが注目する投資先は「○○」？ 大手テック・AI開発企業の上場により、各社従業員の中から大量の「ミリオネア」が誕生すると予測される。 そんな中、SpaceXのエンジニアリングおよび製造拠点が所在するカリフォルニア州南部のロサンゼルス郡ホーソーン市では、2026年9月の平均住宅価格が86万3,012ドル（約1億3,549万円）と、前年同月比1％超上昇していると報告された。この傾向は一時的なものではなく、SpaceXの株式売却制限が緩和されるにつれ、さらに値上がりすると見られている。 なぜなら、一夜にしてAI長者となった人たちの多くが、まず購入するのが「持ち家」であるからだ。 同じカリフォルニア州の北部「AIの都」サンフランシスコでも、同様の傾向が報告されている。その裏では、ミリオネアになったテック企業の従業員たちが家を買いあさっているのではないだろうか。 サンフランシスコの同年9月の平均住宅価格は144万1,021ドル（約2億2,624万円）と、前年同月比で15.5％も高騰している。売りに出された住宅は約2週間で成約となってしまう過熱ぶりだ。 AIミリオネアたちは、10月29日時点で7.24％まで上昇した30年固定住宅ローンの高金利を気にする必要がない。なぜなら、価格の大半をポンと現金で支払えるからだ。住宅市場に参加しようとする一般人は、最初から彼らに買い負けてしまうのである。 「アドバイザーはAI」…それでもAI長者が「人間」を頼るワケ このように住宅市場で「とても同じ土俵で勝負できない」と恐れられているAI長者たちだが、彼らのパワーは現金だけではない。AI企業に勤務する立場から、彼らはIPO前からすでに、深い金融リテラシーを身に付けているのだと、投資アドバイザーたちは口をそろえる。 米経済専門局CNBCのインタビューに応じた複数の投資アドバイザーたちによると、SpaceX社員の顧客たちは、コンサルティングのミーティングにやってくる前にAIで税制や投資プラン、退職後の運用収入に関する予測などについての調べものを済ませ、AIによる分析を基に、鋭い質問を投げかけてくるのだという。 また、資産別の市場パフォーマンス予測のシナリオもAIに考察させ、損失が出る可能性のあるプランのシミュレーションをリアルタイムのデータを基にはじき出している。これらの検討を十分に行ったうえで、金融アドバイザーたちに専門家としての意見を求める顧客さえいるという。 個々の社員が別々の投資企業に運用を任せるのではなく、100人程度が集まって資産をプールするAIミリオネアまで現れた。 合計10億～50億ドル規模の潜在的資産を持つSpaceXの現社員・元社員のグループが、米資産運用会社Choreoと低手数料の資産管理サービスについて交渉した。これにより、通常は年率0.5～1％の手数料を0.5％未満に抑えるのだという。億万長者になっても、利益を最大化しようとする姿勢は、特筆に値する。 AI長者たちは「徹底的な理論武装」「投資家としての団結」をしている。従来型の顧客に比べて、アドバイザー企業にとって手ごわい存在であることは確かだ。 こうした中、新しいミリオネア社員たちがAIで知識を得つつも、専門家に金融面の助言を乞い、運用を任せるのには、合理的な理由がある。AIが金融アドバイスの面で間違うことが多いことを、AI企業の「中の人」として熟知しているからである。 次ページは：「にわかリッチ」がハマる“投資の落とし穴”とは 前へ 1 2 3 次へ 2 / 3ページ 【関連リンク】 Claude・GPT公開に「待った」連発…米トランプ政権が目論む“中国封じ”のAI戦略 実験中のChatGPTが「勝手に」他社システムを攻撃…それでもOpenAIが“得をする”ワケ 時価総額「日本の予算の13倍」…スペースXが圧勝か？ 迫る大型IPO「3銘柄」の明暗 スペースX無双か、まさかの日本逆転か…「宇宙AIデータセンター」争奪戦の意外な行方 「ブラックサーズデー」再来？ 日韓台を襲った「AI・半導体株急落」の正体とは

records.title: 「遅くなった」の原因調査から修正案、回復確認までAIが担当 OpenAIがChatGPTの速度を守る社内の仕組みを公開
records.excerpt: OpenAIは11月19日、ChatGPTなど自社サービスの速度低下をAIが自動で調べ、修正案まで作る社内システム「Performance Factory」の仕組みを 公開 しました。3か月あまりで1700件以上の調査を扱い、600件以上で原因を突き止めたとしています。1日あたり17件の調査を自動で行っている計算です。 対象は、サービスの応答が以前より遅くなる「性能の後退」です。性能の警告が出ると、システムが課題票を1件作ります。続いてAI（同社のCodex）が、どの指標がいつから悪くなり、どのリクエストが影響を受けたかを調べます。警告が出た時点より何時間も前から悪化が始まっていることがあるため、データをさかのぼって始まりを探します。そのうえで、同じ時期のデプロイや機能フラグの変更を調べ、該当するコードを読み、ログやトレースで裏付けを取ります。 特徴は、診断を別のAIに調査させる点です。システム稼働当初は、AIが最初に見つけたもっともらしい説明で調査をやめ、診断が誤っていることがありました。そこで、別のCodexのセッションが診断を反証しようとする工程を加えました。「その変更が当たっていないリクエストは正常だったか」「変更を戻したら指標は回復したか」といった点を確かめます。 診断が通ると、AIが修正のコードを書いてプルリクエストを出します。取り込むかどうかを決めるのはエンジニアです。課題票には、後退の概要、影響、原因、修正案の要約が、指標のグラフやCPUのフレームグラフとともに自動でまとめます。デプロイ後は、AIが性能が元の水準に戻ったかを確かめ、戻っていれば完了にし、一部しか戻っていなければ残りを新しい課題として起こします。 システムは4つの機能で構成。作業の状態と遷移を設定ファイルとMarkdownの指示文で定義する課題管理、準備ができた課題にAIを割り当てる定期処理、Codexをクラウドで動かす社内API、レビューコメントやデプロイ完了といったイベントでAIを起動する仕組みです。AIは専用のサービスIDで動き、権限を絞り、どの操作がAIによるものかを追えるようにしています。 精度について同社は、原因の提案100件を人が確認したところ、70%が正確で、30%はさらに調査する必要があったか因果関係を示し切れていなかったとしています。原因の特定より修正のほうが難しく、AIの修正案が必要以上に複雑だったり、新しい問題を持ち込んだりする例があったとも述べました。キャッシュの追加のように設計上の判断が要る変更は、より上流のエンジニアの判断が要るとしています。 運用の教訓として同社は、AIの出力を人が読める量と形にまとめること、調査手順やモデルを変える前に過去の障害で再テストすること、AI自身の道具の故障を毎日別のAIに点検させることを挙げています。今後は、警告が出ていない小さな悪化をAIが見つける仕組みや、リスクの低い修正を人のレビューなしで出す方法を検討しているとしています。 自社でAIに運用を任せたい企業にとっては、「調べるAI」と「疑うAI」を分けること、人に残す判断を工程として決めておくことが参考になりそうです。Performance Factoryは社内システムで、外部への提供については不明です。

AIで脆弱性の発見から修復までを支援する新たな仕組みへ ニュース 2026.11.20 日立がOpenAIのサイバー防御網に参画！ AIで脆弱性の発見から修復までを支援する新たな仕組みへ IT・デジタル IT・技術基盤 URLをコピーしました！ サイバー攻撃が高度化する中、AIを活用してシステムの弱点を発見し、修復まで支援する取り組みが進んでいます。 株式会社日立製作所は2026年11月20日、OpenAIが推進するサイバー防御のパートナープログラム「Daybreak Defense Network」に参画すると発表しました。 日立が社会インフラや基幹システムの防御・運用で培ってきた知見と、OpenAIの高度なAI技術を組み合わせ、企業のサイバーセキュリティ対策を強化する狙いです。 今後は、システムの脆弱性を発見するだけでなく、リスクの検証や優先順位付け、修復、修復結果の確認までを一連の流れで支援する新たな仕組みの構築を目指します。 AIがシステムの弱点を発見！ OpenAIと連携してサイバー防御を強化 「Daybreak Defense Network」は、パートナー企業が自社の専門知識とOpenAIのフロンティアAIモデルを組み合わせ、サイバー防御機能の開発を進めるためのプログラムです。 セキュリティ担当者が普段使用している製品やサービスにAIを組み込み、日常業務の中で脅威の発見や対策を進められるようにすることを目指しています。 日立は、OpenAIの技術チームと連携し、脆弱性の発見から修復までを支援する防御ワークフローの開発・検証に取り組みます。 例えば、AIを活用してプログラムの弱点を調査し、発見されたリスクの重要度を整理することで、セキュリティ担当者が優先的に対応すべき問題を判断しやすくすることが期待されます。 さらに、修復後に問題が解消されたかを確認する工程までつなげ、継続的なセキュリティ対策を支援する方針です。 ただし、AIがすべての判断や修復を自動で行うわけではありません。日立は、適切な安全対策と人による監督のもとで技術開発を進めるとしています。 公共・金融分野で先行検証！ すでにAI活用のセキュリティ診断を提供開始 日立は2026年6月にOpenAIとの連携を本格化し、サイバーセキュリティ分野でAIモデルの活用を進めてきました。 社内のサイバーセキュリティ専門組織「Cyber CoE」を中心に、日立自身を最初の利用者とする「カスタマーゼロ」の取り組みを実施しています。 公共・金融分野のアプリケーションや社内システムなどを対象に、ソースコードのセキュリティ診断やペネトレーションテストを先行的に実施し、脆弱性の検出や対策立案におけるAIの有効性を検証してきました。 こうした取り組みを生かし、2026年11月12日には、フロンティアAIを活用した「ソースコードセキュリティ診断」と「ペネトレーションテスト」の提供を開始しています。 これらは、企業の事業継続を支援するセキュリティサービス「HMAX Cyber」のラインアップとして提供されています。 今回のDaybreak Defense Networkへの参画により、日立はOpenAIとの技術連携をさらに深め、得られた知見をHMAX Cyberなどの顧客向けサービスに生かしていく考えです。 AIを活用したサイバー防御が、専門家による調査を支援する段階から、脆弱性への対応プロセス全体を支える仕組みへと発展する可能性があります。 詳しくは、 日立のHMAX Cyber公式サイト をご覧ください。 レポート／DXマガジン編集部 records.title: OpenAI、「GPT-6.2 Astra」と「GPT-6.2 Sol」公開。ChatGPT Workなどで提供（あたらしい経済）
records.excerpt: OpenAI、「GPT-6.2 Astra」と「GPT-6.2 Sol」公開。ChatGPT Workなどで提供 11/18(水) 16:39 配信 Astraは複雑な専門業務、Solは日常業務向け ※写真はイメージです。（PIXTA） 米オープンAI（OpenAI）が、新たなAIモデル「GPT-6.2 Astra（アストラ）」と「GPT-6.2 Sol（ソル）」の提供開始を11月18日（日本時間）に発表した。両モデルは、チャットGPT（ChatGPT）の作業支援モード「ChatGPT Work」、開発支援ツール「コーデックス（Codex）」、同社のAPIで利用できる。 アストラは、複雑な専門業務向けの上位モデルだ。スライドや表計算ファイル、文書の作成では、利用者が指定したテンプレートや業界ごとの慣習をより忠実に反映できるという。既存コードの修正やテスト、ウェブサイトや3Dモデルの制作も強化した。 ソルは、文章作成やコーディング、複数の工程にわたる作業など、日常業務向けのモデルだ。オープンAIによると、従来の「GPT-6.1 Sol」より効率が上がり、同じ有料プランでより多くの作業をこなせるという。 実際の業務に基づく複数工程の作業を評価する同社のベンチマーク「GDPval v2」では、アストラが従来の「GPT-6 Astra」を6.2ポイント、ソルが前モデルを5.3ポイント上回った。アストラの出力トークン数は、同じ評価で前モデルから22％減少したという。 入力が27万2,000トークン以下の場合、アストラの標準API料金は、100万トークンあたり入力8ドル（約1,275円）、キャッシュ済み入力0.40ドル（約64円）、出力40ドル（約6,374円）だ。GPT-6 Astraと比べて入力・出力の単価は20％、キャッシュ済み入力の単価は60％下がった。 ソルの標準API料金は、同じ条件で入力2ドル（約319円）、キャッシュ済み入力0.10ドル（約16円）、出力10ドル（約1,593円）だ。いずれもGPT-6.1 Solと同額となる。 同社の公式ガイドによると、ChatGPT Workでの提供対象はPlus、Pro、Business、Enterprise、Eduの各プランだ。EnterpriseとEduでは、ワークスペースの管理者による有効化が必要となる。また、月額200ドル（約3万1,868円）のProプランでは、新たにソルで高速モード「ウルトラファスト（Ultrafast）」が利用できるようになった。 同社が公表した安全性評価では、アストラは、AI研究を加速する能力を測る「AI自己改善能力（AI Self-Improvement）」で「High」のしきい値に達した。オープンAIが外部に提供したモデルでは初めてだという。 大津賀新也（幻冬舎 あたらしい経済） 【関連リンク】 OpenAI、110億ドル調達、ソフトバンクとMGXが参加＝関係者 マイクロソフトのOpenAI関連売上高、四半期100億ドルに。Xbox事業を上回る OpenAI、「GPT-6.1 Terra」提供開始。画面操作を強化、API料金はSolの半額 OpenAI、24時間働くAIエージェント「Dots」提供開始、GPT-6 Astra搭載 OpenAI、次期AIモデル「GPT-6.1 Astra」の公開中止、安全性の基準満たさず＝報道
