records.title: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援
records.excerpt: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援 – 日刊自動車新聞 2026.11.20(金) 管理者 紙面で読む 会社案内 各種申し込み 購読のご案内 ログイン 購読の ご案内 管理者 紙面で 読む ログイン 検索 トップ 自動車流通 開発・生産 行政・輸送 Home 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー お知らせ アーカイブ検索サイトメンテナンスのお知らせ アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー , 自動車メーカー , 人事・組織改正 2026年5月29日 11:30 SNSで共有: 井上勝史氏 ホンダと日立が出資する自動車部品メーカーのアステモ（東京都千代田区）は5月29日、ホンダの井上勝史取締役が7月1日付で社長CEO（最高経営責任者）に就任するトップ人事を内定したと発表した。竹内弘平社長CEOは退任する。6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。1963年10月22日生まれ、62歳。福岡県出身。 〈2026/5/29更新〉 SNSで共有: 関連記事 ホンダ、現実路線で四輪事業の収益改善へ 開発費・期間・工数を半減 「開発スピードは世界トップレベルに」 2026年5月15日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー , 企画・解説・オピニオン ホンダ、電動化戦略を見直し EV目標は撤回 2029年度までに次世代HV15モデル投入 新型セダンとアキュラSUVも公開 2026年5月14日 14:10 ｜ 自動車メーカー ホンダ、アステモを子会社化 ソフトやAI開発加速 新規株式公開も視野 2025年12月18日 05:00 ｜ 自動車メーカー , 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー ホンダ系サプライヤー、EV戦略見直しに「補償求める」「量産前の決断歓迎」などの声 2026年3月13日 05:00 ｜ 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー 資本再編進む自動車サプライヤー 親子上場の解消 円安で外資も意欲 経営資源集中でEVやSDVに対応 2026年1月1日 05:00 ｜ 企画・解説・オピニオン , 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー 日本精工とNTN、2027年10月1日の経営統合を発表 持株会社名は「NTN日本精工」 2026年11月20日 16:50 ｜ 自動車部品・素材・サプライヤー アクセスランキング 直近 昨日 一週間 ランキングを読み込み中です。 ランキングを読み込み中です。 ランキングを読み込み中です。 ワンソクTubeのブログはこちら 【レクサス大丈夫か?!】2026年上半期の新車販売台数ランキングTOP50で異変! 意外な車が上位へ?! レクサスを叱咤激励するオーナーたちの意外な本音とは?! records.title: 一日警察署長の役割は？警視庁に聞いた 10月は管内で8人が“就任” 役割は2つに分かれる 過去にはウエンツ瑛士、広瀬アリス、本田紗来…
records.excerpt: 一日警察署長を務めた時の（左から）松平健、ウエンツ瑛士、本田紗来※ウエンツは事務所提供 著名人が警察官の帽子や制服をまとって市民の前に立つ「一日警察署長」。ニュースで目にする機会が多いが、どのような役割があるのか。警視庁に最近“署長”を務めた著名人を交えて話を聞いた。 【写真】美脚見えてる！一日警察署長を務めた広瀬アリス 一日警察署長と言うと、著名人が警察官の制服、制帽に「一日警察署長」と書かれたタスキをかけて敬礼をする。そんなお決まりの姿が目に浮かぶ。どのような役割があるのか。警視庁の担当者は「各種広報活動における広報効果を高めるため、著名人に一日警察署長を依頼するケースがあります」と説明した。 同庁によると、一日警察署長にも役割が二つに分かれているという。一つは、交通安全を目的として委嘱するもの。事故防止のため、反射材着用や自転車乗車時のヘルメット着用を促すことはこちらに該当しそうだ。もう一方は、地域安全。こちらで委嘱されると、主に特殊詐欺被害の防止など事件を未然に防ぐための啓発をする。 最近、管内で一日署長を務めた著名人を聞くと、9月12日に日野署で元プロ野球選手の井端弘和が交通安全を目的に委嘱された。同13日は同じく交通安全を目的に神田署でタレントのウエンツ瑛士が務めたという。10月には7日に渋谷署でタレントのマツコ・デラックス、17日に蒲田署でお笑いタレントの庄司智春がそれぞれ地域安全を目的に市民に詐欺被害の防止を呼びかけた。 このほか、警視庁の公式サイトのイベント欄を見ると、ヒャダインやプロレスラーの上谷沙弥も今月に一日警察署長を務めていた。オリコンニュースが10月30日に調べた限り、管内で8人が10月に“就任”していた。 公式サイトを見ると、11月にも14日に立川署でももいろクローバーZの高城れに、17日に葛飾署でお笑いコンビ・ななまがりがそれぞれ務める予定だ。 また、オリコンニュースでは過去に、舘ひろし、松平健、黒谷友香、中村静香、広瀬アリス、田村真子、本田紗来らが一日警察署長を務めたことを伝える記事があった。 近年、凶悪事件や悲惨な事故が後を絶たない中、発信力のある著名人の力はこれからも大きく事件や事故の防止に役立ってくれそうだ。 【写真】「タイホされてぇ〜」警察官の制服姿に反響が寄せられた中村静香 【写真】ピーポくんデレデレ…アイドルすぎる婦警姿の皆藤愛子 【写真あり】似合いすぎ！“警察署長”の制服姿を披露した田村真子 【全身カット】かっわい！警察官の衣装で登場した大原優乃 【写真】実際にいそう…一日警察署長を務める松平健

records.excerpt: エステバン・オコンが、2027年にアストンマーティンF1のサードドライバーに就任することで合意に達したと報じられた。2026年F1メキシコシティGPの週末にハースF1を離脱したオコンだが、早ければ今季最終戦後のアブダビテストで再びF1マシン… エステバン・オコン アストンマーティン・ホンダF1のサードドライバー就任で合意との報道 2026年11月19日 18:04 公開 エステバン・オコンが、2027年にアストンマーティンF1のサードドライバーに就任することで合意に達したと報じられた。2026年F1メキシコシティGPの週末にハースF1を離脱したオコンだが、早ければ今季最終戦後のアブダビテストで再びF1マシンをドライブする可能性がある。 RacingNews365が独自情報として伝えたもので、オコンはフェルナンド・アロンソとランス・ストロールを支えるサードドライバーとしてアストンマーティンF1に加わる見通しだという。すでにシートフィッティングも完了しており、正式発表に向けた準備が進んでいるとされる。 オコンはシートフィッティング完了 アブダビテスト参加の可能性 報道によると、オコンはアストンマーティンF1との合意に達しており、2026年シーズン終了前にも同チームのF1マシンをドライブする機会を得る可能性がある。 最初の走行機会として想定されているのは、最終戦アブダビGP後に実施されるポストシーズンテストだ。オコンの加入も、それまでに正式発表される見込みだという。 RacingNews365は、オコンが最近シートフィッティングを済ませており、シーズン終了後のテストに参加するための準備が整っていると伝えている。 アストンマーティンF1にとっても、オコンを早期に起用することには合理的な理由がある。 2度のF1ワールドチャンピオンであるアロンソは、シーズン終了後にダカール・ラリーに向けた準備に集中する予定だ。ストロールはテストに参加できるものの、新たに加入するドライバーに走行機会を与えることで、2027年に向けた貴重なフィードバックを得られる。 オコンはメキシコシティGPの金曜日までハースF1でレースに参戦しており、2026年型マシンでの豊富な実戦経験を持っている。 今季のハースF1はアストンマーティンF1よりも競争力の高いマシンを投入しており、その経験を持つオコンがAMR26をドライブすることは、チームの開発方向を見極めるうえでも重要な意味を持つ。 ただし、現時点でオコンの加入は正式に発表されていない。 RacingNews365がオコン陣営に接触したところ、報道へのコメントは拒否されたものの、内容を否定することもなかったという。 また、ラスベガスGPの水曜日に取材を受けたアストンマーティンF1の広報担当者は、次のように回答した。 「アストンマーティンへの加入を希望するドライバーから、我々は定期的にアプローチを受けている。しかし、我々の方針に従い、噂や憶測についてはコメントしない」 ハースF1を電撃離脱 メキシコGPで契約終了 オコンは2026年F1メキシコシティGPの週末、突然ハースF1を離脱した。 ハースF1はそれ以前から、2026年シーズン限りでオコンとの契約を終了することを発表していた。しかし、実際の別れは当初の予定よりも早く訪れた。 両者の関係はすでに緊張が高まっていたとされ、メキシコシティGPの金曜日に行われたフリー走行2回目の終了後、チームとオコンの間で意見の対立が発生したと報じられている。 その結果、オコンは即座にレースへの出場を取りやめることになり、数日後には契約そのものが解除されたという。 ハースF1はメキシコシティGPでオコンに代えて平川亮を起用。続くサンパウロGPでは、2027年からオコンの後任となることが決まっていたラファエル・カマラをデビューさせた。 突然F1のレギュラーシートを失ったオコンだが、その後もF1でのキャリアは終わっていないと繰り返し強調し、できる限り早い復帰を目標に掲げてきた。 一時は2027年からキャデラックF1に加入する可能性も取り沙汰されたが、同チームはラスベガスGPの水曜日、バルテリ・ボッタスの2027年残留を正式発表。セルジオ・ペレスとのラインアップ継続が決まり、オコンがレギュラーシートを獲得する可能性はなくなった。 そうした状況のなかで浮上したのが、アストンマーティンF1のサードドライバーという新たな選択肢だった。 アストンマーティンF1とは以前から交渉 アロンソの去就が鍵に オコンとアストンマーティンF1の接触は、今回初めて始まったものではない。 RacingNews365は2026年F1オーストリアGPの時点で、オコンがローレンス・ストロール率いるチームと交渉していると報じていた。 当時のオコンは、アロンソが現役引退を選択する可能性を見据え、アストンマーティンF1のレギュラーシート獲得を目指していたという。 しかし、アロンソが2027年もF1で戦い続けることを決めたため、オコンが獲得できるポジションはサードドライバーに限られることになった。 それでも、この役割はオコンにとって将来への希望をつなぐ重要な足掛かりとなる。 アロンソは現在のF1グリッドで最年長のドライバーであり、2027年末に現役を退く可能性もある。仮にアロンソが引退を決断すれば、チームの内部にいるオコンが後任候補として浮上する余地が生まれる。 さらに、オコンはストロール家と非常に良好な関係を築いているという。 ランス・ストロールは、サーキット内外を通じてオコンの最も親しい友人の一人であり、両者の個人的なつながりも今回の加入に向けた背景の一つとなっている。 アストンマーティンF1は2026年からホンダのパワーユニットを搭載し、新たなワークス体制で戦っている。2027年に向けてもマシンとパワーユニット双方の競争力向上が重要な課題となるなか、他チームの2026年型マシンを熟知するオコンの経験は貴重な戦力となり得る。 オコンにとっては、ハースF1との突然の決別からわずか数週間で、新たなF1チームとの関係を築く機会が訪れたことになる。 正式発表はまだ行われていないものの、報道どおりにアストンマーティンF1への加入が実現すれば、2027年はサードドライバーとしてチームに貢献しながら、2028年以降のレギュラー復帰を目指すことになる。 この記事の画像を見る（全2枚） SHARE ポスト シェア LINE B! ブックマーク Pocket

records.excerpt: 103万辆本田车被查自动启停：701份投诉还不是召回结论 103万辆本田车被查自动启停：701份投诉还不是召回结论 来源：汽车商业评论 (summer) 2026-11-17 17:23 发动机在红灯前自动熄火，驾驶者松开刹车时却没有重新启动。 美国国家公路交通安全管理局的EA26007文件 显示，监管机构已将本田自动启停问题提升到工程分析阶段，估算涉及1033632辆车。 范围是2024至2026款Honda Odyssey、Passport、Ridgeline、Pilot以及Acura MDX。NHTSA收到701份投诉，核心场景是车辆完全停住、自动启停介入后，发动机未能按预期恢复运转。这会把车辆留在路口，但文件尚未宣布这些车全部存在缺陷。 Odyssey是调查覆盖车系之一；具体车辆是否出现问题不能凭年款判定。摄影/来源：Deathpallie325；许可： CC BY 4.0 ； 授权页 。 工程分析不等于召回 Reuters的独立报道 确认，监管机构正评估问题频率、安全后果和原有技术服务措施是否足够。工程分析可能导向召回、更多检测或结案；它本身不是车主通知书。 Pilot同样在EA26007范围内，但照片车辆并非被确认的故障样本。摄影/来源：HJUdall；许可： CC0 ； 授权页 。 对车主而言，现阶段不宜把“103万辆”理解为需立即返店维修的数量。若车辆在路口自动熄火后不能重启，应优先离开交通流并记录故障条件，再向经销商与NHTSA报告。下一个关键节点是监管机构是否确认共同缺陷、扩大数据要求或要求召回。 资料来源：NHTSA EA26007；Reuters；AutoMotor News。 上一页 下一页 编辑推荐 奥沙瓦五年造出60万辆Silverado：一座重启工厂的里程碑，也暴露皮卡周期依赖 summer 2026-11-19 17:26 20万内唯一896线激光雷达，2027款岚图知音限时价19.79万元 吴静 2026-11-14 16:14 汽车创新走向邪路？ 吴静 2026-11-09 10:31 福特在密歇根造出首批LFP电芯：Fathom原型车先用，真正考验是2027年电池包量产 summer 2026-11-19 17:13 洛杉矶港多了一个9MW重卡充电工地：50个车位先解决谁的问题 summer 2026-11-17 17:37

records.title: 本田召回63万辆车，机械转向也会故障，EPS安全隐患
records.excerpt: 本田召回63万辆车，机械转向也会故障，EPS安全隐患_车家号_发现车生活_汽车之家 选择城市 更多 移动App 触屏版 小程序 i车商 本地服务 登录 发布作品 下载App 扫码下载汽车之家App 小程序 扫码打开汽车之家小程序 点赞 评论 收藏 分享 当前位置： 本田召回63万辆车，机械转向也会故障，EPS安全隐患 选车侦探 车家号 · 0 浏览 · 2026-11-11 19:04 · 陕西 提到转向系统故障，很多人会想到线控转向。毕竟线控转向取消了方向盘与车轮之间的传统机械连接，一旦电子系统出现问题，转弯就成了问题。但本田近期的一次大规模召回，说明传统机械转向系统同样存在电子故障风险，全球召回数量高达63万辆，接近2025年本田在国内的销量（64.5万辆）。 召回原因是什么？ 此次召回涉及三款车型：2021-2025款讴歌TLX、2022-2024款讴歌MDX、2023-2025款 本田Pilot ( 参数 | 询价 )，对于国内车主来说，好消息是这几款车并没有官方进口，但也要注意是否有平行进口。根据本田提交的召回资料，问题来自供应商开发的EPS控制软件。驾驶员注意力监测系统在特定运行条件下可能出现浮点数除以零的情况，触发内部错误。 简单来说，EPS控制器需要根据车速、方向盘转角、驾驶员输入扭矩等信息，实时计算电机应该提供多少助力。但软件在处理某项数据时出现异常，错误触发了系统的故障保护策略，直接让转向助力进入关机模式。 这次故障的原因是软件错误导致控制器主动关闭助力，所以解决方案是升级EPS控制单元软件，不需要更换转向机和电机。 不是线控转向，为何也会失去助力？ 传统EPS是在机械转向系统上增加电动助力，方向盘依然通过转向柱、传动轴和齿轮齿条机构与车轮连接。如果电机停止工作了，机械结构依旧可以控制车轮。 目前常见的EPS主要有三种，常见的是C-EPS转向柱助力，电机安装在转向柱附近，通过齿轮提供助力，结构紧凑、成本较低，常见于小型车；另一种是P-EPS小齿轮助力，电机作用于转向器输入小齿轮，通过齿轮机构提供助力；豪华车型多数用R-EPS齿条助力，电机直接作用于齿条，通过齿轮或皮带机构提供助力，能够提供更大的转向辅助扭矩，适合车身较重、轮胎较宽的车型。 此次召回的讴歌TLX、MDX和本田Pilot都属于本田的豪华车型，采用R-EPS，从结构上看，R-EPS的电机更靠近齿轮齿条机构，能够提供较大的助力扭矩，但安全性与C-EPS接近。 对用户有什么影响？ 不像线控转向，传统转向如果失去EPS助力，方向盘也不会失控，由于方向盘与车轮之间存在机械连接，依旧可以打方向，不过会变得笨重，如果你开过卡丁车，就会发现，没有转向助力，开一会胳膊发酸，需要和轮胎“较劲”。 笨重的转向在低速时尤其明显，例如停车入库、狭窄道路掉头，轮胎需要克服较大的地面摩擦阻力，此时电动助力系统承担了大部分的力量，如果助力突然消失，方向盘瞬间变得沉重。高速行驶时，转向阻力通常较小，失去助力后的方向盘不像低速时那么沉重。但遇到紧急避让时，转向力度突然变化，可能造成事故。 助力突然没了，需要重新适应不同的方向盘阻力，增加应急操作难度。如果行驶中出现EPS警告灯亮起、方向盘突然变重等情况，应在确保安全的前提下停车检查。 选车侦探观点： 从本田的召回来看，转向系统的可靠性不仅取决于齿轮、齿条和电机，还要考虑传感器、控制器和软件之间的协同。汽车越来越智能，但对于转向、刹车这样的关键安全系统，软件的容错能力和故障保护策略，也不能忽视。 records.title: Vegas Recap | Russell tops day one as major change to F1 stewards announced
records.excerpt: George Russell topped wet FP2 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix as five drivers received grid penalties and the FIA confirmed full-time F1 stewards from 2027. The first day of racing is now in the books at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. GPblog recaps everything that happened for you overnight in Sin City below. The first two sessions of Vegas Recap | Russell tops day one as major change to F1 stewards announced Photo: Race Pictures F1 News 07:39, 20 Nov 1 Comments Kada Sarkozi Kada Sárközi joined GPblog as an editor ahead of the 2023 Formula 1 season. He graduated with a BA in Sports Journalism in the UK and has covered Grands Prix and other F1 events live. The first day of racing is now in the books at the Las Vegas Grand Prix . GPblog recaps everything that happened for you overnight in Sin City below. No lap times in FP1, Russell sets the best lap time in FP2 The first two sessions of the weekend took place during the evening at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. During the first session, no competitive lap times were set due to the extreme weather conditions. Drivers then completed laps on the intermediate tyres during the second free practice session. George Russell improved as the clock ticked down to zero, snatching first place from Charles Leclerc, who had led throughout the session. The Briton's fastest lap was a 1:47.272. Alpine's Pierre Gasly finished just 0.071 seconds behind the Mercedes driver, while Leclerc completed the top three. Isack Hadjar followed in fourth place, finishing ahead of Oscar Piastri, Lewis Hamilton and Lando Norris. This year's world champion, Kimi Antonelli, finished P8, while Max Verstappen set the 13th-fastest time in the second 60-minute session of the opening day. ADVERTISEMENT However, because of the conditions, these lap times are hardly representative of the true power rankings. Read also Russell strikes late to deny dominant Leclerc top spot in Las Vegas FP2 Full Results | Russell snatches top spot from Ferrari on day 1 in Las Vegas FIA stewards confirm grid penalties for the Las Vegas Grand Prix Five drivers will definitely start the upcoming race with a grid penalty. McLaren previously announced that Piastri will receive a 10-place penalty. Antonelli, meanwhile, will drop five places for using a new internal combustion engine in his Mercedes. Carlos Sainz and Lance Stroll will have a 10-place grid penalty each for also changing power unit components in their cars. Moreover, Haas' Oliver Bearman will also be relegated to the back of the grid. ADVERTISEMENT Photo: Race Pictures Full-time stewards are coming to Formula 1 The motorsport federation has announced that, from next season, Formula 1 will have full-time stewards. The FIA will initially recruit a small number of stewards for the 2027 season and aims to establish a pool of 12–15 stewards over the coming years. Under this structure, the department will also be able to support other FIA series. The President of the FIA, Mohammed Ben Sulayem said : "This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport. The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport. "Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships." F1 results: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 – FP2 (Las Vegas Strip Circuit) Thomas Maher 20 Nov 2026 5:14 AM Check out the complete F1 results from the second practice session (FP2) at the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the Strip Circuit... Here are the complete F1 results from the second practice session (FP2) at the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the Strip Circuit, the 21st round of the F1 2026 season. After the washed-out first practice, action finally began in Las Vegas as George Russell took the fastest time for Mercedes What are the F1 results from FP2 at the Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026? The Mercedes driver left it until the final minute of the session to set the fastest time, which took place in wet conditions that meant the drivers all took part on the wet tyres, before switching to the intermediates about 20 minutes in. The battle for the top spot looked set to be solely between Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc and Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar, with the Monegasque fastest after trading fastest times with the French driver. Hadjar’s best lap saw him go purple in the first two sectors, before his third sector was ruined by being blocked by Haas’ Oliver Bearman. Hadjar wasn’t impressed by the block, which saw him lose over two seconds in the third sector, and meant he had to settle for finishing behind Leclerc. A brief red flag was thrown with 10 minutes to go, due to plastic bags floating across the racing line, resulting in the loss of about four minutes of track time. With the track conditions improving in the final minutes when the session resumed, a last flurry saw both of them overhauled by Russell on a 1:47.272. Preview: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 Underlining the improvement was Alpine’s Pierre Gasly, who slotted into second, less than a tenth behind Russell, three-tenths clear of Leclerc. In fifth was McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, while Lewis Hamilton finished sixth for Ferrari. Lando Norris was seventh for McLaren, ahead of Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli. Alpine’s Franco Colapinto was ninth, and Fernando Alonso showed Aston Martin’s promise by finishing 10th, just ahead of Lance Stroll. Max Verstappen finished 13th for Red Bull, having opted to sit out most of the session due to the wet conditions. Emerging with 13 minutes to go, he lost further time to the red flag, only completing six laps in total throughout. records.title: F1 finally makes major change to stewards after years of debate
records.excerpt: Formula 1 will introduce full-time stewards from 2027, with the FIA aiming to improve consistency and professionalise officiating... FIA confirms permanent F1 race stewards in major 2027 change Michelle Foster & Thomas Maher 20 Nov 2026 6:19 AM Kimi Antonelli (Mercedes W17) leads at the start of the 2026 Brazilian Grand Prix After years of debate, the FIA will introduce permanent Formula 1 race stewards from the F1 2027 season. The FIA announced a phased introduction, aimed at bringing “greater levels of consistency” and dedication to race officiating at the “highest levels.” FIA to recruit 12-15 full-time stewards as F1 targets greater consistency The debate over permanent stewards reached fever pitch in late 2024 as Max Verstappen and Lando Norris went wheel-to-wheel for the world title. Several incidents between the two protagonists were penalised, including two 10-second time penalties in one lap that dealt a blow to Verstappen’s title quest at the Mexico City Grand Prix. It reignited the debate over whether permanent stewards would lead to more consistent decision-making – consistency being the application of the same principles to the specific details of individual incidents every time, as opposed to the stewards reaching the same decision on every occasion. Following on from the commencement of full-time operations of the new Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill, the FIA has sought to further bolster its stewarding abilities, and, as of next season, the Formula 1 championship will have permanent stewards augmenting the roster of volunteer stewards that oversee a race weekend. The FIA announced: “FIA to begin recruiting full-time stewards, with a phased introduction during the 2027 Formula 1 season. “Programme aims to establish a department of 12-15 full-time stewards over the coming years, further professionalising officiating and expanding coverage across FIA Single-Seater Championships. “The initiative builds on the recent opening of the FIA Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill, UK, and forms part of the Federation’s wider investment in the people, expertise and infrastructure through its FIA Officials department. “The introduction of dedicated full-time stewards to the FIA’s flagship championship will provide continuity and expertise within the stewarding structure, further advancing the FIA’s commitment to fairness through the ongoing review and continuous improvement of sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines. “It will also allow for deeper implementation of best practice and greater consistency in decision-making. “Beyond race weekends, it will provide increased capacity to identify emerging trends and areas requiring regulatory clarification, helping to inform the evolution of sporting regulations.” The goal is to have between 12 and 15 full-time stewards on board, building to that number over the coming years. Speaking to PlanetF1.com, one of the four chairmen of the F1 stewards, Garry Connelly, explained how permanent stewards will slot into the structure. “They will be people who will possibly come from the existing pool of FIA stewards, not necessarily Formula 1 stewards,” he said. “They could be stewards from elsewhere, people who want to work full time for the FIA, and they will not only do stewarding; they’ll do some work in the Remote Operations Centre, the ROC, at Biggin Hill. “They’ll ultimately also be doing a lot of work in coordination of stewards, like rosters, administration, things like that, and they’ll also be doing training other stewards, particularly training in different categories, and training in different regions of the world. “They’ll be part of the FIA’s Officials Department, but the stewards will always remain independent. “In fact, it’s quite possible that, in the first year, we might only have one or two of those people involved in a lot of F1 events. So it could be a phasing-in period depending on who’s recruited because we don’t know who really wants the job, but they will be full-time professional stewards to augment the current pool of part-time professional stewards. “What I mean by part-time professional stewards, the pool of F1 stewards, for example, was around 30 people 15 to 20 years ago, sometimes even more in a year. So it was like a revolving door. “People would come in and do one event a year, which led to enormous inconsistencies. “For 2027, we’ve got a core pool of 11, so four permanent chairs, four number twos, and three driver stewards. So that’s the smallest pool we’ve basically ever had. “All of those are highly professional. We do an enormous amount of training through the year. “We also commit to a three-day meeting; it’s in Milan next year in January, and, for F1, we now do a debrief meeting after every F1 race, where the entire pool of F1 stewards is involved. There is also an online training programme that runs the entire season. “These new full-time permanent stewards, they’ll be involved not only in F1 but F2 and F3 as well. They may ultimately go to things like Formula E, WRC, and maybe WEC, as well. “You’ll always have a rotating pool, and I think that’s a good thing because, if you go back to the days when there was one permanent chairman, for example, that caused a lot of unrest and ill feeling, with some teams believing that one chairman was either very much against them or very much in favour of another team. “So the only difference in the way they’ll be doing things is they’ll be full-time versus the current crop of part-time. There’ll be a mix at events of full-time and part-time, at least for the next few years. “Now, whether ultimately it ever goes to 100 per cent full-time stewards in F1, we’ll have to wait and see whether enough people are wanting to do the role, who are capable of doing the role and who want to be full-time. “Everyone’s pretty happy with the initiative.” Connelly pointed out that, in recent years, greater consistency in stewarding has already been accomplished, a feat “not easy to do” amongst volunteer staff. “I think what we need to do is look at the areas of improvement that we’ve done in recent years to ensure greater consistency in what we do,” he said. “I think that will just continue and probably work better with some full-time stewards sitting within the FIA able to better coordinate that because previously, until the advent of the Officials’ Department, the stewards were basically a group on their own and, of course, to a certain extent, they should be because we are independent. “Prior to the establishment of the Officials’ Department, there was really no one who was responsible for coordination and training. “A lot of the training and coordination, we had to basically arrange amongst ourselves. “But I think this will help with greater consistency because we’ll have more resources, more ability to add to those things and improve consistency. “I would hope that AI also ultimately will help us improve consistency. I don’t know if it’s quite at that level yet. We have done a little bit of playing with it, but it’s not really at the stage yet where we could rely on it within the Stewards’ Room. However, for sure, it’s coming!” More on the FIA and F1’s governance FIA explained: What does it stand for and how does it govern F1? Lance Stroll 10-place grid penalty confirmed by FIA at Las Vegas GP Stroll was classified 11th in FP2 on Thursday night in Las Vegas, one spot behind two-time world champion teammate Fernando Alonso, as George Russell’s Mercedes topped the times. Following the end of second practice, the FIA confirmed that Stroll – who is yet to score a point in 2026 – will drop 10 places on the grid due to an engine change. The Canadian driver has moved on to a ninth energy store of F1 2026 in Las Vegas, six more than the three permitted over the course of a season. Stroll has also taken an eighth control electronics unit, having already exceeded the limit of three per season. The two changes add up to a total of 10 grid positions. Lance Stroll vs Fernando Alonso: Aston Martin head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates Aston Martin has been hindered by reliability problems over the course of the F1 2026 season, the first of the team’s partnership with Honda. The Silverstone-based outfit has been limited to just seven points, all scored by Alonso, over the course of the campaign. Stroll has retired at 13 of the 20 races held so far this season, with the Canadian forced to wait until the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia – which took place on October 4 – to complete a full race distance for the first time in 2026. The 28-year-old had been lapped during all of his previous race finishes. That’s probably been our biggest issue this year, or probably has been our biggest issue this year, is just the lack of power in the long straights. “And here, there’s a lot of straights, so it’ll probably be a tough weekend, but we’ll do the best we can. “We’re really down on power. We’re probably going to be, like, two seconds just down on the straights. records.excerpt: FIA confirms huge 35-place penalty at Las Vegas Grand Prix FIA confirms 35-place Las Vegas Grand Prix penalty for Oliver Bearman Oliver Harden 20 Nov 2026 7:19 AM The FIA is Formula 1's governing body The FIA has confirmed that Haas driver Oliver Bearman will start from the back of the grid at the Las Vegas Grand Prix following an engine change. Bearman was classified 15th in Friday’s second practice session in Las Vegas as Mercedes driver George Russell set the pace. FIA confirms 35-place grid penalty for Oliver Bearman at Las Vegas GP Following Thursday night’s FP2 session in Las Vegas, the FIA has confirmed that Bearman has exceeded his engine component pool for the F1 2026 season, triggering a sizeable grid drop. The British driver will take a fifth internal combustion engine, fifth turbocharger, fifth exhaust set and fifth MGU-K of 2026 this weekend. The combined changes add up to a 35-place grid penalty. A change to the rules over recent years means that drivers who accumulate grid drops worth more than 15 positions must automatically start from the back of the grid. Oliver Bearman vs Esteban Ocon: Haas head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates Bearman’s grid penalty comes after the 21-year-old expressed his frustration on Thursday that his Haas future is yet to be resolved. Despite an impressive 2026 campaign, Bearman is yet to be officially confirmed by Haas for the F1 2027 season, with the youngster admitting to being “quite disappointed” by the situation. Asked to give an update on his future, he replied: “Nothing new. “If I’m honest, I’m quite disappointed that I’m sitting here at Round 20 [sic], whatever, without a contract signed for next year. “It’s been a strange, strange situation, but we’re getting there and all I can say is that it’s a bit disappointing, and obviously it’s not ideal for a driver’s confidence and things like that. “Of course, I know that I’ve done a good job this year, but the fact that I don’t know what I’m doing next year, it’s not ideal; I’ll tell you that much.” More on Oliver Bearman and Haas from PlanetF1.com Oliver Bearman news Haas news Bearman, a graduate of Ferrari’s junior academy, appeared to hint that the delay regarding his future could be related to his pathway towards a Ferrari seat. Charles Leclerc signed a new contract with Ferrari earlier this year, keeping him with the team until at least 2030, while Lewis Hamilton could remain with the Scuderia beyond 2027. Bearman said: “Of course, I’m under contract with Ferrari and Ferrari has given me this incredible opportunity to step into F1 with them for the first time, and, of course, I’m still a Ferrari junior driver. “My ultimate dream is to race for Ferrari because, first of all, they’re the most iconic team, and they’re the first team that believed in me as a kid, so it’s still my ultimate dream. “But there’s no doubt that, looking into the future, there may be some challenges there. “There’s no denying that. records.excerpt: FIA to Hire Full-Time F1 Stewards From 2027 Skip to content F1 Gets Its First Full-Time Stewards in 2027 as the FIA Plans a Team of Up to 15 Max Verstappen leads the field at the start of the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Mark Thompson/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool By: Darshan Chokhani Published: November 20, 2026 - 5:09 am Darshan Chokhani November 20, 2026 Add MotorBiscuit as a preferred source The FIA will start hiring full-time Formula 1 stewards in 2027, beginning with a small group and building to a department of 12 to 15, it announced on Nov. 19. The FIA said the department could later extend its support to its other single-seater championships. A Small Group First, With Part-Timers Staying On The 2027 F1 season will see a small number of full-time stewards, with the group expanding in 2028 and beyond. The existing FIA stewards will continue to contribute their experience to a mixed roster of full-time and part-time stewards. The new structure will continue to feature a Driver Steward at each event to share their expertise. The FIA is launching a recruitment drive for experienced International Stewards to form the first generation of full-time stewards. The FIA says the full-time stewards will bring more consistency and fairness, and help it keep improving the sporting regulations and stewarding guidelines. They will also play an important role in mentoring future generations of FIA officials. The start of the 2026 Singapore Grand Prix. Image Credit: Sam Bagnall/Sutton Images/Getty Images via Red Bull Content Pool The FIA’s Financial Turnaround Pays for It This is another step by FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem toward fulfilling his promises, amid talks of a V8 return from the 2030 F1 season. It follows last month’s opening of the FIA’s new Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill, UK. The step to secure full-time stewards is possible after a significant financial turnaround under Ben Sulayem, allowing the FIA to invest. A full-time steward would be on a payroll, unlike the historic system, where stewards worked on an unpaid, volunteer basis with only travel and accommodation expenses covered. Ben Sulayem Calls It ‘an Investment in the Future of Our Sport’ Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the field at the start of the 2026 F1 United States Grand Prix. Image Credit: Logan Riely/LAT Images “This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport,” said Ben Sulayem. “The recruitment of full-time stewards is a significant step in our longstanding mission of building a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the FIA Formula One World Championship, it is also an investment in the future of our sport. “Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help to build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships.” Leave a Reply Cancel reply Follow Us Home » Formula 1 » F1 Gets Its First Full-Time Stewards in 2027 as the FIA Plans a Team of Up to 15 Darshan Chokhani Darshan Chokhani is a motorsport news contributor, specialises in Formula 1, with over 10 years of experience. records.excerpt: FIA set to confirm Kimi Antonelli punishment at Las Vegas Grand Prix Kimi Antonelli braced for Las Vegas Grand Prix grid penalty Oliver Harden 19 Nov 2026 7:38 AM Kimi Antonelli is facing a penalty Mercedes driver and F1 2026 world champion Kimi Antonelli will serve a five-place grid penalty for an engine change at this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix. The FIA is expected to confirm the penalty during Thursday practice in Nevada. FIA set to confirm Kimi Antonelli grid penalty at Las Vegas Grand Prix Mercedes is introducing a turbo upgrade in Las Vegas under the FIA’s ADUO (Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities) scheme. The Brackley-based team confirmed earlier this week that only Antonelli will run the new turbo, with teammate George Russell facing an additional grid penalty if he adds further components to his engine pool. It has emerged that Antonelli will also take a new internal combustion engine in Las Vegas, with the change triggering a five-place grid drop. Kimi Antonelli vs George Russell: Mercedes head-to-head stats for F1 2026 season F1 2026: Head-to-head qualifying statistics between teammates F1 2026: Head-to-head race statistics between teammates Toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, gave no indication that Antonelli would serve a grid penalty in Las Vegas in the team’s pre-event preview earlier this week. Wolff also indicated that Mercedes expects the turbo update to bring only a minor performance boost. He said: “We will have the ADUO-enabled turbo specification available from this weekend. “This is primarily about proving out the development in race-weekend conditions, with the expected performance benefit relatively small. “We anticipate running it with Kimi, whilst with George our priority is protecting his grid position with the performance benefit likely too limited to justify taking a grid penalty.” Speaking on Wednesday in Las Vegas, Antonelli identified Red Bull as Mercedes’ biggest threat in Nevada. He said: “I think Red Bull is going to be very strong this weekend. “However, I think we’re the only one who has a set of wings that is slightly less downforce-wise, so a bit less draggy. Let’s see if we’re going to use it here, but definitely it’s going to be very interesting. “I think our power unit has been very strong on the electrical side, obviously also on the combustion, but the electrical side has been very strong. “I think we’re probably the most efficient ones in terms of electrical power and efficiency. “However, Red Bull as well, they have a very strong power unit as well and their car is very efficient on the straight, especially as well with the Macarena wing they have, so I think it’s going to be very interesting. “But as well, it’s so cold this weekend. It’s going to be one of those races that is a bit of an outlier because, again, it’s very difficult on energy, but as well it’s going to be so cold. “Having the tyres in the right temperature is going to be key and also track evolution is going to be massive, so let’s see. “I think tomorrow, FP1, it’s going be drifting [in low-grip conditions] and then maybe FP2 is going to be back to normal driving, but let’s see. “I think our main competitor will be Red Bull this weekend, probably McLaren as well. Let’s see also Ferrari, how they’re going to do.” More on Kimi Antonelli and Mercedes from PlanetF1.com Kimi Antonelli news Mercedes news Antonelli also warned that challenges with deployment and generating tyre temperature in the cold conditions could lead to surprises in Vegas. He explained: “Deployment is not the best [here], I’m not going to lie. “And especially with the long back straight, it’s not the easiest, let’s say, but I guess it’s like this for everyone. “But that will create a lot of opportunity to overtake in all kinds of places. Probably we can expect a yo-yo race because of so many long straights and so many opportunities where to use the battery differently. “But of course, it’s not easy and it’s not going to be straightforward for all of us. “And especially because it’s so cold, you need as much speed as possible everywhere to build any temperature, so I think also the fact of getting the tyre in the right place, I think it’s going to be one of those occasions where you will see us doing multiple warm-up laps just to then start the push lap because definitely going out and pushing straight away is not going to be possible. “Already this year, it has been more difficult to build temperature at any tracks we’ve been. It’s been more difficult to warm up. “I think here it’s going be a step even further on that side. “That’s why I think it’s going to be one of those weekends that could be an outlier because I think just by having the tyres in the right window when starting a push lap is going to be key.” Additional reporting by Thomas Maher Read next: Valtteri Bottas makes feelings clear on Colton Herta rumours after Cadillac announcement Mercedes Kimi Antonelli Related Articles Oliver Harden 20 Nov 2026 FIA confirms Kimi Antonelli penalty at Las Vegas Grand Prix The FIA has made it official. records.title: Max Verstappen struggles in Las Vegas as Red Bull work to fix balance problems
records.excerpt: Red Bull is working to resolve a major balance problem that left Max Verstappen struggling during a disrupted opening day in Las Vegas... Max Verstappen faces ‘major’ Red Bull balance problem after disrupted Las Vegas GP practice Thomas Maher 20 Nov 2026 9:20 AM Red Bull is working to resolve a major balance problem that left Max Verstappen struggling during a disrupted opening day in Las Vegas. Red Bull is working to address the balance problems that affected Max Verstappen during a disrupted opening day at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. After sitting out the entirety of first practice, Verstappen took to the track for just six laps in second practice, but reported a lack of power and difficulties with his RB22’s balance. Max Verstappen struggles with Red Bull RB22 balance in Las Vegas Red Bull’s technical director Pierre Waché said that the four-time F1 World Champion had encountered a “massive issue” with his car balance once his day finally got started at the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Heavy rain severely restricted running during Thursday’s FP1 session, with none of the drivers managing to record a lap time despite green flag conditions throughout. Conditions improved in FP2 as the circuit began to dry, but Verstappen struggled throughout the session, ending the day 13th after reporting a lack of power and difficulties with his car’s balance. “This car is not good, guys!” Verstappen exclaimed over team radio. “This is the same problem as Brazil.” Verstappen climbed all the way to second place at Interlagos, but his chances of catching Lando Norris for victory were reduced significantly by his car abruptly changing behaviour following the change of tyres as the track dried. “I had an extreme amount of oversteer in the car, in the high-speed corners, which made it super difficult to drive,” Verstappen said after the chequered flag. “So we need to understand if something broke on the car, some kind of aero loss or whatever, because this was not normal.” With Verstappen slow to take to the track in FP2, sitting out the first 40 minutes, Waché revealed that Red Bull had deliberately kept him in the garage while the circuit remained wet. “We didn’t plan to run with him when it was full wet tyre conditions,” he explained. “We wanted to check the systems on the car at the beginning, which is why he didn’t run from the start. “After the track dried, we decided to go out on the intermediates before the red flag, but then the red flag happened. We rushed to get him out, unfortunately.” Waché outlined the technical difficulties Verstappen encountered once he eventually began running, highlighting both energy management and balance as areas requiring attention. “He had some issues with the energy management. It wasn’t a massive issue in that respect, just getting the systems working together,” he said. “After that, he had a massive issue with the balance, which we’re trying to understand and fix for tomorrow.” How Free Practice Thursday unfolded in Las Vegas George Russell steals the show with last-gasp lap in Las Vegas GP FP2 Las Vegas FP1 a wash-out with just 20 laps covered and not a single time set With a dry weather forecast for Friday’s final practice and Qualifying, Waché suggested that the team’s performance during Thursday’s sessions offered little indication of their competitiveness for the remainder of the weekend. “The conditions were very cold, and the tyres we use will be completely different tomorrow,” he explained. “I think it will be a completely different day. We’ll be very busy tomorrow afternoon, for sure. But it’s difficult to predict anything at the moment.” While Verstappen may have had a low-key day, Red Bull has reason for optimism following an encouraging performance from his teammate Isack Hadjar, who secured fourth place in FP2 behind George Russell, Pierre Gasly and Charles Leclerc. Indeed, Hadjar looked set to go fastest of all in the tricky wet-to-dry conditions as he set purple sectors in the first and second splits, only for a dawdling Oliver Bearman to put an end to Hadjar’s progress. Waché was pleased with the Frenchman’s performance, particularly his confidence in the car despite the challenging conditions. “I’m happy, and he’s quite happy with the car,” Wache said of Hadjar’s performance. “That’s quite positive. In these conditions, having a car you can trust is quite good.” Hadjar was equally upbeat about his prospects heading into the rest of the weekend, pointing to similarities between the Las Vegas Strip Circuit and the Baku City Circuit as a reason for his confidence. “I have a good feeling about this track,” he said. “This layout in general reminds me of Baku, where we did really well. Long straights, slow-speed corners, low grip. So only the temperature is a different topic. But yeah, let’s see what we can do.” Read Next: Cadillac delays F1 engine debut as GM prepares for 2030 V8 switch Red Bull Max Verstappen

records.excerpt: The Las Vegas Grand Prix will be streamed free in major broadcast change The Las Vegas Grand Prix will be streamed free in major broadcast change Stephen Hurrell 20 Nov 2026 12:14 AM McLaren driver Lando Norris in action in practice at the 2025 Las Vegas Grand Prix This page contains affiliate links and we may earn a commission from any products or services you buy. The Las Vegas Grand Prix will be free to watch in the US without the need for a subscription or even a free trial. Apple TV has confirmed the final North American race of the season will be completely free for fans in the US. It will make Apple TV, Sky Sports and F1TV coverage free to watch here as a gift to fans as the World Championship enters its final stages. Las Vegas Grand Prix will be streamed free in major broadcast change Fans outside the US will not be able to access the coverage without a VPN such as Proton , which has launched its Black Friday deals and offers a free option. Apple TV secured the rights for all of the 2027 F1 season in the US and has been offering all three major streaming services as part of a single streaming package. It has regularly offered free trials to watch the races but this is the first time it is showing the entire event free without a sign up. The glitz and glamour of Las Vegas during a nighttime race is a unique event in the F1 calendar. However, UK viewers will need to get up early to watch the action because of the difference in time zones. The 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix gets underway at 8pm local time on Saturday, November 21. For fans watching in the UK, the race will begin at 4am GMT on Sunday, November 22, meaning an early start for those wanting to catch all the action live. For viewers on the East Coast of the United States, including New York and Miami, lights out is scheduled for 11pm EST on Saturday, November 21. Practice begins on Thursday, November 19, with first practice at 4.30pm local time (12.30am GMT Friday in the UK and 7.30pm EST on Thursday). Second practice follows at 8pm in Las Vegas, which is 4am GMT on Friday in the UK and 11pm EST on Thursday. Final practice takes place on Friday, November 20, at 4.30pm local time, or 12.30am GMT on Saturday in the UK and 7.30pm EST on Friday on the East Coast. Qualifying is scheduled for 8pm local time on Friday, November 20, translating to 4am GMT on Saturday in the UK and 11pm EST on Friday for East Coast viewers. The grid will then be decided ahead of Saturday night’s main event, which begins at 8pm in Las Vegas, 4am GMT in the UK and 11pm EST on the US East Coast. records.excerpt: Oscar Piastri grilled on Mark Webber split ahead of Las Vegas GP Jamie Woodhouse 19 Nov 2026 7:59 PM Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber parted ways McLaren driver Oscar Piastri insisted that his collaboration with Mark Webber had approached a stage where it was better for them to go their separate ways. He reiterated his huge gratitude to Webber and his wife Ann for their role in his career to date. Oscar Piastri and Mark Webber split ‘right time’ On the Monday following the Brazilian Grand Prix, Piastri and Webber both released brief statements which confirmed the end of their alliance. The former Red Bull driver had managed and mentored his younger compatriot since 2019. This parting of ways came after Webber had already scaled back his trackside presence in Piastri’s career in F1 2026. Ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix, the start of a triple-header which brings the season to its conclusion, Piastri was quizzed on the topic. “We were just getting to a stage in our collaboration where it was better for us to go on our separate paths,” he said. “Mark and Ann contributed so much to my career, both in placing me where I am today and the management of everything behind the scenes that nobody ever really sees. It felt like the time was right for something new. “Mark played a massive part in my career, both Mark and Ann, at the end of my junior career, setting me up in Formula 1 and guiding me through those first few years. “The impact they’ve had on my career has been enormous, and I think now it feels like the right time for us both to go on our separate adventures. “I think having the structure around you is an important thing, and it has looked a bit different this year already and will look a bit different again in the future, probably. But they played a big part in where my career is today, so I’m very, very grateful for everything they did.” More on Oscar Piastri from PlanetF1.com Oscar Piastri braced for grid penalty at Las Vegas Grand Prix McLaren explains reasons for Oscar Piastri deficit to Norris in 2026 There is good news and bad news for Piastri heading into the Sin City race. On the plus side, McLaren continues its MCL40 upgrade push this weekend with the arrival of a new floor, as the team continues laying foundations for next season’s car. However, Piastri is due to take a 10-place grid penalty for a fifth internal combustion engine. “Vegas is always unique as a weekend, as an event,” he said. “We’re going to be starting a little bit further behind no matter where we qualify, but yeah, just trying to maximise what we can do. “We don’t know exactly where we’re going to sit with things. Hopefully the new engine is going to help out a little bit! But there are obviously going to be some spots to make up. “Just try and learn as much as we can about the race through practice. We learnt a lot in Monza about what qualifying could look like and the slipstreams and tows that people are going to want. It’s going to be a pretty interesting qualifying session as well as the race, I think.” Read next: Liam Lawson lifts lid on ‘background conversations’ after Racing Bulls contract delay Mark Webber Oscar Piastri

records.excerpt: Charles Leclerc addresses ‘harsh’ FIA punishment after ‘F2’ move on Liam Lawson Jamie Woodhouse 19 Nov 2026 4:01 PM Charles Leclerc does not agree with his Brazilian GP penalty Charles Leclerc does not agree with the five-second penalty which he received after making contact with the Racing Bulls of Liam Lawson in Brazil. That being said, casting his mind back to Mexico City, and the same sanction which he picked up for an incident also involving Ferrari teammate Lewis Hamilton, Leclerc quipped that this was the five seconds which he didn’t get catching back up with him. Charles Leclerc challenges FIA penalty decision Leclerc , on the inside line into Juncao, rubbed wheels with his Racing Bulls rival as they exited the uphill left-hander. It was enough to unsettle Lawson, with the Ferrari driver taking the place as they navigated the Senna S at the end of the long front straight. Lawson compared it to a move from the Monegasque’s junior racing days in GP2 (now Formula 2), in a blunt assessment. The FIA stewards settled on a five-second penalty for Leclerc which demoted him a position to eighth, swapping he and Lawson around in the final classification. “While the contact was minor and Car 30 was able to maintain the lead thereafter, the driver of Car 30 claimed that the contact damaged the rear left rim of his car and also enabled Car 16 to get closer to him on track and then eventually overtake him 5 corners later,” the stewards explained. “Furthermore, under the Driving Standard Guidelines, Car 30 had the right to the corner and it was for Car 16 to take the necessary steps to avoid a collision. “The driver of Car 16 claimed that it was a minor contact with no obvious sporting consequence. “While we acknowledge that the contact was minor, having examined the fight on track between the two cars, we conclude that Car 16 was able to get closer to and thereafter overtake Car 30 because of the contact. The contact clearly disrupted Car 30 and allowed Car 16 to pull up alongside when it was further away before the contact. This was an obvious sporting consequence. “In mitigation, the wet conditions coupled with the nature of the contact (ie minor) was taken into account in imposing a 5-second time penalty as opposed to a 10-second time penalty.” Leclerc was asked ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix whether he believed his penalty received at Interlagos to have been a fair one. “From my point of view, I don’t think it was,” he argued. It was a sanction which had the Ferrari man harking back to the Mexican Grand Prix. Neither he nor Lewis Hamilton made Turn 4, as the Ferraris battled on the opening lap. That opened the door for Max Verstappen to pick off Hamilton and later Leclerc, who was hit with a five-second penalty for leaving the track and gaining an advantage. That move infuriated Hamilton in a spat which would continue into Brazil, before team boss Fred Vasseur held talks where his drivers squashed the beef. “If I look at the last two race weekends, then that’s probably the five seconds that I didn’t get in Mexico,” Leclerc continued. “But if I only look at Brazil, I also believe that for me it’s part of racing, particularly in those conditions. I mean, it’s very tricky to overtake. So you’ve got to take first of all a risk. “I knew that it could end in a slight touch, but I also knew it wouldn’t end in shambles in that particular corner. “So yeah, I thought it was a bit harsh, but it’s also a very difficult decision to take. “I don’t think there’s one very wrong or very right decision, but I do believe that it didn’t deserve the penalty.” More on Charles Leclerc from PlanetF1.com Lewis Hamilton sets record straight after eye-opening Leclerc comments Charles Leclerc responds as journalist faces FIA repercussions over article commentary Attention now switches to Las Vegas and the triple-header which brings F1 2026 to its conclusion. Ferrari is out to secure second in the Constructors’ Championship standings and is in a very strong position to accomplish that. The gap to P3 Red Bull is 95 points. records.excerpt: Fernando Alonso F1 V8s announcement as '16 years pure racing lost' Fernando Alonso makes F1 V8s announcement as ’16 years pure racing lost’ Jamie Woodhouse 19 Nov 2026 12:51 PM Fernando Alonso will not stick around for the new Formula 1 V8s V8 engines are returning to Formula 1 in 2030, according to the FIA president, but Fernando Alonso will not be around to race them. That is the announcement which the 45-year-old made when asked about the topic ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. He looks at it as “16 years lost of pure racing” in the era of hybrid Formula 1 engines. Fernando Alonso will not race into F1’s new V8 era Formula 1’s current set of engine regs only came into force this year, but already, it has been declared by the FIA president that the V8s are coming back in 2030. Alonso , Max Verstappen and Lando Norris have featured among the drivers to criticise the current power units, which have introduced a far greater reliance on electrical energy, the impact seen at times around ‘energy poor’ circuits and through what has been coined ‘yo-yo racing’. The new engine formula is due to feature less electric, and a beefing up of the current V6s to V8s, last used by the sport in 2013. Alonso made his debut all the way back in 2001 when V10s were in fashion. He made an honest admission looking ahead to 2030. “I will not be around for the V8. 100 per cent,” he confirmed to the media. Put to Formula 1’s most experienced driver that he has surprised us all in the past, Alonso added: “Yeah, surprised myself. But this time I think is the good one. “When I stop, it will be the moment and I will try different things. “It’s a long way ahead, and yeah, I think it will be enough.” Quizzed on whether it will be frustrating to miss those new breed F1 V8s by a year or two, he replied: “Yes, frustrating that we didn’t have it in 2014 already. It was from 2014 to 2030 or 2031. “So 16 years or 17 years lost of pure racing.” Alonso is not the only veteran of the current F1 grid who doesn’t envisage himself continuing into that era. “I won’t be able to see them, so it changes nothing for me,” declared Cadillac’s Sergio Perez. Various drivers gave their latest thoughts on the V8s ahead of the Las Vegas race, including Kimi Antonelli, the F1 2026 world champion and youngest to ever do it. He was only seven years old when F1 last used that engine spec. “I think it’s going to be very cool to go back to more old style,” he said. “Also, the cars will get lighter. We’re talking about, I mean, obviously now it’s very early, but probably 70 kilos, which is immense. “Definitely, I think it’s going to be a very exciting regulation change. Many people are looking forward to that.” Latest Formula 1 news on PlanetF1.com Lewis Hamilton sets record straight after eye-opening Leclerc comments ‘Won’t be involved’ – Max Verstappen breaks rank over ‘landmark’ F1 2027 change Williams’ Carlos Sainz is waiting to discover the on-track experience before getting too carried away. “I need to drive it first to see if it’s a win. I think the idea of it definitely is appealing, and what they’re trying to do, it is for me the right direction for the sport. “But then you need to drive it and evaluate it with an actual experience from it, so I look forward to it for sure.” Racing Bulls’ Liam Lawson was singing from the same hymn sheet. That being said, the excitement is bubbling away underneath the surface, after his experiences of driving V8-powered Red Bull cars. “As Carlos said, obviously you need to experience it first, but I’m excited. “Any experience I’ve had growing up watching Formula 1, I was watching the blown diffuser days when [Sebastian] Vettel was fighting with [Lewis] Hamilton, 2010, sort of that time. “I’ve been lucky enough to drive those cars with Red Bull as well, doing show runs, and the feeling is very hard to describe, but it’s an incredible feeling driving those cars. “I feel like it’ll be really, really cool, honestly. But obviously, you don’t know until you actually experience it, what it would be like for everybody.” Read next – Las Vegas GP predictions: Mercedes team orders, Ferrari failure, Lawson surprise Fernando Alonso Related Articles Oliver Harden 19 Nov 2026 Fernando Alonso to miss Las Vegas Grand Prix FP1 as Aston Martin reserve steps in Fernando Alonso will sit out FP1 in Las Vegas. records.excerpt: Charles Leclerc reacts after F1 journalist loses FIA accreditation for remainder of season Charles Leclerc responds as journalist faces FIA repercussions over article commentary Thomas Maher 19 Nov 2026 7:12 AM Ferrari's Charles Leclerc at the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Charles Leclerc has offered his thoughts on an F1 journalist having his accreditation revoked for the remainder of the F1 2026 season following an article written about the Ferrari driver. Daily Mail journalist Jonathan McEvoy revealed in an article last weekend that his FIA accreditation for the remaining three races has been removed following an article in which he labelled Charles Leclerc a “sneaky little b*****d.” Charles Leclerc reacts to journalist losing FIA accreditation Last week, following the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, McEvoy published an article revealing that FIA general manager Alberto Villarreal had called him to tell him that his permanent media pass for the remainder of the season had been revoked. This was following a column after the Mexico City Grand Prix in which McEvoy had referred to the Monegasque in disparaging terms, with the British journalist revealing in his follow-up “half-humorous” column that his contention had been written as an “English idiom.” “You could take a poll of 1,000 people, and perhaps 500 would agree with my argument,” he wrote. “I am not saying I am right. I was just giving my view, albeit containing the half-swear word I have never previously committed to print in my own name. Drivers can’t stop their profanities, incidentally… “It was neither the best piece nor the worst I ever wrote. But journalism is about freedom of expression. It is the whole point of the trade. You can’t be wrong; only people can disagree with you.” The journalist in question is set to sit out the remainder of the season before being eligible to apply for media accreditation for the F1 2027 season, as standard. With Leclerc at the heart of the incident, however unwittingly, the Ferrari driver was asked for his thoughts on the journalist’s expulsion when he appeared before the media ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix. “I saw the article,” Leclerc said. “I was quite surprised by the choice of words, but apart from that, I don’t have much to say. “On the sanction itself, obviously, I have got absolutely nothing to do with it, and I don’t have much to say about it. “The only thing I’ll say is that, as Formula 1 drivers, I think we are used to this kind of criticism: not this kind of criticism, but to criticism in general and to critics. “It’s definitely the job of journalists to kind of ask the bad questions and do some of the tough headlines sometimes, but I was surprised by the choice of words.” When asked by PlanetF1.com for comment on the revocation of press privileges, an FIA spokesperson said, “As set out in the 2026 FIA Formula One World Championship Guidelines, media accreditation is granted at the sole discretion of the FIA and may be revoked at any time without notice. “The Guidelines state that the highest standards of fairness and professionalism are expected as a minimum requirement for media accreditation.” The context of the comment written about Leclerc was due to the ongoing on-track battle for supremacy between the Monegasque and his teammate, Lewis Hamilton, with a tense first lap in Mexico seeing the two jousting for the lead. In the spirited battle, both went off track, resulting in Max Verstappen pouncing to get ahead of Hamilton, before stalking Leclerc and, eventually, coming out on top to snatch a victory away from Ferrari from its early 1-2 position. The tensions were dispelled early in the Brazil weekend, following a meeting between the two drivers and team boss Fred Vasseur at Interlagos. Leclerc opened up on how the meeting had only briefly needed to remain on the topic of the battle, with the pair having quickly moved on to lighten the mood. “I think everything has been taken out of proportion,” he said. “I’m kind of used to it now, driving for Ferrari for so many years, but things are very often taken out of proportion. “Of course, the goal is not always to agree, and that will never happen. We can have different opinions, and that was the case, for example, in Mexico. “Just the fact of speaking is all tension, and we’re completely fine with it. “It’s not that we had to speak for an hour, even though it ended up lasting an hour, just because we had a good time and we started speaking about many other things in trying to help the team go forward. “But the discussion about the tension was like maybe five or 10 minutes, and then the air was clean, and that’s it.” Read next: Lance Stroll warns Honda power deficit could make his Las Vegas GP ‘almost dangerous’ Ferrari Charles Leclerc Related Articles Thomas Maher 20 Nov 2026 F1 results: Las Vegas Grand Prix 2026 – FP2 (Las Vegas Strip Circuit) Check out the complete F1 results from the second practice session (FP2) at the Las Vegas Grand Prix at the Strip Circuit... records.excerpt: FIA announces major F1 stewarding overhaul with full-time officials from 2027 Scuderia Fans Home » FIA announces major F1 stewarding overhaul with full-time officials from 2027 FIA announces major F1 stewarding overhaul with full-time officials from 2027 The FIA has announced a major overhaul of Formula 1 stewarding, confirming that full-time race stewards will be introduced from the 2027 F1 season. The initiative, announced under FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem, aims to improve consistency, fairness and expertise in race officiating, with a long-term objective of establishing a dedicated team of 12 to 15 full-time stewards. The changes will be introduced gradually, marking a significant step towards professionalising how Formula 1 races are officiated. Rather than replacing the existing stewarding structure immediately, the FIA intends to combine newly recruited full-time officials with experienced part-time stewards, while strengthening the resources available to assess incidents and apply sporting regulations consistently. FIA confirms full-time F1 stewards from 2027 The FIA has confirmed that recruitment for the first full-time Formula 1 stewards will begin as part of a phased implementation during the 2027 championship. The initial group will subsequently be expanded from 2028 onwards, with the longer-term ambition of building a department consisting of between 12 and 15 permanent, full-time officials. This represents an important change to the organisation of Formula 1 stewarding, where decisions taken during race weekends have frequently attracted scrutiny over their consistency and interpretation of the regulations. The initiative is designed to strengthen the existing structure rather than immediately replace it. Current stewards will continue to play an essential role, working alongside the newly recruited officials in a mixed system of full-time and part-time personnel for the foreseeable future. The FIA has also emphasised that Driver Stewards will remain a fundamental part of the officiating process at every event. Their direct experience of competitive racing is regarded as particularly valuable when assessing incidents and making sporting decisions. A recruitment campaign will target experienced international stewards, who will form the first generation of full-time FIA officials while complementing the existing pool of qualified personnel. How the new FIA stewarding system aims to improve F1 decisions One of the central objectives behind the introduction of full-time stewards is to establish greater continuity and expertise within Formula 1’s decision-making structure. By employing officials on a permanent basis, the FIA intends to strengthen its commitment to fairness and consistency, supported by the continuous review of sporting regulations and operational guidelines. The new approach should allow best practices to be applied more thoroughly, helping to establish greater uniformity in the decisions made throughout the championship. Consistency has been a recurring subject of debate in Formula 1, including situations involving Lewis Hamilton’s criticism of FIA stewarding decisions . However, the responsibilities of full-time stewards will extend beyond the investigation of incidents during Grand Prix weekends. Between races, the dedicated officials will have greater opportunities to identify emerging trends, examine recurring situations and highlight areas of the regulations that require clarification. This continuous involvement is intended to support the evolution of the sporting rules and improve the overall quality of officiating across Formula 1. Full-time stewards will also be involved in training and mentoring future generations of FIA officials, contributing to the federation’s High Performance Programme and encouraging greater consistency between different championships. Existing F1 stewards and Driver Stewards will retain important roles Although the new structure represents a substantial change, the FIA has made it clear that experienced officials currently working in Formula 1 will remain essential to the system. The introduction of full-time positions will take place progressively throughout 2027, with further recruitment and expansion planned from 2028 onwards. For an extended period, Formula 1 will therefore operate with a combination of full-time and part-time stewards, allowing the federation to preserve the experience already available within its officiating network. The specialist contribution of Driver Stewards will also remain important at every Grand Prix, with their practical knowledge of racing continuing to inform the assessment of on-track incidents. The programme is expected to develop over several years until the planned group of 12 to 15 full-time stewards has been established. Once the department reaches its intended size, the FIA also plans to extend its support progressively to other championships under the federation’s authority. FIA Remote Operations Centre forms part of wider Formula 1 restructuring The introduction of permanent stewards forms part of a broader effort to strengthen Formula 1 officiating, combining investment in personnel, expertise and technological infrastructure. One of the most significant recent developments has been the opening of the FIA Remote Operations Centre at Biggin Hill in the United Kingdom. This facility represents another element of the federation’s investment in race management and is intended to support the highest standards of officiating. The wider restructuring began under FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem at the beginning of his tenure, initially including a complete reorganisation of Race Control in 2022. That was followed by the creation of the FIA Officials department and continued investment in operational systems, training and infrastructure. The emphasis on developing a more professional officiating structure also reflects the growing demands placed on race officials, an issue previously highlighted in discussions about Formula 1’s expanding responsibilities and the limitations facing volunteer officials . According to the FIA, the programme has been made possible by a significant improvement in the federation’s financial position under its current leadership, enabling further investment in its core sporting responsibilities. The objective is to ensure that the people and structures responsible for managing championships receive the resources required to perform their duties at the highest level. Mohammed Ben Sulayem explains major FIA investment in F1 stewarding FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem described the introduction of full-time Formula 1 stewards as a significant investment in the future of motorsport officiating. “This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to ensuring the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport. The recruitment of full-time stewards represents a significant step in our long-standing mission to build a dedicated officiating ecosystem in the Formula 1 World Championship; it is also an investment in the future of our sport. “Following the milestone opening of the new FIA Remote Operations Centre and the strengthening of officiating development through initiatives such as the FIA High Performance Programme, this development will help build greater expertise and continuity within our stewarding structure, strengthening our ability to review and improve regulations, support the development of future officials and ensure the highest standards of consistent officiating across all our championships.” The comments underline the federation’s intention to create a more specialised and consistent officiating system, with permanent personnel contributing not only to race decisions but also to regulatory development and the training of future officials. Alonso to miss Las Vegas FP1 as Aston Martin announce driver change Photo: Race Pictures Breaking News Updated : 19:31, 18 Nov 2 Comments Henry Eccles Henry Eccles is a freelance Formula 1 journalist for GPblog, covering breaking news, live race blogs, and features across the F1 calendar. Since joining in 2026, he has produced high-volume reporting on the sport’s biggest stories, alongside feature pieces including analysis and historical content. Fernando Alonso will miss FP1 of the Las Vegas GP, with Aston Martin announcing third driver Jak Crawford will participate in the practice session at the Vegas strip circuit. The FP1 session will be a special one for Crawford , with the 21-year-old American making his first F1 appearance on home soil. It is also Crawford's fifth FP1 appearance of the 2026 season, having accumulated 4,800 kilometres behind the wheel of an F1 car. Crawford most recently drove the AMR26 at the Mexico City GP, filling in for Lance Stroll. Speaking on Aston Martin's website, Crawford said: "I'm really looking forward to getting back behind the wheel of the AMR26 in Las Vegas. It's particularly special to be doing it in the United States, and I'm excited to get out on track in front of the American fans. "My session in Mexico City finished earlier than planned, so it's great to have another opportunity to get behind the wheel again so soon. I'll be focused on making the most of the session and providing useful feedback to help the team prepare for the weekend." With the focus on the young American's development, Aston's chief trackside officer Mike Krack added: "We're pleased to give Jak another opportunity to drive the AMR26 in Las Vegas. ADVERTISEMENT "Making his first FP1 appearance in the United States will be a special moment, and this session provides another opportunity for him to build on his experience while supporting our preparations for the weekend." records.title: McLaren address Mercedes partnership for next F1 power unit regulations
records.excerpt: Article To news overview © XPB Images McLaren has no plans to design its own power unit for Formula 1's next engine regulations, according to CEO Zak Brown, who says the Woking-based squad remains fully committed to its Mercedes customer relationship. The topic has gained fresh relevance with F1, the FIA and manufacturers pushing to introduce a 2.1-litre turbocharged V8 formula from 2030, a year earlier than originally planned under the current cycle. McLaren has run as a Mercedes High Performance Powertrains customer since the start of the current regulations and is contracted to continue doing so through 2030, alongside fellow customers Williams and Alpine. Brown's comments come after McLaren endured early reliability issues in 2026, including hybrid battery problems that contributed to a double no-show in China, and after the team previously acknowledged a calibration knowledge gap compared to the factory Mercedes operation. Asked whether McLaren was considering building its own power unit, Brown told the Sky F1 podcast there was no such plan in motion. Team McLaren Lando Norris Oscar Piastri News Results Statistics "There's no plan," said Brown. "You know, it's something that we look at. We're very happy with Mercedes HPP; they've been a great partner. We won two championships. I think we debunked the 'you can't win a championship with a customer engine' argument, so I think people don't need to kind of worry about that anymore. "I think the challenge is, you can do what Red Bull did, well done. You can also be where Aston Martin is right now, so I'm just not sure the risk is worth the reward when we can win championships with Mercedes. "Some of these challenges we had at the start of the year, if you had your own engine... But then if you get it wrong... "So, I think with the V8s being pulled forward to 2030, which is what it looks like, I also think that, whether we wanted to or not, I don't think there's enough time to get ready. So, I think it's a watching brief, but at this point we have no plan." Brown's reference to Aston Martin points to the Silverstone-based outfit's well-documented struggles since switching to a works Honda power unit this season, with packaging and vibration issues severely restricting its early-season running. Red Bull, by contrast, successfully launched its own in-house engine project with Ford backing for 2026. records.title: Lance Stroll faces frightening Las Vegas prospect as Honda power deficit bites
records.excerpt: Lance Stroll expects a difficult Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Honda's lack of power so severe that he fears it could become dangerous... Lance Stroll warns Honda power deficit could make his Las Vegas GP ‘almost dangerous’ Thomas Maher 19 Nov 2026 3:21 AM Lance Stroll expects a difficult Las Vegas Grand Prix, with Honda's lack of power so severe that he fears it could become dangerous. Lance Stroll says the lack of power from his Honda power unit will be “almost dangerous” on the long straights of the Las Vegas Strip Circuit. With Honda as one of the weakest power units of the five manufacturers, the disparity in performance is such that Stroll is anticipating an unenjoyable weekend due to the length of the back straight at the Las Vegas venue. Lance Stroll fears Honda power deficit will hurt Aston Martin in Las Vegas While reliability has been a major issue for Honda this season, the Japanese manufacturer has also struggled for outright performance. Under the FIA’s ADUO [Additional Development and Upgrade Opportunities], Honda is one of three manufacturers to be found over the four per cent threshold to earn two homologation upgrades, with multiple sources having indicated that it is Honda which is bringing up the rear of the PUMs behind Ferrari and Audi, which are also over the four per cent mark. Following the arrival of Aston Martin’s significant upgrade package in Budapest, the aero and mechanical performance of the AMR26 has proven capable: Fernando Alonso went as far as to call it “phenomenal” through the corners after the recent Interlagos race, having been able to keep up with, and battle, the Ferraris. But, on power-sensitive circuits, Aston Martin slumps to the rear of the pack once again, due to the deficit of power and reliability that it, as well as Honda, is transparent about. Ahead of the Las Vegas weekend, Honda chief engineer Shintaro Orihara explained how further countermeasures have been introduced to the Honda battery to mitigate recent issues on the ERS side of the power unit. But the deficit is such that, along the fearsomely long straight that encompasses the Las Vegas Strip, Lance Stroll is anticipating an unpleasant weekend in the United States. “If you have a good car, I’m sure you enjoy it, like every track. But this weekend will most likely not be very enjoyable for us,” he said of the circuit, which debuted on the F1 calendar in 2023; a year in which the Canadian driver finished fifth in the altogether more competitive AMR23. “I mean, it’s probably going to be a tough weekend for us. Lots of long straights here, and we know we’re very down on power. That’s probably been our biggest issue this year, or probably has been our biggest issue this year, is just the lack of power in the long straights. And here, there’s a lot of straights, so it’ll probably be a tough weekend, but we’ll do the best we can. “We’re really down on power. We’re probably going to be like two seconds just down on the straights. So it’s not going to be feeling great out there with all these straights and with the lack of power we have. “Sometimes it’s almost dangerous, that lack of power, at times, how much we’re missing. So yeah, some good memories here. It’s just probably not going to be as enjoyable this weekend. But yeah, we’ll try to get what we can out of it.” With three races remaining on the calendar, including Las Vegas, 2026 has been an annus horribilis for the Silverstone-based squad, whose first car under Adrian Newey has been significantly hamstrung by the weakness of the Honda power unit. The reasons for the underperformance from the Japanese manufacturer are well-documented at this point, and, with the end of the first season together in sight, Stroll pointed to how he believes a much brighter future awaits. “[We’ve had] a lot of issues throughout the year. Way too many retirements,” he said. “We know that we’re not where we want to be, so we’re just focused on the future and trying to make things better. “I’m just thinking a lot about the future. I think we have a great team. We have really good people, really talented people. We’re not where we want to be right now, but I think the future is very exciting for Aston Martin. So I’m just thinking about that.” Asked about what this future could look like, perhaps even as soon as the F1 2027 season, Stroll said, “The plan is to hopefully make a big step forward, but we’ll see. All I know is we have a great team back at Silverstone. Everyone’s pushing really hard. [There’s] a lot of talent in Silverstone. So yeah, hopefully we get much stronger soon.” Unlike his teammate, Fernando Alonso, who is dovetailing his preparations for ’27 with another appearance in the Dakar Rally, competing with an Aston Martin entry, Stroll revealed he has “nothing planned” in terms of any extracurricular racing outside of F1. His focus is on staying positive between now and the 2027 season opener in Bahrain, during which time the Canadian could yet set an unenviable record. Having retired from 13 races this year, he is one race retirement away from matching the record of 14 DNFs in a season, set by Andrea de Cesaris in 1986 and ’87, and Rubens Barrichello in 1997. “I heard about it, but, like, you know, we had a lot of issues out there, a lot of engine problems,” he said, when asked about whether such a record is on his mind. “It’s been a tough year for the whole team. We’re just not nearly as competitive as we want to be, and it’s been a long year for everyone. “But as I said earlier, all we can do is just stay positive and look forward to the future, and hopefully we’ll be in a much more competitive spot next year.” Read Next: Fernando Alonso admits Dakar Rally plans were linked to potential F1 retirement Aston Martin Lance Stroll

The 21-year-old has made four FP1 appearances so far this year, most recently at the Mexican Grand Prix, where he was forced to stop trackside after his car developed a problem. Ahead of this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix, Aston Martin has confirmed that Crawford will have a fifth FP1 outing of the season in Thursday practice, deputising for Alonso.
