records.title: SpaceX Plans Vermilion Parish Wharf to Ship Louisiana-Made Rocket Parts
records.excerpt: A new SpaceX Vermilion Parish filing outlines a logistics hub for Louisiana-fabricated components: a 3,529-foot wharf, barge access and a heavy-haul road. SpaceX Plans Vermilion Parish Wharf to Ship Louisiana-Made Rocket Parts SpaceX Plans Vermilion Parish Wharf to Ship Louisiana-Made Rocket Parts Joe Cunningham Joe Cunningham Published: November 17, 2026 Justin Sullivan, Getty Images Share on Facebook Share on Twitter SpaceX plans to build a wharf and shipping hub on Freshwater Bayou in coastal Vermilion Parish to move Louisiana-made rocket components to its Texas and Florida facilities, according to newly filed state permit documents . A Nov. 9 addition to SpaceX’s coastal use permit application gives a clearer picture of the company’s $100 billion launch and recovery facility. The facility is planned south of Pecan Island, roughly 45 miles southwest of Lafayette. The new filing calls for a wharf about two-thirds of a mile long and extensive dredging. A heavy-haul road would link barge traffic to oceangoing ships. Get our free mobile app What Would the Hub Mean for Louisiana Suppliers? SpaceX already buys tens of millions of dollars in materials and equipment fabricated in Louisiana for its Texas and Florida operations, the application says. Right now, suppliers and vendors arrange their own transportation and storage, often by rail, truck or third-party port. SpaceX says that requires some equipment to be built in smaller sections that fit rail cars, tractor-trailers or shipping containers. Building in sections adds fabrication, handling and transportation costs, the company says. Credit: Joe Cunningham/TSM Credit: Joe Cunningham/TSM The hub would let SpaceX consolidate that work, from receiving and inspecting Louisiana-made components to storing and loading them for shipment. Under the plan, Louisiana-built equipment would be loaded onto barges at or near the proposed Pecan Island fabrication site. The barges would travel the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway and project channels to an inland wharf. The cargo would be unloaded and staged there. Specialized heavy-haul vehicles would then carry large components along a connecting road to a Gulf-facing wharf. Ocean-going vessels would take them from there to SpaceX facilities in Texas and Florida. The site sits directly on the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway , which early reporting identified as an advantage of the location. How Big Is the Wharf and Dredging Plan? The filing lists a 3,529-foot wharf along Freshwater Bayou Channel, south of the Army Corps of Engineers’ Freshwater Bayou Lock. That location gives SpaceX access to the Gulf of Mexico without passing through the lock. Construction would require dredging more than 1.16 million cubic yards of material across about 54 acres. The work would create ship berths and a turning basin and deepen parts of the channel to 16 feet. The heavy-haul road would connect inland wharf facilities to the Gulf wharf. The original application , received by state regulators Sept. 25, listed the wharf at 3,500 feet. It also described a heavy-haul road of roughly 15.5 to 16 miles and an elevated bridge of about 1.5 miles. Does the Wharf Depend on the Launch Site? SpaceX says it does not. The project “has utility independent of any other development,” the company stated in its permit documents. The wharves would support its existing operations and Louisiana suppliers, SpaceX says, whether or not other proposed facilities are built. The launch site is a much larger undertaking. SpaceX and state officials announced Aug. 25 that Starbase Louisiana would include five launch complexes at full buildout, each with two launch pads. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, with a first launch targeted as soon as 2029. Which Roads and Bridges Does the Application Mention? The permit documents also describe transportation work planned or underway in the region. The Louisiana Department of Transportation and Development is investing in several road and bridge projects. Those include improvements to La. 3147, also called Freshwater City Road, and rehabilitation or replacement of bridges along La. 82, La. 92, and La. 339. Photo by Joe Raedle/Getty Images SpaceX Falcon-9 Rocket And Crew Dragon Capsule Launches From Cape Canaveral Sending Astronauts To The International Space Station The application also references a proposed bypass from the Lafayette Metropolitan Expressway Commission. The semicircular route would connect Interstates 10 and 49 with U.S. 90. SpaceX’s heavy-haul access road would tie into that proposed network at La. 82. State and federal highway officials posted notice of a Tier 1 environmental decision on the corridor in February 2023. State records describe it as a controlled-access toll road. What Happens Next for Vermilion Parish? The Nov. 9 filing adds to a permit request submitted to state and federal regulators. The September application lists a work window from March 1, 2027, to Sept. 1, 2032. SpaceX has said it will also fund marsh rebuilding and shoreline protection beyond what regulators require. As of early September, the scope and spending were unclear . At SpaceX’s first public meeting with parish residents in September, a packed crowd of supporters and critics filled Magdalen Place in Abbeville. Some residents worry the project will change the rural landscape. Others see a major economic opportunity. records.title: BBM: Phl eyes SpaceX deal to host commercial rocket launches
records.excerpt: The Philippines is exploring a potential partnership with SpaceX to develop commercial rocket launch sites in the country, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said, as the government seeks to attract foreign operators to the emerging space industry. The Philippines is exploring a potential partnership with SpaceX to develop commercial rocket launch sites in the country, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said, as the government seeks to attract foreign operators to the emerging space industry. BUSINESS Elon Musk President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Elon Musk's SpaceX SpaceX Philippines BBM: Phl eyes SpaceX deal to host commercial rocket launches TM Toby Magsaysay · 20 November 2026 · 5:11 PM PHT · 3 MIN READ DAILY TRIBUNE images Text size Save The Philippines is exploring a potential partnership with SpaceX to develop commercial rocket launch sites in the country, President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said, as the government seeks to attract foreign operators to the emerging space industry. Speaking on the sidelines of the APEC Summit in Shenzhen, China, Marcos said discussions with the company founded by billionaire Elon Musk were still at an early stage. He said the proposal was aimed at making the Philippines a commercial launch site rather than establishing a national space program. “We are just beginning any kind of discussions thus far. But what is happening is he is expanding the launch sites for SpaceX. And maybe the Philippines can look into it,” Marcos told reporters in Shenzhen on Friday. Also read PSEi plunges to weakest close since March 2020 “We are not trying to be NASA. We are not trying to send a man to the moon or to Mars. What we are trying to do is to get into the business of launch sites,” he added. The President said the country's location along the western Pacific could make it suitable for rocket launches, with the government hoping SpaceX would consider the Philippines as it expands its launch operations. Marcos also clarified that the recent rocket launch in Cagayan was not the start of a national space program but part of efforts to build a commercial business that would attract launch operators. “The launch of our rocket in Cagayan is not the beginning of a space program. It is the beginning of a business that will attract launches. You can pay for that,” he said. A local launch site could also make it easier and cheaper for the Philippines to deploy its own satellites, Marcos said. Also read LIMA Estate showcases model for higher-value investments Asked about reports that Musk was considering developing two Philippine islands, the President said he had no details and that no concrete arrangements had been made. “I don't have any details on it. I don't think there are any details on it,” he said. The proposed venture remains exploratory, with no investment agreement or confirmed launch-site locations announced. Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel ‘Babes’ Romualdez said on Thursday that Musk frequently visits the Philippines discreetly and was reportedly eyeing one or two islands for possible investments or development. It remains unclear whether the islands mentioned by Romualdez are being considered for the proposed SpaceX launch sites. "From what I'm told, Elon Musk comes here quietly very often because he has one or two islands, I'm told, that he's developing," Romualdez said. "Again, that's a big sign. The richest man in the world is actually very interested in the Philippines. He loves the Philippines,” he said. Follow Daily Tribune on Google News

AnthropicのIPOが近づく――ナスダックはSpaceX上場前のラリーを再現できるか？ $アンソロピック (ANT.US)$ 技術株が継続的な圧力に直面する中、同社の11月19日の上場が予定されている。新規株式公開そのものに加え、投資家はAI関連株への信頼回復につながるかどうかを注視している。 との比較 $スペースX (SPCX.US)$ 6月のIPOは興味深い類似点を示している。 $ナスダック総合 (.IXIC.US)$ は両社の上場前に下落した。ただし、SpaceXの上場前には、指数はIPOの2営業日前に短期安値をつけ、その後回復した。 Anthropicの株式公開がカレンダー上で同様の時期に近づいている中、再び反発が起こる可能性はあるか？ 大型上場2件を控えた局面で似たような調整が発生 SpaceXの上場6営業日前のナスダック終値を起点とすると、指数は上場2営業日前までに6.19%下落した。 これが観察期間中の安値となった。その後ナスダックは反発し、上場後の初営業日には起点からわずか0.55%低い水準まで戻した。 Anthropicの上場予想前にも類似のパターンが見られる。11月17日、つまり予定される上場の2営業日前時点で、ナスダックは公募の6営業日前の終値から4.47%下落していた。 下落幅は小さかったものの、タイミング的には過去に回復局面入りした時期と同じ窓に入っている。 そのため、この比較は注目する価値がある。ただし、現在の調整が底入れしたことを意味するものではない。 類似のタイミングが同じ結果を保証するわけではない SpaceXの事例は歴史的な比較対象であり、信頼性の高い予測ルールではない。また、あの時の反発がIPOによって広範な市場の回復が引き起こされたことを証明するものでもない。 今日のテクノロジーセクターは、バリュエーション、収益予想、AIインフラへの資金調達に関する疑問点に依然直面している。これらの要因が、上場スケジュールに関わらず、株価が安定化するかどうかを決定づけるだろう。 Anthropicの株式公開初日がAIへの投資家の関心を再び喚起すれば、市場センチメントの触媒となる可能性があります。ただし、単一の銘柄への熱狂だけでは、セクター全体の投資収益率や資金調達ニーズに関する懸念を解消することはできません。 より説得力のある回復を実現するには、幅広い証拠が必要です。ナスダックの安定化、AI関連資産への資本流入の再開、そして企業ファンダメンタルズに対する信頼感の改善が求められます。 結論 Anthropicの予想されるIPO前におけるナスダックの下落は、SpaceXの上場前の調整局面と似ています。前の事例では、指数は上場初日の2営業日前から回復し始めており、Anthropicも現在まさにその期間に入っています。 重要な点は、この株式公開が単に新規上場銘柄への注目を集めるだけでなく、テクノロジー株全般の信頼回復に寄与できるかどうかです。 歴史は有用な比較材料を提供してくれます。ファンダメンタルズ、資本フロー、そしてリスク選好度が、今回も同様の回復をもたらすかどうかを決定づけるでしょう。 免責事項：このコンテンツは、Moomoo Technologies Incが情報交換及び教育目的でのみ提供するものです。 さらに詳しい情報 24 3 1 1386万 回閲覧 報告 コメント（2） サインイン コメントをする コメント入力 2 28 records.title: アンソロピック、IPO引受手数料5.5億ドル SpaceXの記録を更新

Anthropicが米国証券取引委員会（SEC）に提出した書類によると、同社はIPOに際してウォール街の投資銀行に約5.5億ドル（約880億円）の引受手数料を支払った。これはSpaceXが保持していた5億ドル（約800億円）の記録を上回る。ゴールドマン・サックスとモルガン・スタンレーが主幹事を務め、他に20行が配分に参加した。引受手数料率は約68ベーシスポイント。Anthropicと7人の共同創業者は、規模を拡大したIPOと同時期の私募増資を合わせて1,073億ドル（約17.2兆円）を調達し、史上最大の上場調達記録を樹立した。最先端の大規模モデルを主力とする企業として初めて公開市場に上場する。なお、両案件ともグリーンシュー・オプション部分については引受手数料を支払っていない。 11月19日、人工知能企業Anthropicが米国証券取引委員会（SEC）に提出した最新の書類により、同社が新規株式公開（IPO）に際してウォール街の投資銀行団に約5.5億ドル（約880億円）の引受手数料を支払ったことが明らかになった。この数字は従来SpaceXが保持していた5億ドル（約800億円）の記録を上回り、史上最大規模のIPO引受手数料となった。 書類によると、Anthropicが同意した引受手数料率は約68ベーシスポイントで、SpaceXの上場案件で投資銀行が受け取った配分水準とほぼ同程度である。ゴールドマン・サックス（GS）とモルガン・スタンレー（MS）が今回のIPOの主幹事を務め、両社はSpaceXの上場案件でも同様の中核的役割を担った。この2社に加え、他に20行がAnthropicのIPOに参加し、この引受手数料を比例配分で受け取る。 引受団には日本の金融グループ2社の米国子会社が含まれている。登録書類によれば、みずほフィナンシャルグループ傘下のみずほ証券アメリカと、三菱UFJフィナンシャル・グループ傘下のMUFG証券アメリカスがいずれも引受人名簿に記載されている。日経アジアの報道によると、みずほはソフトバンク関連取引の経験を活かして米国株式引受市場を開拓し、Armの2023年米国上場やPayPayの2026年3月の米国上場で主幹事を務めたほか、2026年6月のSpaceX上場時にも引受団に加わった。三菱UFJはモルガン・スタンレーと2008年から戦略的提携関係にある。今回のIPOの公募販売範囲は日本、オーストラリア、カナダ、英国、スイスおよび一部の欧州経済領域諸国に及ぶ。 Anthropicと7人の共同創業者は、規模を拡大したIPOおよび同時期に実施した私募増資を通じて、合計1,073億ドル（約17.2兆円）を調達し、史上最大規模の上場調達記録を樹立した。最先端の大規模モデルの研究開発を主力事業とする企業が公開市場に上場するのはこれが初めてである。 今回のIPOは11月18日に公開価格が決定され、1株83ドル（約1.3万円）と、当初予定していた70～78ドル（約1.1万～1.2万円）のレンジを上回った。完全希薄化ベースの評価額は約1.5兆ドル。株式は11月19日にナスダックに上場し、ティッカーシンボルはANT。ロイター通信の報道によると、競合のOpenAIは早ければ2027年に上場を目指す見通しだ。 両案件にはもう一つ共通する特殊な取り決めがある。AnthropicとSpaceXはいずれも、超過配分選択権（グリーンシュー・オプション）部分について投資銀行に引受手数料を支払っていない。グリーンシュー・オプションは、新株上場直後に株価が下落した場合、引受幹事が超過配分分の株式を活用して市場価格を安定させることができる仕組みである。 対照的に、通常のIPOでは1件あたりの調達規模は一般に10億ドル（約1,600億円）未満で、投資銀行が受け取る引受手数料率は調達額の4～7％程度が一般的だ。超大型案件では手数料率が大幅に圧縮され、多くの投資銀行が引受ランキングでより上位の座を獲得する代わりに、より低い報酬を受け入れることをいとわない。集計データによると、SpaceX案件に牽引され、ウォール街の大手投資銀行の第2四半期の株式引受アドバイザリー収入は2021年以来の高水準となった。9月30日までの四半期では、ゴールドマン・サックスが引受ランキング首位に立った。 案件 上場時期 調達規模 引受手数料 引受手数料率 Anthropic 2026年11月 1,073億ドル（IPO 813億＋私募260億） 5.5億ドル 約68ベーシスポイント SpaceX 2026年6月 750億ドル（約12兆円） 5億ドル 約67ベーシスポイント アリババ 2014年9月 250億ドル（約4兆円、超過配分含む） 3.004億ドル（約480億円） 1.2% 一般IPO — 通常10億ドル未満 — 4%～7% 注：SpaceXとAnthropicはいずれも超過配分部分について引受手数料を支払っていない。Anthropicの引受手数料率は813億ドルのIPO規模に基づいて計算。 業界全体の観点から見ると、Anthropicの上場は最先端大規模モデル企業に公開市場での資金調達ルートを切り開いた。その1,000億ドル超の調達規模と5.5億ドルの引受手数料は、後続の同種テクノロジー企業の価格設定や投資銀行サービスの手数料率に参照基準を提供する。引受幹事にとっては、こうした超大型案件は手数料率が圧縮されるものの、もたらされる収入の絶対額とランキング効果は依然として無視できない。

records.excerpt: Anthropic joins SpaceX as a mega-IPO company Skip to main content Chart shows sums raised in the top global IPOs. The largest is SpaceX at $86 billion, Anthropic is second at $93.5 billion. Anthropic joins SpaceX as a mega-IPO company The AI company goes public Includes exercise of overallotment options. Anthropic’s have not been exercised yet and the $93.5 billion figure assumes they will be fully exercised. Anthropic has surpassed SpaceX in making the largest stock market debut on record, raising $81.3 billion in an initial public offering that could increase to as much as $93.5 billion if overallotment options are exercised. The AI developer of Claude also raised another $26 billion through a private placement of shares alongside the IPO offering, securities filings showed. SpaceX’s IPO in June had raised a total of $86 billion including the exercise of overallotment options. Anthropic’s owners plowed ahead with their decision to go public despite a recent selloff across the tech landscape, as investors question whether the AI boom’s returns will justify the massive spending and mounting debt costs in an elevated interest-rate environment. Unlike previous generations of major technology companies, Anthropic is going public with a business built almost entirely around generative AI, a technology that has only recently gained widespread commercial adoption. Its proprietary large language model, Claude, is at the center of that business. Anthropic is all AI Estimated shares of 2026 Q2 revenue from different sectors for four companies with significant AI investment A graphic showing the estimated share of revenue from AI for companies Anthropic, SpaceX, Salesforce and Amazon during the second quarter of 2026. Anthropic is 100% AI while AI makes up less than 50% of the others. Anthropic’s September prospectus detailed how the company has grown sharply in the last year — revenue grew twelvefold in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion. However, compared with other major tech companies, such as those in the Magnificent 7, its revenue is still modest. Anthropic still posts relatively modest revenue Market value versus annual revenue in 2025 for select companies $0 $1 $2 $3 $4 $5 trillion Market capitalization $0 $200 $400 $600 $800 billion Annual revenue Amazon Apple Alphabet Microsoft Meta Nvidia Tesla SpaceX Anthropic Magnificent 7 Chart showing market value versus annual revenue for select firms. Still, so far in 2026, Anthropic’s revenue has continued to grow, especially during the first two quarters. This growth has so far defied concerns over potential greater oversight and regulatory hurdles, propelled by surging demand ​for its products, particularly its ⁠viral Claude models. Anthropic’s revenue growth While quarterly revenue is increasing, the pace of growth slowed during the third quarter Revenue in each quarter $20 billion $15 $10 $5 0 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 Quarterly growth in revenue +160% +120 +80 +40 0 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 Revenue in each quarter $20 billion $15 $10 $5 0 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 Quarterly growth in revenue +160% +120 +80 +40 0 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 Revenue in each quarter Quarterly growth in revenue $20 billion +160% $15 +120 $10 +80 $5 +40 0 0 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 Revenue in each quarter Quarterly growth in revenue $20 billion +160% $15 +120 $10 +80 $5 +40 0 0 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 2025 Q2 Q3 Q4 2026 Q1 Q2 Q3 A chart shows the quarterly revenue amount for Anthropic and its quarterly growth. Its revenue has grown dramatically to $17 billion in the third quarter of this year, however the speed at which it is growing has slowed. Anthropic’s net loss narrowed to $23.29 billion in the third quarter of 2026 from $66.3 billion in the second quarter. Its net loss widened to $80.7 billion in the first half of 2026, largely reflecting an increase in the fair value of bonds convertible into company shares, up from $13 billion a year earlier. Its operating loss last year was $8.06 billion, larger than many companies with comparable revenue numbers. Anthropic’s stock will be closely watched when trading opens on the Nasdaq on Thursday — and long afterward. records.title: Starlink Lost 1,000 Customers After Forcing Pilots Onto Expensive New Plans
records.excerpt:
SpaceX reveals the subscriber impact in response to a class-action lawsuit over a March restriction and price hike affecting small plane owners.

Starlink’s decision to increase prices on small plane owners in March caused about 1,000 of them in the US to cancel the satellite internet service, according to a class-action lawsuit.

The figure was revealed in a court document SpaceX filed while moving the lawsuit from California Superior Court to US District Court. The class action was filed in September by a California customer, Thomas Daniel, who alleged that Starlink engaged in a “bait-and-switch” scheme by promoting its service to plane owners, only to suddenly change the plans.

SpaceX imposed a 100mph limit on the more affordable Starlink Roam plans, effectively blocking planes from accessing it. Instead, the company pushed affected customers to new, but pricier aviation plans that permitted speeds of 300mph and 450mph, but could cost as much as $1,000 per month, and required extra payment to exceed the data caps.

You May Also Like

In a 10-page court filing, Cory Clark, a senior partnership manager for Starlink’s aviation business, disclosed the subscriber impact. “Approximately two weeks after the aviation plans were offered, more than 1,500 customers in the United States switched from a non-aviation plan to an aviation plan. This data excludes customers who initiated an aviation plan without any prior history with Starlink,” he said.

But on cancellations, Clark noted: “There were more than 1,000 customers in the United States who received the March 1, 2026, email advising that they exceeded the speed threshold and thereafter cancelled their service within 35 days (the next billing cycle).”

That said, it’s possible some of those customers returned. In late April, Starlink slightly improved some of the pricing and perks for the aviation plans. However, Clark’s filing doesn’t address this.

records.title: Anthropic’s IPO nets Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley $113 million apiece in fees, eclipsing their SpaceX paydays
records.excerpt: Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO on Thursday delivered one of Wall Street’s largest underwriting paydays in history, with the banks behind the listing raking in at least $550 million in fees, eclipsing the $500 million that was earned from Elon Musk–led SpaceX’s debut in June. Recommended Video Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley , the lead underwriters on the deal, each garnered fees of $113 million, according to Anthropic’s prospectus and confirmed by a source familiar with the matter. That’s because they both took on underwriting commitments of 20.5% of the $81.3 billion IPO. It’s also more than the roughly $100 million Goldman and Morgan Stanley each raked in from fees on the SpaceX deal over the summer. JPMorgan and Citigroup each agreed to underwrite 10% of the Claude maker’s offering, putting their estimated fees at roughly $55 million apiece if allocated in proportion to their commitments. Bank of America , which committed to underwriting 3%, would receive an estimated $16.5 million in fees. The last IPO to generate more than Anthropic’s in underwriting commissions was Visa’s 2008 debut, which delivered a $550.2 million fee pool. Anthropic could surpass that figure if underwriters exercise the offering’s over-allotment option, which allows banks to sell up to 15% more shares than initially planned. Anthropic shares, trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, surged 17% in their Thursday debut, giving the company a fully diluted market capitalization of $1.27 trillion at the close. The $81.3 billion offering was the largest IPO in history by deal size. Anthropic’s listing generated roughly 30 to 40 times the commissions of a typical IPO owing to its massive size, according to Matt Kennedy, senior IPO market strategist at Renaissance Capital. “By deal count, 2026 wasn’t the blowout year many were hoping for,” Kennedy said in a statement to Fortune. “So, mega IPOs like Anthropic have done a lot of the heavy lifting to make this a standout year for investment banks.” Fortune Daily breaks the traditional barrier between audience and newsroom. records.title: Crypto platform’s plan to offer tokenized shares for Anthropic IPO comes up short, following similar SpaceX flop
records.excerpt: In the lead up to Anthropic’s record-setting Thursday IPO , several crypto platforms announced plans to offer their customers exposure to the offering in the form of tokens tied to its shares. It’s far from clear, however, whether these tokenized stocks—crypto tokens designed to track a stock’s price—will actually provide exposure at Anthropic’s offering price, or at all. The maker of the Claude chatbot opened at $111.50 a share on Nasdaq, about 34% above its $83 IPO price. Recommended Video Binance Wallet, the wallet tied to the crypto exchange, is already off to a rocky start. Minutes after the stock began trading, the platform said it hadn’t secured enough shares to fill customers’ orders. It said it would refund everyone who put up money and split the available tokens among eligible customers for free, based on how much each had committed. The announcement came a day after Binanced Wallet opened Anthropic-linked tokens at the company’s eventual IPO price, plus a 5% fee. Within hours, users had committed $500 million, hitting the campaign’s cap and prompting it to close early. Firms like Binance typically offer tokenized stocks by obtaining allocations of shares for themselves, which they hold in custody, and then issue tokens that serve as claims on the stock. Kraken also let eligible customers request Anthropic-linked tokens at the final IPO price plus 5%, without guaranteeing an allocation. Ondo, a tokenization platform, took a different approach. It said it would launch its token once Anthropic shares began trading on Nasdaq, giving buyers exposure at market prices rather than a shot at the IPO price. Other platforms, including Bitget and bStocks, also joined the rush. Tokenized stocks have gained momentum over the past year as crypto companies have used them to bring U.S. equities to investors abroad. They let buyers gain exposure to those stocks without owning shares directly and, on some platforms, trade outside regular market hours. That growth is part of a broader push to put traditional assets on blockchains. By September, the total value of tokenized real-world assets had topped $34 billion, according to a report by blockchain analytics platform Dune. Tokenized stocks grew fastest, rising more than 2,000% as the number of active holders surpassed 1 million. In an IPO, tokenized stocks can give buyers who might otherwise have to wait for public trading a chance to get in at the offering price. That can be a better deal if the stock opens higher, but it depends on whether the token provider secures enough shares to fill their orders. SpaceX’s IPO in June was an early stress test for tokenized IPO access, and several crypto platforms came up short. The company priced its IPO at $135 a share , with investors requesting more than four times as many shares as were on offer. The surge in demand left token providers scrambling for shares. Binance Wallet, for example, had taken requests from customers hoping to buy in at the IPO price, but its token provider couldn’t secure enough shares to fill those orders. Binance Wallet canceled the offering and refunded customers, who missed out on the opening jump when SpaceX began trading about 11% above its IPO price. records.title: Retail investor enthusiasm for Anthropic IPO to rival SpaceX debut
records.excerpt: Title: Retail investor enthusiasm for Anthropic IPO to rival SpaceX debut URL Source: http://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-retail-investors.html Final URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-retail-investors.html Published Time: 2026-11-18T14:03:41+0000 Markdown Content: ![Image 1: Anthropic's blockbuster IPO tests retail investors' appetite for AI](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108553384-261113_cg_33_anthropic_ipo_thumb_SITE.png?v=1794944506&w=750&h=422&vtcrop=y) watch now Retail investor Dan Shetty is so eager to get in on the [Anthropic](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/ANT/) initial public offering that he “drained” his Roth IRA and moved roughly $12,000 from Fidelity to [Robinhood](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/HOOD/) for a chance to participate. “I don’t want to tell my grandkids that I didn’t invest in Anthropic and I didn’t invest in OpenAI during the AI bubble,” he said. Shetty’s enthusiasm is shared by many, with excitement among small investors for the blockbuster IPO expected to be off the charts. Vanda Research estimates that Anthropic could see approximately $250 million of retail net buying when it starts trading Thursday, double the size of [SpaceX’s](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/SPCX/) IPO. “That would be far and away the largest amount of net retail buying of any stock that we’ve seen in our data on the first day of its listing,” Jai Malhi, senior strategist at Vanda, said in an interview with CNBC. The artificial intelligence laboratory — which will trade on the Nasdaq under ticker symbol ANT — is [selling 825 million shares](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/10/anthropic-sets-price-range-of-70-to-78-in-upcoming-ipo.html) at an expected price range of $70 to $78 per share in the IPO, though sources told CNBC the stock is likely to price [above that range](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/17/anthropic-ipo-price.html). Individual investors are expected to be allocated as much as 20% in that initial offering. And if Vanda’s figures prove correct, the buying enthusiasm will be big as regular trading begins. Founded less than six years ago, Anthropic aims to raise as much as $64.4 billion, giving it a valuation of $1.405 trillion. If demand is especially strong, Anthropic could even raise more than the [record $85.7 billion](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/15/spacex-ipo-spcx-greenshoe-overallotment.html) that SpaceX sold in its record IPO in June. The tech trade has been in turmoil since Jensen Huang’s departure last week as [Nvidia](https://www.cnbc.com/quotes/NVDA/) CEO [raised questions](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/13/nvidia-jensen-huang-resignation-ai-financing.html) about the future of AI financing. Before then, a potential [slowdown in data center development](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/ai-stocks-texas-governor-data-centers.html) resulting from Democratic victories in the 2026 midterm elections, and [signs of moderation](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/29/microsoft-google-ai-capex-estimates.html) in the capital expenditures boom, had already spooked investors. These all stand in marked contrast to the market backdrop in place at the time of the SpaceX IPO. In June, both positioning and sentiment were high, Malhi said. The Anthropic IPO could see a different dynamic, however. Demand could be strong across the entire investor spectrum given that sentiment is depressed, meaning that the bar to beat expectations is “much easier to overcome,” he explained. “What we’re seeing across both retail and institutional positioning is that there is plenty of dry powder to take part in this IPO,” the strategist said. ### ‘Pure-play AI leader’ For the 27-year-old New Yorker Shetty, who himself works at agentic data platform Data Workers, this is his first time vying to take part in an IPO. He said Anthropic’s emphasis on “safety first” drew his interest. “I’ve been telling all of my friends, ‘If you have like $5, you should invest it in this stock because this is the pure-play AI leader,’” Shetty said. “I think of my father who invested in Microsoft during the dotcom bubble, and he divested from that stock, and it was such a silly thing to do.” Not everyone agrees. Joe Pak, a former macro portfolio manager who is now an independent researcher outside London, is opting against participating in the Anthropic IPO for two reasons: the likelihood of limited allocation and current macroeconomic conditions. He believes the odds are probably stacked against retail investors when it comes to the allocation of shares. “It’s very difficult as a retail investor to actually get an allocation in these blockbuster IPOs,” the 36-year-old said. “You get maybe one share, and the base case is you don’t get any at all. So, it’s a bit of a catch-22. If you do get a lot of shares, it probably means that the institutional bid was weaker, and in that case, you don’t actually want the shares at that level.” In terms of the economy, conditions “need to be favorable” to hold a position in a stock like Anthropic, he said. But with the Federal Reserve having [raised interest rates in September](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/16/fed-rate-decision-september-2026.html) and widely expected to do so again next month, the backdrop could be darkening. > “From a price-to-sales ratio, Anthropic’s like a really good deal. ... [But] it’s still a massive valuation for a $1.4 trillion company, and there are significantly better deals out there if you are a fundamental investor.” > > > > Russ Faigen > > > Retail investor “The risk that you have is the financial conditions deteriorating” before the company starts to grow into anticipated profit and revenue, which would justify purchase of the stock, Pak said. While Pak is steering clear of the IPO, he did say that at a certain level, it would make sense to get into Anthropic. Other retail investors such as Bryan Nearnberg share Pak’s view. “I’m planning to eventually buy Anthropic, just not at the IPO price, considering when the lockups expire and there’s some selling pressure,” said the 37-year-old Westchester County, N.Y. resident, who works in finance operations. “We are not at the end of this short-term negative headline sentiment.” IPOs are a sore spot for Nearnberg, who hasn’t had much luck trading stocks on their opening day. His skepticism toward IPOs can be traced all the way back to when he was in college. “I didn’t get an allocation to the Facebook IPO, but I ended up buying it the first day of open. I got burned pretty quickly,” Nearnberg told CNBC. “Same thing with Zynga. I didn’t get an allocation, but [got] burned pretty quickly in terms of price.” As a result of those experiences, “I’m pretty sure we’ll see a good entry price underneath the IPO for Anthropic by Memorial Day next year,” Nearnberg said, citing sour sentiment toward technology and concern surrounding [circular financing](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/16/imf-georgieva-warning-ai-circular-financing.html) as short-term headwinds. ### Waiting game To be clear, all the retail investors CNBC spoke with are optimistic on AI as a transformative technology — even the ones sitting out the IPO. One trader said he believes in AI so much that he uses Anthropic’s Claude, a conversational AI assistant, every day. But Russ Faigen, a 27-year-old in Austin, Texas, is undecided on whether to subscribe for a piece of the IPO. “From a price-to-sales ratio, Anthropic’s like a really good deal,” Faigen said. But “it’s still a massive valuation for a $1.4 trillion company, and there are significantly better deals out there if you are a fundamental investor.” Faigen, who works for an agentic brokerage firm, said he’s “leaning towards patience,” as he believes Anthropic is going to be public “for a very long time.” “I just am not in a rush to get in on day one based off the valuation,” he told CNBC. Anthropic’s valuation depends on its ability to sustain its rapid growth. In the nine months through Sept. 30, revenue reached more than $33 billion, 1,200% above the year-earlier

Here's Why. Anthropic is expected to list on the Nasdaq on Nov. 19. By Adam Spatacco – Nov 17, 2026 at 3:00PM EST Key Points Anthropic is expected to go public this week in one of the largest IPOs of all time. Many investors expect big tech to be the most direct beneficiaries of a successful Anthropic offering. SpaceX could emerge as the quiet winner of Anthropic's IPO thanks to a growing tie-up between the two companies. 10 stocks we like better than Space Exploration Technologies › Anthropic is preparing for what is expected to be one of the largest initial public offerings (IPO) of all time. The company behind the Claude chatbot is expected to price its IPO on Wednesday, Nov. 18, before beginning trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market on Thursday, Nov. 19. Much of the attention around Anthropic's IPO has focused on Amazon and Alphabet , two companies with meaningful financial and strategic relationships with the AI developer. However, I see Space Exploration Technologies ( SPCX -3.53% ) emerging as an unexpected winner of Anthropic's public debut. A closer examination of Anthropic's S-1 filing reveals that its relationship with SpaceX is much larger than previously thought. This potentially creates an overlooked catalyst for Elon Musk's aerospace and AI infrastructure company. SPCX - Space Exploration Technologies $138.43 -$5.07 (-3.53%) NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/19/26 Key data points Market cap Market cap calculated using publicly traded shares outstanding only. Does not include unlisted, private, or dual-class non-traded shares. Implied market cap may vary. $1.88T Day's range $135.50 - $147.29 52wk range $104.83 - $225.64 Volume 1.3M Avg volume 95.4M Anthropic's IPO could reignite enthusiasm for AI stocks Anthropic's public debut will be an important test of Wall Street's appetite for AI stocks. The offering comes during a period of heightened volatility among technology stocks. Amazon and Alphabet are obvious candidates to benefit from Anthropic's IPO because both companies have invested heavily in the start-up and provide cloud computing infrastructure to Anthropic's models. An enthusiastic reception could increase the market value of their respective Anthropic positions while reinforcing investor confidence in their AI road maps. SpaceX presents a different opportunity. Following its IPO back in June, SpaceX has increasingly positioned itself as a diversified technology company spanning reusable rockets, satellite connectivity, and AI infrastructure. Anthropic's upcoming listing could draw renewed attention to the scale of SpaceX's computing business, particularly as investors scrutinize the AI developer's spending commitments . Image source: Getty Images. Anthropic's filings reveal a massive agreement with SpaceX A few months ago, SpaceX disclosed that Anthropic had agreed to pay $1.25 billion per month for access to computing capacity across its Colossus I supercomputer. The arrangements involved access to 220,000 Nvidia GPUs, with payments scheduled through May 2029. At the full monthly rate, this deal represented $15 billion in annualized revenue potential for SpaceX. However, Anthropic's amended S-1 paints a much different picture. Between May and October, Anthropic entered into an amended agreement with SpaceX.AI, a subsidiary of SpaceX. According to the filing, Anthropic agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion on SpaceX computing services through 2029, with aggregate monthly payments reaching about $3.1 billion once the expanded capacity is fully scaled. This represents an annualized revenue of approximately $37.2 billion, nearly 2.5 times the previously disclosed amount. Anthropic expects the additional compute to be delivered by December, suggesting the expanded arrangement could begin contributing to SpaceX's revenue in the near future. Importantly, this agreement demonstrates that SpaceX is swiftly becoming a meaningful supplier of AI compute to major frontier labs rather than relying exclusively on its own AI applications such as Grok. Why SpaceX stock could surge after the Anthropic IPO The interesting aspect of Anthropic's relationship with SpaceX is that investors may not fully appreciate its significance. Although the original agreement was publicly disclosed, the new, larger arrangement appeared within Anthropic's lengthy IPO registration statement. It's highly likely that most investors haven't yet accounted for the expanded economics in their expectations for SpaceX's AI infrastructure business. I think Anthropic's IPO will change that. As analysts pour over the company's financial statements, computing obligations, and infrastructure partners, SpaceX's role may receive substantially more attention after Thursday. As such, this could strengthen the argument that SpaceX is quietly evolving into a new kind of hyperscaler , capable of serving external AI developers alongside its aerospace, satellite, and proprietary AI applications. In my eyes, Anthropic's IPO could become an unexpected catalyst for SpaceX stock if investors begin to assign greater value to its fast-growing AI infrastructure segment. The difference between the originally disclosed agreement and the expanded contract is too meaningful to overlook. If Anthropic's IPO brings that relationship into sharper focus, SpaceX could easily attract renewed investor enthusiasm as one of the AI industry's increasingly important infrastructure providers. records.excerpt: Title: Anthropic's $81.3 billion IPO shatters SpaceX's record as rising rates and political headwinds shake the sector URL Source: http://the-decoder.com/anthropics-81-3-billion-ipo-shatters-spacexs-record-as-rising-rates-and-political-headwinds-shake-the-sector/ Final URL: https://the-decoder.com/anthropics-81-3-billion-ipo-shatters-spacexs-record-as-rising-rates-and-political-headwinds-shake-the-sector/ Published Time: 2026-11-19T14:02:22+00:00 Markdown Content: **Claude developer Anthropic has surpassed SpaceX's previous record IPO. While tech giants are pouring in billions, a key early investor is warning about the consequences of an unchecked AI race.** [Anthropic priced its IPO](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-prices-initial-public-offering) at $83 per share, beating the original target range of $70 to $78. Overwhelming demand pushed the public benefit corporation and its seven co-founders to sell roughly 980 million Class A common shares, up from a planned 825 million. The offering raised $81.3 billion, according to a [CNBC report](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/18/anthropic-ipo-ai-offering-price.html), overtaking the previous record set by Elon Musk's SpaceX, which raised $75 billion in June. Anthropic's fully diluted market cap stands at about $1.5 trillion, while its market value excluding stock options sits closer to $1 trillion, [according to the Wall Street Journal](https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/anthropic-prices-ipo-at-83-a-share-0290494c). Shares begin trading Thursday on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT." The underwriting syndicate, including Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, also received a 30-day option to purchase an additional 147 million shares. Each of the seven co-founders is selling 3.38 million shares for a combined $1.96 billion, none of which flows to Anthropic itself. ## Claude Code sends revenue soaring as losses climb into the billions Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers led by CEO Dario Amodei, Anthropic saw explosive growth in its enterprise business in 2026, fueled by the coding tool Claude Code. Revenue surged about 1,200 percent year over year to $33.24 billion in the first nine months through September 30. By the end of October, annualized revenue had already reached roughly $81 billion. Net losses for the same nine-month period widened from $25.1 billion a year earlier to $104 billion, driven primarily by revaluations of convertible notes and derivative liabilities. Amazon and Google rank among the largest shareholders, each holding stakes worth more than $100 billion. Together with Microsoft, Nvidia, and AMD, these tech giants are investing another $26 billion at the offering price. They also sell Anthropic expensive hardware, counting the company as a customer. The IPO amounts to a stress test for the AI industry, which has recently been rattled by rising interest rates for data center developers, political headwinds from the U.S. midterm elections, and the ousting of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang last week. Anthropic itself clashed with the U.S. government twice this year over safety issues and lists risk factors across more than 90 pages in its prospectus. Rival OpenAI, meanwhile, has confidentially filed for an IPO planned for 2027. ## Early investor Dustin Moskovitz warns of an unchecked AI race Amodei said in a roadshow video that the technology could usher in an age of wonders with careful risk management, but one of Anthropic's most important early investors disagrees. Facebook co-founder Dustin Moskovitz is sharply distancing himself from the IPO, as the [New York Times reported](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/19/business/anthropic-ipo-dustin-moskovitz.html). Moskovitz invested between $15 million and $25 million in Anthropic's first funding round in 2021, after turning away from OpenAI. His goal was to help build a safety-focused research lab. On Bluesky, however, the former board observer called the IPO problematic and pointed to recent incidents in which AI agents coordinated cyberattacks on their own outside controlled environments. His funding of Anthropic "might well be an action that ended the world," Moskovitz wrote. "Cari and I invested in Anthropic to promote safety, not racing," Moskovitz told the newspaper, referring to his wife Cari Tuna. To avoid personally profiting from the IPO, the couple transferred their multibillion-dollar stake to a nonprofit organization in early 2025. Dario and Daniela Amodei have not spoken with Moskovitz in more than a year, according to the Times' sources. ### AI News Without the Hype – Curated by Humans Subscribe to THE DECODER for ad-free reading, a weekly AI newsletter, our exclusive "AI Radar" frontier report six times a year, full archive access, and access to our comment section. [Subscribe now](https://the-decoder.com/subscription/)

records.excerpt: Title: Anthropic vs SpaceX: Which Mega IPO Won The 2026 Stock Market Battle? URL Source: http://www.ndtv.com/business-news/anthropic-vs-spacex-ipo-which-stock-debut-won-2026-share-market-battle-12353637 Final URL: https://www.ndtv.com/business-news/anthropic-vs-spacex-ipo-which-stock-debut-won-2026-share-market-battle-12353637 Published Time: 2026-11-20T14:17:11+05:30 Markdown Content: **Share Market News:** The world's biggest stock market debut of 2026 has delivered a new winner. But when it comes to the stock market performance, the battle between Anthropic and SpaceX is far from one-sided. Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence (AI) chatbot, has overtaken Elon Musk's SpaceX to claim the title of the largest initial public offering (IPO) in history. Its blockbuster listing raised $81.3 billion, beating the $75 billion raised by SpaceX in June. However, the size of an IPO is only one way to measure its success. The price at which shares begin trading, the valuation investors are willing to pay and how the stock performs after listing tell a different story. **Also Read | [Layoffs Are Rising In Tech, But These Skills Are Helping People Unlock Better Pay](https://www.ndtvlaunchpad.com/course/job-bootcamp-data-analytics/3wtn25wla2v31u3evaj9?pfrom=business_article)** And on some of these measures, SpaceX still has reason to celebrate. ### **Anthropic vs SpaceX: The IPO numbers** Anthropic priced its shares at $83 apiece on November 18, above its initial price range of $70-$78. The company offered around 980 million shares, raising approximately $81.3 billion. The offering could increase to $93.5 billion if the overallotment option is fully exercised. [Anthropic also raised](https://www.ndtv.com/business-news/anthropic-ipo-raises-81-3-billion-stock-soars-then-slips-what-comes-next-12352190) another $26 billion through a private placement of shares. SpaceX, meanwhile, raised $75 billion through its June IPO by offering approximately 555.6 million shares at $135 apiece. Its total fundraising reached around $86 billion after including the overallotment option. That puts Anthropic ahead on the amount raised through its public offering, although the final figures depend on the exercise of additional share options. ### **Anthropic vs SpaceX: Share Price And Market Debut** Anthropic also had the stronger opening when its shares started trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. The stock opened at $111.50, a 34.3 per cent premium over its IPO price of $83. SpaceX, which listed at $135 in June, began trading at $150, an 11.1 per cent premium. But the initial excitement around Anthropic did not last throughout the trading session. The stock briefly climbed to $114.99 before slipping below $100. It eventually closed its first day at $97.17, up around 17 per cent from its IPO price. SpaceX had a relatively stronger [first-day trading performance](https://www.ndtv.com/business-news/anthropic-ipo-mints-millionaires-what-workers-plan-to-do-with-their-wealth-12352639). Its shares touched $176.52 during the first two hours of trading, gaining 17.7 per cent from their opening price of $150. The stock eventually closed at $160.95. The Motley Fool highlighted this difference in its comparison of the two listings. While Anthropic won on the size of the IPO and the initial listing premium, SpaceX performed better on the first-day trading measure. ![Image 1: Latest and Breaking News on NDTV](https://c.ndtvimg.com/2026-11/6bldofos_chart_625x300_20_November_26.png) ### **Valuation: Anthropic Briefly Crossed The $2 Trillion Mark** Anthropic's opening share price of $111.50 implied a valuation of around $1.5 trillion based on its outstanding shares. However, its fully diluted valuation, which also accounts for employee stock options, restricted stock units and convertible securities, reached approximately $2 trillion. SpaceX's debut valuation was estimated at around $1.95 trillion on a comparable fully diluted basis. This put the two companies almost neck and neck in the valuation race. Anthropic's first-day closing price of $97.17 brought its market capitalisation down from the initial peak. Reuters estimated its fully diluted valuation at around $1.75 trillion at the close. The distinction between market capitalisation and fully [diluted valuation](https://www.ndtv.com/business-news/anthropic-ipo-raises-81-3-billion-stock-soars-then-slips-what-comes-next-12352190) is important. The latter includes shares that could enter the market in the future, while the former generally reflects shares currently outstanding. ### **Anthropic's AI Business Versus SpaceX's Diversified Operations** Anthropic is essentially an AI business. Its Claude family of models is the centre of its operations, with products such as Claude Code helping it attract enterprise customers. SpaceX, on the other hand, operates across several areas, including rocket launches, satellite internet through Starlink and AI through its association with xAI. Reuters' analysis of company disclosures showed that AI accounted for virtually all of Anthropic's estimated second-quarter 2026 revenue. For SpaceX, AI represented less than half of its revenue. This makes Anthropic a relatively direct bet on the commercial adoption of [generative AI](https://www.ndtv.com/business-news/anthropic-ipo-how-much-dario-amodei-6-other-founders-stand-to-earn-12347529?pfrom=home-ndtv_topscroll_Imagetopscroll). The company's growth has been striking. Its revenue increased twelvefold in 2025 to nearly $4.6 billion. The momentum continued in 2026. Revenue reached $16.96 billion in the third quarter, a 47 per cent increase from the previous quarter. However, there is a catch. Anthropic is spending heavily to keep up with demand. It spent nearly $9 billion on computing capacity and infrastructure in the first half of 2026, almost four times the amount spent during the corresponding period last year. It also has nearly $900 billion in computing commitments with infrastructure partners, including Amazon and Google. The company's third-quarter operating loss stood at $567 million, compared with an operating profit of $974 million in the preceding quarter. This raises a critical question for investors: Can Anthropic turn its explosive revenue growth into sustainable profits while continuing to spend heavily on computing infrastructure? ### **What Makes Anthropic's IPO Important For AI Industry?** Anthropic's listing is significant beyond the money it has raised. It is the first major frontier AI model developer to enter the public markets. Its stock will give investors a direct way to participate in the business of developing and commercialising advanced AI models. Until now, much of the AI investment opportunity has been available through chipmakers, cloud companies and other businesses supplying the technology's infrastructure. Anthropic's listing could also offer a valuation benchmark for other AI companies preparing to go public, including rival OpenAI. But investors are not ignoring the risks. The [AI industry](https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/musk-no-longer-a-trillionaire-what-went-wrong-with-spacex-ipo-11736472) faces questions about the enormous cost of developing advanced models, the availability of computing infrastructure and whether businesses will generate enough revenue to justify their investments. There are also concerns about competition. Anthropic must continue investing in its models while competing with OpenAI, Google, Meta and other technology companies. ### **Anthropic vs SpaceX: Who Won The IPO Battle?** On the amount raised, Anthropic has taken the crown. It also delivered a bigger opening premium than SpaceX. But SpaceX had a stronger first-day trading trajectory, with its shares maintaining momentum after listing. records.excerpt: Retail investors traded $772 million in Anthropic shares on its Nasdaq debut Thursday, but their net purchases totaled just $60 million, about half the $118 million they put into SpaceX on its first day of trading in June.Anthropic’s first-day retail trading volume topped SpaceX’s $669 million and… Anthropic’s $81B IPO draws half the net retail buying of SpaceX’s Less than 1 min read ANT SPCX Retail investors traded $772 million in Anthropic shares on its Nasdaq debut Thursday, but their net purchases totaled just $60 million, about half the $118 million they put into SpaceX on its first day of trading in June. Anthropic’s first-day retail trading volume topped SpaceX’s $669 million and was the highest for any market debut in Vanda Research’s data, which go back to 2012, Yahoo Finance reported. Volume counts both purchases and sales, while net buying measures how much purchases exceeded sales. The Claude AI developer and its existing shareholders offered 980 million shares at $83 each in the $81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO). Anthropic shares opened on Nasdaq at $111.50 on Thursday, 34.3% above the IPO price, and closed at $97.17 for a first-day gain of 17.1%. SpaceX shares gained 19.2% in their June 12 debut, closing at $160.95 against an IPO price of $135, according to Nasdaq. Although Anthropic’s base offering exceeded SpaceX’s initial $75 billion sale, SpaceX ultimately raised $85.7 billion after underwriters exercised their option to purchase additional shares. Before the IPO, Vanda forecast about $250 million in net retail buying, more than four times Thursday’s total. Its forecast drew on retail trading in past market debuts and the volume of Anthropic perpetual futures traded on decentralized exchange Hyperliquid. Shortly before Nasdaq trading began, those futures traded at $110.48, just 0.9% below the stock’s opening price. Cointelegraph IPOs US stocks Read more from Cointelegraph More news from Cointelegraph

(Joel Saget/AFP/Getty Images/TNS) Joel Saget Facebook Twitter WhatsApp SMS Email Print Save (TNS) – Anthropic PBC and its seven co-founders have raised $107.3 billion in an upsized IPO and private placement, becoming the first frontier AI lab tapping the public markets to fund its development of thinking machines. The artificial intelligence firm sold 956.4 million shares and the co-founders sold 23.6 million shares for $83 each, according to a statement Wednesday confirming an earlier Bloomberg News report, above the marketed range. The company had marketed 801.4 million shares, while the co-founders offered 23.6 million shares, in a range of $70 to $78 each, according to its filings. The offering also includes a $26 billion private placement listed in Anthropic’s filings, with firms including Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Microsoft Corp. participating. Anthropic’s IPO is the biggest of all time even without the placement, with the $81.3 billion base deal topping SpaceX’s at $75 billion. Pricing the shares above the range gives the company a fully diluted valuation of roughly $1.5 trillion. Anthropic’s debut marks a watershed moment for AI, signaling that investors have begun to expand their focus from primarily backing chipmakers and other infrastructure providers to the makers of platforms such as Claude as they weave themselves into the fabric of business, academia, government and healthcare. Soaring Demand Demand for the IPO soared, nearing seven times the number of orders for the shares available, Bloomberg News reported Sunday. Buyers from Wall Street to London to Tokyo clamored for a slice of a stock that’s expected to quickly join indexes such as the Nasdaq 100 after it begins trading Thursday. Bankers told prospective investors that existing backers would be prioritized by Anthropic, and some would-be buyers would receive smaller allocations than they expect, people familiar with the matter have said. Some investors are offering a portion of their Anthropic IPO allocation to other prospective backers, letting them collect additional fees and reduce their risk before trading begins, while others with pre-IPO stakes are marketing them to buyers via special purpose vehicles. Anthropic’s IPO puts it among the 15 largest publicly traded companies by market value, neck and neck with Tesla Inc. but ahead of Eli Lilly & Co., according to data compiled by Bloomberg. The valuation is below the $2 trillion floated months ago but well above $1.1 trillion that some on Wall Street suggested in the depths of the recent selloff in tech stocks. Anthropic’s listing is the first ever by a frontier AI lab, a cohort of firms building the most advanced models that are intended to tackle difficult problems and assist users in complex tasks such as software design, legal work and scientific discovery. The debut puts the company firmly ahead of rival OpenAI, which isn’t planning to go public before 2027. The stock market didn’t offer a supportive setting for the Claude chatbot maker’s debut, with the Nasdaq 100 Index down 4.4% over the past week through Wednesday’s close. Nvidia Corp. extended a losing streak to a fifth day, sinking 2.9% during regular trading, a day after the chipmaker reported earnings that beat expectations. It is set to buy $10 billion of Anthropic stock as part of the private placement, the filings show. “We’re not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day, or what market conditions we go public into,” Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei told JPMorgan Chase & Co. CEO Jamie Dimon at an event last Friday. He said the best piece of advice he’s gotten throughout the process is, “Never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it’s really worth.” The debut is set to enhance the personal fortunes of the co-founders, including Amodei, as well as many of Anthropic’s employees. It will also juice returns for its venture capital backers, including Iconiq, Coatue Management and Spark Capital, which has a seat on the board. Goldman Sachs Group Inc. and Morgan Stanley led Anthropic’s IPO, with participation from 20 other banks, the filing shows. The stock is expected to trade Thursday on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol ANT. records.title: No invite for China at Anthropic IPO: After SpaceX, Claude parent too shuts Chinese investors out
records.excerpt: Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one! Everyone wants a slice of the AI bigfoot, but where you come from could decide whether you get one!Earlier billionaire Elon Musk's AI and aerospace giant SpaceX barred investors from Hong Kong and mainland China from buying its shares. Now, Anthropic followed a similar route. While the IPO was open only to investors from selected countries, the repeated exclusion of Chinese investors by major US technology companies raises questions.The artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot reportedly turned away investment from Chinese and Hong Kong firms ahead of its public listing, in what went on to record as the biggest initial public offering (IPO) in history.Three people familiar with the decision said Anthropic had excluded investors from the two regions, New York Times reported.The move comes amid growing US efforts to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence technology. As Washington and Beijing compete for supremacy in AI, technology and investment are increasingly becoming flashpoints in their already strained relationship.Why keep Chinese investors at arm's length?The exclusion comes against the backdrop of a growing technology rivalry between the US and China. The Trump administration has been taking steps to restrict China's access to advanced AI technology, while both countries are drawing red lines around their homegrown technologies.Anthropic's decision appears in line with a wider trend among major American technology companies. SpaceX and its bankers had taken a similar step ahead of the company's blockbuster IPO in July, shutting Chinese investors out of the offering.OpenAI, another leading AI company, is also expected to bar Chinese investors from its eventual public listing. It has already prevented investors from China from participating in its private fund-raising rounds.There is another common thread connecting all three companies: Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI have all counted the US government among their clients.Trump and Xi may be talking, but technology remains a sticking pointThe decision also comes at an interesting moment in US-China relations. US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping met on Thursday at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen, China, with both leaders looking to bring some stability and goodwill into an increasingly rocky economic relationship.During the meeting, Xi called on members to build an "open ecosystem" for technology. Yet, while the two leaders are attempting to improve ties, their governments continue to build barriers around trade, technology and capital.The latest developments around AI chips underline just how difficult that balancing act is. Hours before Trump arrived in Asia for meetings with regional leaders, his administration moved to restrict China's access to advanced artificial intelligence chips.Beijing was quick to warn that it could respond with countermeasures if Washington continued with the restrictions."If the US persists, China will take countermeasures," China warned.A spokesman for China's Ministry of Commerce also expressed strong opposition to the latest US measures on Thursday."China is deeply concerned about — and firmly opposes — a series of recent economic and trade restrictive measures taken by the US against China," the spokesman told NYT.The latest restrictions on artificial intelligence are adding to a series of escalating moves by both countries. China experts have warned that the new AI rule could make it harder for Trump and Xi to reach any meaningful agreement to ease tensions.Money habits form by age 7. records.title: In Historic IPO Debut, Anthropic Surpasses Elon Musk's SpaceX Launch
records.excerpt: Crime & Safety In Historic IPO Debut, Anthropic Surpasses Elon Musk's SpaceX Launch The company began trading Thursday at $111.50 a share, more than 30% above the original public offering price. Fernando Haro , Patch Staff Posted Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 10:27 am PT | Updated Thu, Nov 19, 2026 at 10:59 am PT Dario Amodei, co-founder and CEO of Anthropic, right, and Daniela Amodei, co-founder and president, left, react during the opening bell ceremony at Nasdaq MarketSite as part of the Anthropic IPO in New York, Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig) SAN FRANCISCO, CA — When Anthropic announced it would go public earlier this month, critics were skeptical, investors were nervous, and the AI bubble teetered as the industry was plagued by scandals involving honeypotting Chinese spies. But those concerns seemingly went out the window Thursday when the San Francisco-based company and Claude chatbot-makers made a historic debut on the Nasdaq, surpassing Elon Musk's SpaceX launch in June. "It’s a big win for the tech sector after a white-knuckle time with Nvidia," said Dan Ives, a financial analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co. "The pricing shows strong demand among investors." Find out what's happening in San Francisco for free with the latest updates from Patch. By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . Anthropic had earlier set a much lower price range between $70 and $78 per share, one that experts predicted would rival SpaceX's opening. When SpaceX opened in June, shares were priced at $150. It jumped to $161 per share at the open, and the company raised $75 billion. It also raised the company's value to $2 trillion. Find out what's happening in San Francisco for free with the latest updates from Patch. By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . Just a day before opening, Anthropic announced its updated initial public offering at $83. But on Thursday, Anthropic shares began trading at $111.50, spiking more than 30% above the initial public offering price. With 980 million shares offered, Anthropic raised $81 billion, surpassing Musk's SpaceX launch. A big test remains: whether investors maintain the classic “IPO pop” by keeping the stock aloft on its first day — or if it will tumble by the close. Despite a record-breaking opening, Anthropic still faces big financial challenges ahead. Anthropic already has taken on $6.2 billion in debt, which it acknowledges in financial filings is “substantial.” Adding to the strain, the company is unprofitable, at least under standard accounting rules, suggesting that its resources to pay interest and principal are limited. While the company has ample cash for now , it will likely run through it quickly if it cannot raise more soon, given its outsize spending plans. The company said it has already signed leases and other deals requiring it to spend $900 billion on computing power and infrastructure in the coming years, including $70 billion in the next 12 months. An IPO is essentially a way to raise money, instead of going into further debt. And borrowing has gotten more expensive. That’s partly due to inflation fears and partly due to the sector’s massive cash needs, which have drawn comparisons to the Gilded Age splurge on railroads. Lenders fear that AI companies have taken on too much debt to expand while having no clear path to profitability. Anthropic's IPO also means its employees can begin to sell their vested stock, a payout that will make many of them millionaires. The IPO could also give Anthropic enormous resources to accelerate its expansion and potentially add billions of dollars to the fortunes of CEO Dario Amodei and his sister and co-founder, Daniela Amodei. There's also growing concern over industry regulations and the ongoing fight for dominance against other competitors, including Google. Dario Amodei cautioned in September that the AI industry should slow its fast-moving development to give safety measures time to catch up. Without such a slowdown, Amodei warned, AI could be capable of letting loose a swarm of agents that could take over the internet within months. In comments at the opening bell Thursday, Amodei sought to dampen fears by stressing a commitment to ensure humans are in control of the technology. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same," he said. "The goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.” More California News: Planes Land Without Air Traffic Controllers At CA Airport: Report Nationwide Emergency Alert Test Today: What To Know In California Video Captures Waterspout Over Stormy San Francisco: Report CA Aerospace Firm Wins NASA Moon Base Contracts NorCal Faces Tornado Threat As Storm Rages, Weather Service Warns Major Bank Outages Disrupt Accounts, Transactions Across CA 2 More CA Amusement Parks To Close — How Many Are Left? AP reporters Bernard Condo and Barbara Ortutay contributed to this story.

records.title: Trump's accounts bought shares of Palantir and SpaceX near federal contract awards
records.excerpt: Trump accounts bought Palantir, SpaceX shares near contract awards Subscribe Markets Trump's accounts bought shares of Palantir and SpaceX near federal contract awards The September disclosure lists Nvidia trades as well; the White House says independent managers make all investment decisions By Cris Tolomia · 2 min read · Updated November 19, 2026 Add QZ to Google President Donald Trump outside the White House. (Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images) President Donald Trump's investment accounts reported purchases of shares of Palantir $PLTR and SpaceX in September, in the weeks around federal contract awards to both companies, according to a disclosure released Thursday. The filing lists Palantir purchases of $15,001 to $50,000 on Sept. 2 and $1,001 to $15,000 on Sept. 9. The Department of Housing and Urban Development awarded Palantir a $10.4 million delivery order that started Sept. 16, according to USAspending.gov. The order covers an AI-powered grant intelligence platform. On Sept. 29, the Department of Homeland Security awarded Palantir a $32.1 million software license contract . Palantir CEO Alex Karp took part on Sept. 29 in a White House session on artificial intelligence, alongside Trump, Elon Musk, Nvidia $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang and several other tech industry leaders, according to CNBC . For SpaceX, the filing shows purchases of $1,001 to $15,000 on Sept. 9 and $15,001 to $50,000 on Sept. 24. The accounts also bought $100,001 to $250,000 in SpaceX debt on Sept. 1, according to CNBC. NASA said on Sept. 18 that it was extending its SpaceX deal by $946 million, which pays for three more crewed flights to the International Space Station and lifts the contract’s overall worth to $5.92 billion, according to CNBC. The filing shows four Nvidia purchases totaling $152,004 to $380,000, including two on Sept. 2 worth as much as $350,000 combined, according to CNBC. The others were purchases of $1,001 to $15,000 on Sept. 9 and Sept. 10. The accounts also sold $1,001 to $15,000 in Nvidia shares on Sept. 24, the day Huang attended Trump’s state dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping, CNBC said. Reuters put the September Nvidia purchases at as much as $265,000. The filing reports values in ranges, so exact amounts are unclear, according to both outlets. CNBC said the trades push the number of Trump’s Nvidia transactions since early 2025 to a minimum of 108. Huang resigned as Nvidia 's CEO on Nov. 12 after reports of two extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of intelligence ties to Beijing. CNBC's analysis of the 25-page filing tallied 751 trades, both buys and sells, with a combined value of about $40.9 million to $148.1 million. White House spokesman Davis Ingle said independent managers run Trump's portfolio, and that the president and his family have no say over trades. "All investment decisions are made entirely by independent managers," Ingle told CNBC. CNBC said it found nothing showing that Trump directed the transactions, or that his managers had advance knowledge of government decisions. records.title: Bitcoin Below $62K After Anthropic IPO: Could a SpaceX-Style Crash Follow?
records.excerpt: For traders wondering why crypto is down, the much-anticipated “post-ANT” rebound has turned into another disappointment. Bitcoin’s anticipated post-Anthropic IPO rally has yet to materialize. Instead, BTC slipped below $62,000 on Thursday, November 19, as US stocks fell roughly 2% on the same day t... For traders wondering why crypto is down, the much-anticipated “post-ANT” rebound has turned into another disappointment. Bitcoin’s anticipated post-Anthropic IPO rally has yet to materialize. Instead, BTC slipped below $62,000 on Thursday, November 19, as US stocks fell roughly 2% on the same day the AI company made its Nasdaq debut. Bitcoin closed at $61,987, marking its first daily close below $62,300 since July 8, before sliding further to around $61,800 on Friday morning. BREAKING: MicroStrategy, $MSTR , and Bitmine, $BMNR , extend losses to their lowest level of the day as Bitcoin falls below $63,000. The stocks are now down -88% and -91%, respectively, from their record highs. pic.twitter.com/BgxojZPDps — The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 19, 2026 Anthropic itself had a strong but messy first day. Priced at $83 a share, it opened at $111.50, then faded to close at $97.17. The S&P 500 lost 2.0% and the Nasdaq Composite 2.3%, after the Nasdaq had opened higher. SpaceX’s June listing is the closest comparison. We tracked Bitcoin’s path after that IPO day by day: it kept falling for almost three weeks before it bottomed. So could Bitcoin repeat the SpaceX pattern, and when would the bottom come? Stocks Drop 2% on Anthropic’s Debut: Why Is Crypto Down? The listing was supposed to end the pressure. Bitcoin fell 22.7% in the 24 days before Anthropic’s debut, as traders sold crypto and other risky bets to make room for a mega-listing. Some, including Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse, expected that selling to stop once the shares started trading. Instead, Thursday turned into a broad sell-off: Stocks: the Dow lost about 1,100 points, and the S&P 500 posted its sixth straight daily loss. Coverage pointed to doubts about how long the AI spending boom can last. Anthropic: the stock still closed 17% above its $83 offering price , but 13% below where it opened. Buyers who chased the open were sitting on losses by the close. Bitcoin: down 1.7% on the day, with a low of $61,428, and a new low of $61,291 on Friday. When tech stocks fall this hard, Bitcoin usually falls with them. That link is the simplest answer to why is crypto down this week. Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl After SpaceX Listed, Bitcoin Bottomed 19 Days Later SpaceX listed on June 12. We lined up Bitcoin’s daily closes from 24 days before that day to 80 days after, and did the same for Anthropic. Before the listing: Bitcoin fell 17% in the 24 days before SpaceX, and 23% before Anthropic. The run-up looks very similar. The first days: after SpaceX, Bitcoin bounced 4% by day three, helped by a stock rally. The S&P 500 rose 1.7% on the next trading day. This time, there was no bounce. The bottom: Bitcoin kept sliding after the SpaceX bounce. It hit $57,800 on July 1, 19 days after the listing and 9% below its listing-day close. The recovery: Bitcoin was back at its listing-day level by day 23. It then moved sideways for about six weeks before a sharp rally in mid-August took it 24% higher by day 75. So far, Anthropic is following the SpaceX script with one difference: it skipped the early bounce. EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Tumbles 19% Ahead of Anthropic IPO: Is SpaceX Crash Repeating? Why Is Crypto Down and Could Bitcoin Repeat the SpaceX Pattern? Two listings are not a rule, and the backdrop has changed since June. For anyone asking why is crypto down and when it stops, here’s what lines up and what doesn’t. This is what matches: The pre-IPO slide: both listings came after a fall of about 20% in Bitcoin, as investors made room for a mega-listing. The timing: after SpaceX, the bottom came about three weeks after listing day. The same timing now would point to around December 8. What’s different: Stocks are weaker: after SpaceX, stocks rallied. This time, the S&P 500 has fallen six days in a row, and AI stocks are leading the drop. Rates: traders expect another Federal Reserve rate hike in December, which tends to hurt Bitcoin and tech stocks alike. The starting point: Bitcoin is already below the $62,300 floor it had held since February. If the SpaceX pattern holds, the worst could come in early December, followed by weeks of sideways trading. If stocks keep falling, the bottom could come sooner and lower. Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar Bitcoin Price Analysis: $62,300 Turns Into Resistance On the daily chart, Bitcoin trades at $61,865. That is below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $74,655, and its 200-day EMA at $75,470. Resistance: $62,300, the floor Bitcoin held in June, July, August, and twice this month, now acting as a ceiling. Above that, $65,500. Support: $58,500, where Bitcoin turned in early and late June and again on July 1, after the SpaceX listing. BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView Outlook Trigger Level to watch Rebound A daily close back above $62,300 $65,500, the June-August ceiling Holding pattern Price stays between $58,500 and $62,300 A range like the one after SpaceX Sell-off A daily close below $58,500 $57,800, the July 1 low, then lower The next few weeks will show whether the SpaceX pattern holds, and the answer to why is crypto down may come from stocks more than from crypto. A bottom near $58,500 in early December, with stocks steadying, would look a lot like June. A break below $57,800 while stocks keep falling would mean this sell-off is bigger than one IPO. next The post Bitcoin Below $62K After Anthropic IPO: Is a SpaceX Style Crash Coming? appeared first on Coinspeaker .

records.excerpt: Bigger than SpaceX: Anthropic's massive IPO by the numbers - News | InDaily, Inside South Australia News Business Opinion In Depth Events Quiz Donate Subscribe News Business Opinion In Depth Events Quiz Donate Subscribe In Depth Bigger than SpaceX: Anthropic’s massive IPO by the numbers Anthropic has broken all records for money raised on Wall Street, with a price tag on its shares was enough to put the value of the San Francisco company well beyond $US1 trillion. A AAP Nov 20, 2026, updated Nov 20, 2026 Anthropic's IPO was the biggest Wall Street debit ever, with an initial valuation of $US1.5 trillion. Anthropic has made a superlative-filled debut, breaking all records for money raised on Wall Street as it became the first major artificial intelligence lab to become a publicly traded company. The price tag on its shares was enough to put the value of the San Francisco company well beyond $US1 trillion ($A1.5 trillion). That kind of number was once unheard of for a company’s first moments trading on the stock market. But an acceleration in corporate wealth — and most recently the artificial intelligence boom — has changed that. Anthropic is the second business to debut with a value over a trillion dollars (following SpaceX just months ago), and will join a handful of other tech giants that measure their wealth by figures reaching 13 digits. Time will tell how Anthropic ultimately fares on the public market. The Claude maker decided to proceed with its IPO despite jitters among some investors over market volatility, fears of a possible AI bubble and growing unease among the public about the technology’s risks overall. Experts unpick Malinauskas and the Cool Britannia playbook Here are some numbers to help understand Thursday’s IPO. The amount in proceeds raised by the offering: $US81 billion ($A121 billion). That makes Anthropic’s debut the biggest ever. Ahead of trading on Thursday, it offered 980 million shares priced at $US83 ($A124) each, putting Anthropic ahead of Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which set a previous record with its IPO proceeds of about $US75 billion ($A112 billion) in June. The next biggest IPO hauls went to South Korean chipmaker SK Hynix ($US26.5 billion [$A39.7 billion] in July) and oil giant Saudi Aramco ($US25.6 billion [$A38.3 billion] in 2019). Stay informed, daily Anthropic’s initial valuation: $US1.5 trillion ($A2.2 trillion). The initial price per share was set at $US83 ($A124). But in early trading, that spiked more than 30 per cent — to $US111.50 ($A166.95) a share — pushing the company’s total valuation by half a trillion dollars to $US2.01 trillion ($A3.01 trillion) just before noon US Eastern Time. By market close on Thursday, Anthropic finished its first trading day at $US97.17 ($A145.49) per share. That’s still more than 17 per cent higher than its initial public offering price. In June, SpaceX ended its first day of trading on the public market with a valuation of $US2.1 trillion ($A3.1 trillion). Its market cap has since fallen to closer to $US1.95 trillion ($A2.92 trillion). Number of public companies that have reached the trillion-dollar club in the S&P 500: 11 Apple currently leads the pack at $US5.1 trillion ($A7.6 trillion), followed by Microsoft ($US3.8 trillion [$A5.7 trillion] and Nvidia ($US3.6 trillion [$A5.4 trillion]), among others. That does not count SpaceX and Anthropic, which also have joined the trillion-dollar club even though they aren’t in the S&P 500 index yet. By Matthew Bird November 19, 2026 A SpaceX Falcon 9 launch on Monday was visible over the Phoenix area. Shawn McCormick Tags: Science & Technology Audio By Carbonatix Wherever We're Needed. We're There. From the stories making headlines to the restaurants, music and culture that make Phoenix one of a kind, New Times is there. SpaceX is scheduled to launch a Falcon 9 rocket from southern California to deliver more Starlink internet satellites into low-Earth orbit in the evening of Thursday, Nov. 19, and there’s a chance we’ll be able to see it here in Phoenix. When will the next SpaceX launch happen? As of Thursday afternoon, the next SpaceX launch that we may be able to see in Arizona currently has a scheduled launch window of 9:33 p.m. tonight.
