records.excerpt: 11月19日、AI大手のAnthropicが米NASDAQに新規 上場しました 。初値は公開価格を34％上回る111.5ドルとなり、好調な滑り出しとなりました。 公開価格は1株83ドルで当初提示されていた70～78ドルの価格レンジを上回る水準でのIPOとなりました。 初日の取引では、時価総額が一時2兆ドルを突破。記事執筆時点では約1.23兆ドルとなっています。 Anthropicは、OpenAIの元研究者らによって設立されたAI企業で、AIチャットボット「Claude」シリーズで知られています。今回の上場は、フロンティアAIラボと呼ばれる最先端AI開発企業として世界初の株式公開であり、AI企業に対する投資家の評価を測る試金石になると見られています。 史上最大規模のIPOとなったAnthropicですが、ここ最近のAI業界には複数の不安要素がありました。NVIDIAのジェンスン・フアンCEOの辞任に加え、米中間選挙の結果を受けて、AIデータセンターへの規制が強化されるとの懸念も広がっていました。 そうした状況にもかかわらず、AnthropicのIPOに対する需要は市場の予想を上回りました。これは、AI関連企業への投資意欲が依然として根強いことを示す結果と言えそうです。 Anthropicの共同創業者兼社長であるダニエラ・アモデイ氏は、上場前のスピーチで「AIに不安を感じている方、自分にとって何を意味するか分からない方へ。この技術にはあなたが必要です。信頼でも利用でもなく、あなたの声が必要なのです」と 述べました 。これはAIの急速な発展に伴う社会的な懸念に対し、幅広い人々の声を開発に反映させる姿勢を示した発言といえます。 ちなみに、Anthropicの創業者らがかつて在籍していたOpenAIも、2027年のIPOを目指していると報じられています。AIモデル市場をめぐる競争は、今後も激しさを増しそうです。 Acer Swift Go 14 AI インテル Core Ultra 7 OLED 光沢 DCI-P3 100% WUXGA 16:10 32GBメモリ 1TB SSD 14インチ 23.5時間駆動 薄型軽量 1.24kg 207万画素 IR Webカメラ Wi-Fi 7 日本語キーボード Copilot＋PC スチームブルー ノートパソコン SFG14-75-A73Z ￥250,505 (価格・在庫状況は記事公開時点のものです) Amazon HP OmniBook7 Aero 13-bg 13.3インチ グレイシャーシルバー (BF8H6PA-AAAA) | ノートPC,AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 プロセッサ,32GBメモリ,1TB SSD,バッテリー最大15.5時間,軽量1.0kg,Windows11 Home,薄型軽量 ￥219,800 (価格・在庫状況は記事公開時点のものです) Amazon ASUS ノートパソコン Vivobook 14 M1407KA 14インチ AMD Ryzen AI 5 330 メモリ16GB SSD 512GB Microsoft 365 Personal (24か月版) 搭載 Windows 11 重量 1.54kg Webカメラ内蔵 Type-C給電対応 Copilot+PC M1407KA-AI5165BUSAM ￥159,800 (価格・在庫状況は記事公開時点のものです) Amazon Apple 2026 MacBook Pro - スペースブラック | 12コアCPU、12コアGPUのM6チップ搭載ノートパソコン。AIのためのパワフルなプラットフォーム、14.2インチLiquid Retina XDRディスプレイ、24GBユニファイドメモリ、1TBストレージ ￥372,041 (価格・在庫状況は記事公開時点のものです) Amazon Apple 2026 MacBook Air M5チップ搭載13インチノートブック：AIとApple Intelligence、13.6インチLiquid Retinaディスプレイ、16GBユニファイドメモリ、512GB SSDストレージ、12MPセンターフレームカメラ、日本語キーボード、Touch ID - ミッドナイト ￥224,800 (価格・在庫状況は記事公開時点のものです) Amazon

records.title: Stock indices get beat up with the Dow, S&P, Nasdaq and Russell indices all falling more than 2%
records.excerpt: US stocks closed sharply lower Thursday, with all five major indices down more than 2%. The S&P 500 was up as much as 1.3% early before reversing to close down 2.02%, its sixth straight loss. The Dow shed 1,101 points, and only one of its 30 stocks finished higher. Stock indices get beat up with the Dow, S&P, Nasdaq and Russell indices all falling more than 2% Stocks Greg Michalowski 13 hours ago , published 19/11/2026 at 09:25 PM Tags Stocks Summary The only victory was Anthropic. The rich get richer. US stocks closed sharply lower Thursday, with all five major indices down more than 2%. The S&P 500 was up as much as 1.3% early before reversing to close down 2.02%, its sixth straight loss. The Dow shed 1,101 points, and only one of its 30 stocks finished higher. Buyers had their shot early as demand for Anthropic lifted AI shares. That bid faded, and all seven Magnificent Seven stocks finished lower. Persistent inflation remains a headwind for valuations as investors weigh how long the Fed may need to keep policy tight. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 5.05% from 5.07% Wednesday, offering little relief for equities. investinglive.com US closing levels Dow Industrial Average −1,101.11 points (−2.19%) to 49,101.92 S&P 500 −147.83 points (−2.02%) to 7,175.80 Nasdaq Composite −550.69 points (−2.25%) to 23,879.20 Russell 2000 −59.18 points (−2.18%) to 2,655.13 Nasdaq 100 −599.21 points (−2.21%) to 26,517.05 Anthropic gives back much of its early gain Anthropic opened at $111.50, reached $115.10 and closed at $97.17. That was 17.07% above the $83 IPO price and 12.85% below its opening trade. The $81.34 billion offering was the largest on record. An offering that size can prompt investors to trim other holdings to make room, which may have added to the pressure on AI shares. No tears for the employees of Anthropic who on average are $40 million dollars richer today. Sellers controlled the breadth The S&P 500 had 446 decliners against just 37 advancers. On the Nasdaq, 2,578 stocks fell and 674 rose. Energy dropped 3.52%, health care lost 2.18% with all 45 names in the snapshot lower, and financials fell 1.11%. The Russell 2000’s 2.18% drop showed the pressure extended to small caps. Winners and losers Magnificent Seven — Amazon −3.87%, Alphabet −3.46%, Nvidia −3.30%, Meta −3.27%, Tesla −2.43%, Microsoft −1.97% and Apple −0.92%. AI and chip stocks — Nebius Group −9.39%, AMD −7.72% and CoreWeave −6.11%. Intel bucked the selling, gaining 1.92%. Other standouts — Ambarella +7.85%, Palo Alto Networks +6.42%, Western Digital +2.98% and CrowdStrike +2.71%. Other laggards — Zoom Communications −9.56%, Celsius −6.20%, Block −6.02%, DoorDash −5.80%, SharkNinja −5.75%, Nike −5.43% and Shopify −5.34%. Other winners...Anthropic Employees Anthropic’s IPO added roughly $7.7 million per employee in paper gains from the $83 offering price to the $97.17 first-day close. That lifted the estimated average value of employee equity awards from about $44 million to $52 million , before taxes. The estimate uses The Wall Street Journal’s tally of stock options and restricted stock across roughly 5,300 employees. wsj.com The $52 million is an average equity value. Actual cash proceeds are unknown, and the filing doesn’t disclose the median employee’s holdings. Awards vary widely, and vesting and lockups limit when employees can sell. Trading lesson. Use breadth to check the bounce. If the S&P or Nasdaq bounces next session, watch whether more stocks start participating and whether that improvement holds. A handful of large stocks can lift an index while most names are still under pressure. After a day when S&P 500 decliners outnumbered advancers by roughly 12 to 1, a sustained improvement in breadth would give buyers more evidence that they’re taking back some control. records.excerpt: After pricing its initial public offering at $83 per share, the AI giant is valued at $1.5 trillion dollars, surpassing SpaceX as the biggest IPO on record. Support WBUR Anthropic begins trading on the Nasdaq 05:29 Copy the code below to embed the WBUR audio player on your site <iframe width="100%" height="124" scrolling="no" frameborder="no" src="https://player.wbur.org/hereandnow/2026/11/19/anthropic-ipo-nasdaq"></iframe> Here & Now Newsroom November 19, 2026 Anthropic, the company behind the Claude artificial intelligence chatbot, is trading on the Nasdaq for the first time Thursday. After pricing its initial public offering at $83 per share, the AI giant is valued at $1.5 trillion dollars, surpassing SpaceX as the biggest IPO on record. Here & Now ’s Scott Tong talks with Ali Velshi , chief data reporter at MS NOW, and host of “The 11th Hour with Ali Velshi,” about the significance of the tech company’s debut on Wall Street. This segment aired on November 19, 2026.

records.excerpt: Title: S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow Jones Dip Amidst Anthropic IPO Debut URL Source: http://dmarketforces.com/sp-500-nasdaq-dow-jones-dip-amidst-anthropic-ipo-debut/ Final URL: https://dmarketforces.com/sp-500-nasdaq-dow-jones-dip-amidst-anthropic-ipo-debut/ Published Time: 2026-11-20T09:23:49+01:00 Markdown Content: Global markets endured a volatile session as Anthropic’s record-breaking initial public offering (IPO) debut failed to provide an “all-clear” for the AI theme. Wall Street remained volatile as doubts grew about the AI trade’s durability, with hawkish Federal Reserve commentary adding to investors’ cautious tone, First National Bank (FNB) said in a brief on Friday. The S&P 500 closed 2.02% lower, the NASDAQ lost 2.25%, and the Dow Jones ended the session down 2.19%, after early gains reversed around Anthropic’s debut. Nvidia (-3.30%) extended its decline amid a leadership crisis, while concerns over AMD’s (-7.72%) Chinese exposure compounded pressure. That reversal carried into Europe, where pharmaceuticals, utilities and insurers weakened alongside technology shares, with tariff uncertainty adding pressure. The FTSE 100 was down 0.93%, while the Euro Stoxx 50 fell 0.66%. The sell-off is deepening in Asia as disappointing technology earnings, US semiconductor restrictions and uncertain AI returns weigh on sentiment. The Hang Seng Index is trading 1.71% lower and the Nikkei 225 gave back 4.58% so far, while the ASX 200 closed down 1.58% amid recession concerns, softer labour data, and falling commodity prices. South African equities ended Thursday’s session in the red, with the SARB’s monetary policy decision as the dominant theme. The SARB held its benchmark repo rate at 7.25%, as was widely expected, but the tone was decidedly hawkish, and Governor Lesetja Kganyago warned that rate increases could resume in 2027 if inflationary pressures intensify. The SARB flagged upside risks to inflation, projecting it to peak at 5.4% in November, while keeping its 2026 GDP growth estimate unchanged at a modest 1.2%. This hold weighed on rate-sensitive Financials, which fell 1.20%, dragged lower by Sanlam, which dropped 7.8% after a weaker-than-expected 9M26 operating update. The broader All Share Index closed down 0.33%, while the Top 40 fell 0.35% – its eighth consecutive day of declines partly reflecting the global AI-driven equity selloff that weighed on Naspers, the index’s biggest drag, which fell 2.63%. As such, Industrials shed 0.83%. Resources were the sole bright spot, gaining 1.15%, supported by elevated precious metals prices (+1.20%) as gold continued to attract safe-haven demand amid the global equity rout. South African government bond yields, which had been rising for eight consecutive sessions, partially reversed after the decision. records.excerpt: Selling pressure is spreading well beyond technology stocks, raising concerns that Wall Street's recent pullback could develop into a more pronounced market correction. Free Article Explore Premium Services Stock Market Today, Nov. 19: Dow Plunges 1,100 Points as the S&P 500 Suffers Its 6th Straight Day of Losses Selling pressure is spreading well beyond technology stocks, raising concerns that Wall Street's recent pullback could develop into a more pronounced market correction. By RJ Fulton – Nov 19, 2026 at 4:50PM EST Wall Street's sell-off intensified on Thursday, November 19, as selling pressure spread across nearly every sector of the market. The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI -2.19% ) plunged more than 1,100 points, falling 2.19% to 49,097 and moving closer to correction territory. Meanwhile, the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC -2.02% ) fell 2.00% to 7,177, marking its sixth consecutive session of losses, while the Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC -2.25% ) dropped 2.23% to 23,886 as investors continued to retreat from growth stocks. Selling pressure extended beyond equities, with gold falling 2.10% to $3,663.50. The 10-year Treasury yield eased three basis points to 5.07%, offering little relief to equity markets. Energy and consumer staples were among the few sectors to finish in positive territory, gaining 0.14% and 0.04%, respectively, while industrials plunged 2.61%. Today's biggest moves Despite the broader market sell-off, Insmed ( INSM +20.58% ) surged 20.58% following reports that French pharmaceutical giant Sanofi ( SNY -2.25% ) is considering an acquisition of the biotechnology company. Palo Alto Networks ( PANW +6.42% ) also bucked the broader trend, gaining 6.42% after reporting stronger-than-expected quarterly earnings and announcing a $4.5 billion acquisition. Conversely, Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD -7.72% ) plunged 7.72% following a media report alleging ties to a blacklisted Chinese server manufacturer. The report adds another layer of regulatory uncertainty to a semiconductor industry already grappling with tightening U.S. export restrictions and deteriorating investor sentiment. What this means for investors Perhaps the most concerning development on Wall Street is how broadly selling pressure has spread. What initially appeared to be a pullback driven by elevated technology valuations is increasingly developing into a broader market downturn. Even Nvidia 's ( NVDA -3.30% ) exceptional quarterly earnings have failed to reverse sentiment, suggesting that concerns surrounding inflation, interest rates, and stock valuations are taking precedence over strong corporate results. Looking ahead, investors should pay particularly close attention to Treasury yields and the U.S. dollar. With the Federal Reserve signaling that further interest rate hikes may be necessary, persistently restrictive financial conditions could put additional pressure on corporate earnings and stock valuations heading into 2027. Walmart's ( WMT -1.04% ) upcoming quarterly earnings report will also provide an important assessment of consumer spending heading into the holiday shopping season. While recent results from Target ( TGT +0.92% ) and TJX Companies, Inc. ( TJX -0.63% ) have been encouraging, any signs of weakening consumer demand could introduce another headwind for equities. For a meaningful recovery to materialize, investors should look for improving market breadth, stabilizing Treasury yields, and the S&P 500 reclaiming its 200-day moving average. Until then, investors should be cautious about interpreting isolated rallies as signs of a broader market recovery. In the early minutes of availability, shares were trading at $111.50, a 33% premium over the $83 IPO price. Set on Wednesday, the IPO price was already higher than the projected range set by the company, which anticipated a price between $70 and $78 per share. All told, the offering will raise over $81 billion, directed to a combination of employees and the company’s own coffers. The IPO funding, together with existing fundraising and new private offerings timed to coincide with the company’s public market debut, will leave Anthropic with an expected $220 billion in cash reserves. As one analyst told TechCrunch , “Anthropic’s going to have more cash on hand than any company has ever had.” The share price continues to fluctuate, but the opening price would put the company’s market cap over $2 trillion, making it more valuable than Meta, Tesla, or Walmart. Only five companies boast a higher valuation by market cap: Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Microsoft. In a speech before the opening bell , Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei emphasized the company’s commitment to safety. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so, only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. records.title: At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development
records.excerpt: At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development | TechCrunch TechCrunch Desktop Logo TechCrunch Mobile Logo Topics Latest AI Amazon Apps Biotech & Health Climate Cloud Computing Commerce Crypto Enterprise EVs Fintech Fundraising Gadgets Gaming Google Government & Policy Hardware Instagram Layoffs Media & Entertainment Meta Microsoft Privacy Robotics Security Social Space Startups TikTok Transportation Venture More from TechCrunch Staff Events Startup Battlefield StrictlyVC Newsletters Podcasts Videos Partner Content TechCrunch Brand Studio Contact Us Image Credits: CHARLY TRIBALLEAU / Contributor (opens in a new window) / Getty Images AI At Nasdaq opening bell, Anthropic CEO recommits to pacing AI development Sarah Perez 8:19 AM PST · November 19, 2026 As Anthropic made its Wall Street debut on Thursday in the largest IPO in history, CEO Dario Amodei reaffirmed the company’s commitment to developing AI responsibly. In his speech ahead of the Nasdaq opening bell, Amodei vowed that the AI company would not bend to either business or political pressure and would “remain under human control.” Reading the speech from a printout, the CEO began by talking about Anthropic’s origins as a way to build powerful technology to help humanity — something that he said was inspired by the loss of his father to a disease that became curable just a few years later. He acknowledged that while human intelligence had made diseases like the plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world, there were still too few scientists with too little time to make progress in other areas of disease. AI, he said, could help with this by working in concert with humans to further medical progress. It’s telling that Amodei began with a story highlighting AI’s potentially lifesaving applications, since he’s warned repeatedly about the risks of advancing the technology too quickly. In September, Amodei drew headlines when he outlined a plan to pace AI development , which included things like coordinating with other leading companies on safety standards and embedding evaluators from third-party organizations to verify that companies were following their safety commitments. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, and xAI owner Elon Musk said they agreed with Amodei’s position, although few concrete commitments have been made. In this morning’s speech, Amodei again stressed the need to progress AI technology and the safety required in doing so. He referred to the “very real risks” of AI in the hands of bad actors, whether those were individuals or nation-states, and the potential for things like “economic disruption” and “losing control of AI systems.” Anthropic believes these risks are avoidable, he noted, as long as there are safeguards in place. Amodei said the company would continue to be invested in the work of AI alignment and testing, and developing new ways to understand AI behavior so it could remain under human control. “There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us,” he said. “The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed more so than it has already towards double and triple checking that those AI systems are safe and remain under human control.” “And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control,” Amodei concluded. His sister, Anthropic co-founder Daniela Amodei, echoed these sentiments in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, noting that while the risks were real, the promise of AI was also “incredible.” “We were really founded on this idea that it is our job to mitigate those risks, and I think we have to date done an incredible job doing that. We obviously have more work ahead of us, but we are deeply committed to safety,” she added. The full text of Dario Amodei’s opening speech is below: Thank you, Daniela. My co-founders and I started Anthropic because we believe that the most powerful technology of our time should be built for the benefit of humankind. Daniela and I lost our father to a disease that just a few years later became curable. I started my career in biology, hoping to help future cures come sooner. In the lab, I saw the vast thicket of complexity that scientists face when they’re trying to understand disease and develop new treatments. So many of the scientific tools that can cut through that thicket — tools for gene editing, tools for gene synthesis, tools for controlling brain cells with light — started as pure ideas. In other words, they came from thinking, from intelligence. Human intelligence has already made diseases like plague, smallpox, and polio history for most of the world. But progress in other diseases has been too slow for so many patients and their families. Going from a great idea to a treatment can take decades. It took many years from the first discovery of a strange repeating pattern in DNA to the approval of the first treatment for a disease using CRISPR. Nature is full of these patterns, but we’ve had too little intelligence to decipher most of them. Too few scientists with too [little] time. Now we can build that intelligence. Whether it’s protein folding, drug design, cancer genetics, or clinical trial administration, scientists across many areas of biology and medicine are finding Claude can help them do their research in a fraction of the time it would have taken just a couple of years ago. I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade. I don’t want to get ahead of myself. At this point, all we have are early results. Experiments and clinical trials will still take time, and although they involve slow and ponderous processes, I believe these processes can be substantially accelerated by AI. We hope that in the future fewer families miss a cure by a few years. Medicine is just a particularly vivid example, but there are many other applications of Claude. Our customers, the world’s most ambitious companies, nonprofits, and individual people, are already applying the intelligence we’ve built to stimulate economic growth, lift people out of poverty, protect democracy and free societies, even make everyday services like the DMV work better. We’re proud to work alongside them, and I’m extremely optimistic about what we can do together in the future. At the same time, we’ve always been honest that this technology has very real risks. These range from misuse of the technology by individuals or by nation-states to economic disruption to losing control of AI systems. We discuss these risks not because we think they are inevitable and we are building anyway, but because we think they are avoidable and we can avoid them. Avoiding them depends on the choices made by the people building AI. There is a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety. And an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic’s DNA from the start, from safeguards against biological and cyber risks to alignment training and testing to looking inside our models like an X-ray, Anthropic has pioneered methods for understanding and steering the behavior of AI and keeping it under human control. records.title: Anthropic shares open 34% above IPO price in Nasdaq debut after record listing
records.excerpt: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 in their Nasdaq debut on Thursday, 34% above their $83 IPO price, putting the Claude maker on track for a $2 trillion valuation (€1.8tn) after it raised $81.3 billion (€74bn) in the largest initial public offering in history. Shares in Anthropic, the AI firm behind the Claude models, opened 34% above their IPO price on the Nasdaq on Thursday, at $111.50 against $83, putting it on course for a $2 trillion (€1.8tn) valuation.It raised $81.3 billion (€74bn) in the biggest stock market listing ever, beating SpaceX's record raise back in June.That fully diluted value, up from $1.5 trillion (€1.36tn) at the IPO price, puts Anthropic roughly level with SpaceX, the world's sixth most valuable listed company.In a speech at Nasdaq's opening bell, CEO Dario Amodei stated: "I believe sufficiently powerful AI, working in concert with humans, could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade.""We will not bend to either business nor political pressure," Amodei added, as the company remains locked in a dispute with the Trump administration over military uses of its technology.President Daniela Amodei said Anthropic had been "a safety company since day one" and bore ultimate responsibility for training its AI models to be safe.Anthropic priced its shares above its initial $70 to $78 range and enlarged the offering to 980 million shares from 825 million. More than half of the roughly 1,200 institutional investors that bid for shares reportedly got none, with allocations heavily favouring US-based investors.About 15% of the public offering, or roughly $12 billion (€10.9bn) of shares, went to retail investors, according to Bloomberg citing people familiar with the deal.That is below the 20% maximum set out in the prospectus and SpaceX's roughly 20% retail allocation, but far above the norm.Investors including Nvidia, Google and AMD are also buying $26 billion (€23.6bn) of non-voting shares at the IPO price in a separate private placement, taking the total raised to $107.3 billion (€97.7bn).The Wall Street banks that ran the deal made an estimated $550 million (€501mn) in fees.What investors are buyingAnthropic was founded in 2021 by seven former OpenAI researchers and executives, including siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, now its CEO and president respectively.Its revenue jumped to about $17 billion (€15.4bn) in the third quarter from $1.4 billion (€1.27bn) a year earlier, and the company puts its annualised revenue at about $81 billion (€73.7bn) as of the end of October.It booked a $104 billion (€94.7bn) net loss in the first nine months of the year, but almost all of it stems from accounting revaluations that disappear once the company lists.Excluding stock-based pay and donations, its operations made a $2.5 billion (€2.27bn) profit in the third quarter.It has also committed at least $518 billion (€471bn) to cloud computing and infrastructure suppliers over roughly a decade.The founders keep 50.1% of the voting power, while a trust appoints four of the seven board members, a set-up a shareholder advocacy group says leaves investors with almost no voice.Anthropic is also locked in a dispute with the Trump administration, which in February ordered federal agencies to stop using its technology after the company refused to let Claude be used for mass surveillance of Americans or fully autonomous weapons.Retail investors in nine European countries, including France, Germany and Spain, were able to apply for shares through participating brokers.

records.excerpt: US stock futures climbed on Thursday as investors prepared for the stock market debut of artificial intelligence developer Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), following... Wall Street Futures Advance Ahead of Anthropic’s Record IPO as Fed Signals Further Rate Increases: Dow Jones, S&P, Nasdaq Fiona Craig Thu, 19 November 2026 at 2:51 am GMT-8 7 min read ANT ^GSPC ^IXIC ^NDX CL=F Trading floor of the New York stock exchange ©Carol M. Highsmith Archive, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division US stock futures climbed on Thursday as investors prepared for the stock market debut of artificial intelligence developer Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT), following a record $107.3 billion fundraising that valued the company at approximately $1.5 trillion. The anticipated listing provided support for technology shares, although uncertainty surrounding Federal Reserve interest rate policy and renewed tensions between the United States and Iran continued to influence financial markets. Indications from the grey market suggested Anthropic shares could begin trading between 20% and 26% above their $83 offering price. Meanwhile, oil prices advanced following reports that US President Donald Trump was considering further military strikes against Iran. Nasdaq Futures Gain 1.9% as Technology Shares Recover At 03:02 ET (08:02 GMT), Nasdaq 100 futures were up 504 points, or 1.9%, reflecting renewed investor interest in technology stocks ahead of Anthropic's debut. S&P 500 futures gained 81 points, equivalent to 1.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures advanced 354 points, or 0.7%. The gains followed a mixed session on Wall Street, where the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.4%, while the S&P 500 and Dow Jones finished lower. Nvidia (NASDAQ:NVDA) remained under pressure despite reporting stronger-than-expected earnings and providing an encouraging sales outlook earlier in the week. Shares in the semiconductor manufacturer have declined approximately 25% during November amid uncertainty following the unexpected resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang and concerns about the sustainability of artificial intelligence investment. Deutsche Bank analysts observed that recent market weakness had extended beyond the technology sector. "It was not just a technology story, and equity losses have become increasingly widespread over the last few sessions," the analysts said. Asian equities also reflected cautious sentiment, with a regional benchmark edging lower and Taiwanese stocks falling more than 4%, reflecting their substantial exposure to semiconductor and artificial intelligence companies. European markets opened modestly higher. Anthropic's $107.3 Billion Offering Establishes New Market Record Anthropic, the developer of the Claude artificial intelligence chatbot, was preparing to begin trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker ANT. The company raised a combined $107.3 billion through an expanded initial public offering and private placement, surpassing the record established by SpaceX earlier in 2026. The transaction valued Anthropic at approximately $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis. The company sold 956.4 million shares, while its co-founders offered an additional 23.6 million shares. The offering was priced at $83 per share, above the range previously presented to investors. According to Bloomberg News, grey-market indications pointed to a potential opening gain of between 20% and 26%. The scale of demand highlights investor interest in companies developing advanced artificial intelligence models, even as questions persist over the industry's long-term profitability. Anthropic's listing represents an important development for the sector because it offers investors direct exposure to a leading AI model developer rather than primarily to the semiconductor manufacturers and infrastructure providers supporting the technology. The market's response could provide an indication of whether investment interest is broadening towards commercial AI applications or shifting away from established infrastructure companies. Needham Highlights Anthropic's Long-Term Growth Potential Analysts at Needham expressed confidence in Anthropic's position within the expanding artificial intelligence market. "Growth opportunities like Anthropic rarely come along, and we believe the company belongs alongside major technology businesses such as Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft," the brokerage said. Needham described Anthropic as a leading provider in an AI market that could eventually represent 10% of the current $56 trillion global labour market. The assessment reflects expectations that artificial intelligence applications could capture a substantial share of expenditure currently associated with human labour. However, investors continue to evaluate whether growing demand for AI services will translate into sustainable profitability. The sector faces significant capital requirements, particularly for computing infrastructure, data centres and the development of increasingly sophisticated models. Anthropic's first trading session is therefore expected to attract considerable attention as investors assess valuations across the wider artificial intelligence industry. Federal Reserve Minutes Reinforce Expectations of December Rate Hike Beyond developments in technology shares, investors were assessing the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October policy meeting. The US central bank maintained its benchmark interest rate within a range of 3.75% to 4.00% at that meeting. However, the minutes indicated that policymakers remained concerned about inflation and broadly supported further monetary tightening. According to the document, "almost all" officials believed additional interest rate increases would be necessary in the coming months if economic conditions developed as expected. A "couple" of policymakers also considered a larger 50-basis-point increase appropriate if inflation developments proved "unfavourable." The comments reinforced expectations that the Federal Reserve would increase borrowing costs at its December meeting. CME Group's FedWatch tool indicated that investors were assigning a high probability to a rate increase of at least 25 basis points, although a larger adjustment remained possible. US Treasury yields reflected the more restrictive monetary policy outlook. The benchmark 10-year yield remained above 5%, while the two-year yield, which is particularly sensitive to interest rate expectations, moved higher. Rising bond yields can increase financing costs and place pressure on equity valuations, particularly among companies whose market values depend heavily on anticipated future earnings. Trump Reportedly Reviews Options for Further Strikes on Iran Geopolitical concerns also returned to the forefront following reports that President Donald Trump was considering additional military operations against Iran. The New York Times reported that Trump was reviewing intelligence concerning Tehran's military capabilities and requests from Israel for a renewed campaign. The newspaper cited US and Israeli officials familiar with the discussions. According to the report, Israeli officials believe Iran is rebuilding its missile and drone capabilities and advancing chemical and biological weapons programmes. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was reportedly seeking US participation in a military campaign involving four to seven days of airstrikes. However, Trump had not reached a final decision. The discussions have reportedly exposed differences within the US administration over the reliability of the intelligence and the potential consequences of renewed military action. Officials are also considering the economic impact of further conflict, including the possibility of higher energy prices. records.title: Why Are Nasdaq, Dow, S&P 500 Futures Trading Lower After Anthropic’s Debut?
records.excerpt: Anthropic has quickly become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading much above its allocation price of $83. ANT stock soared more than 17% at close, ending the session at $97.17 and taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion. Chipmakers posted a selloff despite the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia’s recent upbeat revenue forecast. Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management said expectations for Anthropic’s listing, which lifted the broader AI trade, were a case of “classic groupthink.”U.S. stock futures slipped overnight late Thursday as broader markets faced pressure following Anthropic’s (ANT) record debut on Nasdaq. As of 9:21 p.m. EST, Dow futures fell 0.24%, while the S&P 500 futures declined 0.21% and Nasdaq-100 futures slumped 0.59%. On Thursday, the three U.S. benchmark indexes closed lower. The Nasdaq Composite led the decline, shedding 550 points to end the session down 2.25%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 2.19% lower and the S&P 500 fell 2.02%. IndexMoveCloseDow Jones Industrial Average-2.19%49,097.06S&P 500-2.02%7,175.83Nasdaq Composite-2.25%23,879.20ANT IPO Fails To Lift AI TradeThis week, all eyes have been on Anthropic’s debut on stock markets, which began trading on Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker “ANT.” The Claude-maker has quickly become one of the most valuable public companies in the world after its shares began trading much above its allocation price of $83. ANT stock soared more than 17% at close, ending the session at $97.17 and taking its valuation to roughly $1.76 trillion. The AI company's Thursday debut on the Nasdaq, considered a crucial test for the AI industry, proved that plenty of excitement is still around. However, it squeezed the liquidity out of the rest of the stock market. Analyst Michaël van de Poppe said in a post on X that ANT stock would eventually see a selloff after its run-up in the first few days, after which liquidity would rotate toward other risk-on assets. “I would expect to see $NQ, $BTC and other assets to rally upwards from that liquidity injection alongside a drop in Oil and the Yields,” he said. Meanwhile, Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management said that the expectation for Anthropic’s listing lifting the broader AI trade was a case of “classic groupthink.”“My take: Today’s action isn’t an indictment of AI. It’s what happens when many were on the same side of the trade. Investors still want the exposure, and the $80B Anthropic raised will soon fund infrastructure and applications,” he said in a post on X. Mohamed El-Erian, chief economic adviser at Allianz, said in a post on X that Anthropic’s debut was making room for more AI trades. “For those surprised that the NASDAQ and other US stock market indices are down 1.5–2% (CNBC data below) while Anthropic is trading 20% above its IPO price, remember this isn't just about the promise of AI, but about making room for it,” he said. “In a narrow sense, investor financing of the mega-IPO involves making room by selling other holdings. In a broader sense, it mirrors what we have been seeing with yields: with no large borrowers reducing their use of the bond market, financing costs rise for everyone, hitting rate-sensitive sectors particularly hard,” he added. NVDA Extends Losing Streak, AMD Hits Back At Short-Seller ReportChipmakers posted a selloff despite the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia Corp.'s (NVDA) recent upbeat revenue forecast. NVDA shares fell more than 3%, extending losses to a sixth straight session, while Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) nearly 8% after short-seller Hunterbrook disclosed a short position in the company citing its reliance on a potentially risky business in China. AMD denied the allegations, saying in a statement that Hunterbrook’s “claims misrepresent AMD’s business practices and relationships.”Deutsche Bank strategist Binky Chadha believes that the market is now “very oversold,” even as growth and earnings remain strong.In a CNBC interview, Chadha said, “The broader market, whether you look at positioning, whether you look at valuation .. we are sort of completely washed out.” “It all started with a big rotation out of tech. … As the cycle has happened, we’ve unfortunately also gotten a lot of negative catalysts,” the strategist said, adding, “That has then bled into the wider market.” Why Are Gold, Silver Prices Falling?Meanwhile, the precious metals trade bled sharply on Thursday, with gold spot prices falling to their lowest level since Aug. 2025, slipping below $3,600 an ounce. Meanwhile, silver spot prices are currently trading at $42.38, also near Aug. 2025 levels.Rising Treasury yields and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike in December weighed on precious metals. Jurrien Timmer, Director of Global Macro at Fidelity, said in a post on X, “More Fed tightening amid a rising cost of capital lead to tightening financial conditions, which is what the investment clock shows. We are out of the sweet spot (9-12 o’clock) and into a regime where decelerating earnings growth meets tighter financial conditions. It’s not the end of the world but it’s also no longer all tailwinds.”He added that “This shift in the investment clock has not been lost on the dollar, which increasingly is looking like a base breakout. In my view this is also why gold has been falling. Gold needs monetary inflation to thrive, and global liquidity is decelerating.”On Friday, traders will be watching for November’s final reading of the University of Michigan’s consumer sentiment report. Trending Tickers To Watch Anthropic (ANT): Shares of the AI company surged more than 17% at close but fell more than 5% in the overnight session as some of the buying pressure following its record debut wore off. iShares Silver Trust (SLV): The silver-linked exchange-traded fund fell sharply overnight, losing more than 5% as the selloff in precious metals continued amid a growing liquidity squeeze.SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD): The gold-linked exchange-traded fund was on the retail radar amid a steep decline in the price of the yellow metal amid a rising dollar and Fed’s hawkish comments. Advanced Micro Devices Inc. (AMD): Shares of the chipmaker were on the retail radar amid a sharp selloff in AI-related names, defying expectations that Anthropic’s IPO would revive the sector. Nvidia Corp. (NVDA): California Attorney General Rob Bonta said on Thursday that his office had sent an investigative subpoena to the AI chipmaker over the former CEO, Jensen Huang, and his alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy, adding that such actions could violate California law if the company is found to have misled investors and the public.Other Market Trends Among ETFs tracking benchmark indexes, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust (DIA) edged lower in the overnight session. The 10-year U.S. Treasury yield was trading at 5.022%, while the 30-year yield was at 5.387%. The iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) was up 0.19% amid ‘bullish’ sentiment. Asian markets opened lower on Friday. South Korea's KOSPI, China’s SSE Composite index, Japan’s Nikkei 225 and Australian stocks all traded lower at the open. records.excerpt: US stocks suffered sharp losses during trading on Friday, as selling pressure swept across Wall Street, pushing the Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average significantly lower. BUSINESS 1 min read Add as Preferred Source US Stocks Suffer Sell-Off as Nasdaq, S&P 500 Drop Nearly 2%; Wall Street Fear Gauge Surges 15.4% Taarek Refaat Business · Fri 20 Nov 2026 | 06:30 AM US stocks suffered sharp losses during trading on Friday, as selling pressure swept across Wall Street, pushing the Nasdaq Composite, S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average significantly lower. The Nasdaq led the declines, falling 2.14% to 23,907.06 points, reflecting the scale of the selling pressure across the US equity market. The S&P 500 dropped 1.90% to 7,184.42 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 2.09% to 49,146.84 points. The simultaneous declines across all three major benchmarks highlighted the breadth of the market downturn, with investors facing mounting uncertainty and increased volatility. Monthly Losses Deepen Across Wall Street The latest sell-off has added to an already difficult month for US equities, with all three major indices recording substantial monthly declines. The Nasdaq Composite has fallen 9.53% so far this month, while the S&P 500 has lost 6.58%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average has also come under pressure, declining 5.45% over the same period. The figures point to increasingly widespread weakness across the US stock market, extending beyond individual sectors and highlighting the scale of the ongoing correction. Wall Street's Fear Gauge Surges 15.4% As equities tumbled, Wall Street's key volatility indicator surged, reflecting a sharp increase in investor anxiety. The CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), widely known as Wall Street's fear gauge, jumped 15.39% to 28.34 points. The sharp rise in the VIX signals heightened demand for protection against market volatility and reflects growing uncertainty among investors. The combination of steep equity losses and a rapidly rising volatility index underscores the increasingly defensive tone dominating US financial markets. Investors Face Mounting Market Uncertainty The latest declines mark a significant deterioration in the performance of major US equity benchmarks during the month. With the Nasdaq approaching a monthly loss of 10% and the S&P 500 and Dow Jones also posting substantial declines, market participants are closely monitoring developments that could influence investor sentiment and the direction of equities. #US Stocks #Dow Jones #SP 500 #Nasdaq #Wall Street Taarek Refaat Contributor at SEE News — Sada Elbalad English. records.excerpt: シラ、パナソニック・エナジー・オブ・ノースアメリカと長期オフテイク契約を締結し、米国内のバッテリー生産を支援 - 宮崎日日新聞DIGITAL 2026年11月20日(金) ログイン サイト内検索 紙面購読申込 ホーム プレスリリース 共同通信PRwire シラ、パナソニック・エナジー・オブ・ノー･･･ シラ、パナソニック・エナジー・オブ・ノースアメリカと長期オフテイク契約を締結し、米国内のバッテリー生産を支援 2026.11.20 09:43 【画像： https://kyodonewsprwire.jp/img/202611200639-O3-1yyDxSNO 】 米国国内のバッテリーサプライチェーンの強靭化と先端技術の発展を促進するため、Titan Silicon®シリコン・カーボン負極材を供給 米カリフォルニア州アラメダ--( BUSINESS WIRE )-- （ビジネスワイヤ） -- バッテリー技術および材料のリーディングカンパニーである シラ は、パナソニック・エナジー・オブ・ノースアメリカとの商業オフテイク契約を締結したと発表しました。本契約は複数年にわたるもので、長期的な商業関係の一環として、将来的に10億米ドルを超える取引となる可能性があります。シラは、ワシントン州モーゼスレイクの工場から、独自開発のTitan Silicon®シリコン・カーボン（Si/C）負極材を供給し、パナソニックのバッテリーセルの性能向上を支援します。また、本提携により、米国での製造業および建設関連の雇用創出も大幅に見込まれます。米国独自の技術とノウハウに裏打ちされたシラの国内負極材生産により、パナソニックとそのOEM顧客は、より安全で強靭かつ持続可能な国内サプライチェーンの構築に向けた道筋を得ることになります。 本プレスリリースではマルチメディアを使用しています。リリースの全文はこちらをご覧ください。： https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261118671697/ja/ 【画像： https://kyodonewsprwire.jp/img/202611200639-O4-QW5zW174 】 Sila, a leading battery technology and materials company, today announced a commercial offtake agreement with Panasonic Energy Corporation of North America. シラの共同創業者兼CEOであるジーン・ベルディチェフスキーは、「今回のオフテイク契約は、シラにとって重要な商業上の節目であり、モーゼスレイク工場が顧客認定取得後に主要な戦略的顧客向けの高性能材料を供給できる状態となり、必要に応じて生産を拡大できることを示すものです。パナソニックのような世界的な業界リーダーとの提携は、当社の技術を裏付けるものです。米国で開発・製造された負極材が米国製セルに組み込まれ、今後何年にもわたって重要産業を支えることになります」と述べています。 本契約は、次世代シリコン・カーボン負極材を米国内で製造することにより、米国の技術競争力と産業の強靭性を強化するための重要な一歩となります。また、シラとパナソニックは、両社のパートナーシップをさらに強化・発展させるため、知的財産分野でも協力していきます。 パナソニック・エナジー・オブ・ノースアメリカのCEOである高本泰明氏は、「モーゼスレイクでのシラの急速な進展、すなわち着工から生産開始に至るまでの取り組みは、非常に素晴らしいものです。同社の技術的リーダーシップは、当社が最高水準の品質と性能を実現するうえで、信頼できるパートナーであることを示しています。この協業は、北米のバッテリーサプライチェーンの強靭化に貢献するとともに、パナソニックの米国製造への取り組みを示すものです」と述べています。 今回発表された契約は、シラが米国防総省の戦略資本局（OSC）から最近14億米ドルの融資コミットメントを獲得したことに続くものです。確実性の高い商業オフテイク契約の確保は、事業全体における実行力と商業化への準備が整っていることを示す重要な節目であり、自然な次のステップです。また、シラが本契約およびその他の商業契約に対応するために生産を拡大することに伴い、ワシントン州モーゼスレイクの工場で製造・建設関連の雇用が約500人追加で創出されると見込まれています。 シラのモーゼスレイクにあるシリコン・カーボン負極材製造施設は、米国内のバッテリー製造の強化と重要なエネルギーサプライチェーンの確保において、重要な役割を果たすことが期待されています。独自のTitan Silicon Si/C負極材の現地生産を拡大することで、同施設は米国の製造業の競争力を強化し、地域におけるハイテク分野の雇用創出を促進するとともに、世界の電気自動車（EV）、AI、重要技術市場向けの安全で競争力のある北米のバッテリーサプライチェーンの基盤を築きます。 シラについて シラは2011年に設立されたバッテリー技術および材料の企業であり、重要産業およびフィジカルAIを支える製品を開発・製造しています。シラが開発したSi/C負極材技術「Titan Silicon®」は2021年に登場し、ドローン、衛星、電子機器、ロボット、AI、電気自動車などの性能向上に貢献しています。米国の知的財産とギガスケールの製造技術を組み合わせることで、各国が必要とする電力性能、サプライチェーンの安全性、コスト効率を実現しています。シラのバッテリー材料は、ワシントン州モーゼスレイクにある画期的な製造施設で生産されています。同社は8VC、アトレイデス・マネジメント、ベッセマー・ベンチャー・パートナーズ、コートゥー、インキュテル、マトリックス・パートナーズ、サッター・ヒル・ベンチャーズ、ティー・ロウ・プライス・アソシエイツが助言するファンドおよびアカウントから支援を受けています。 records.excerpt: Canada approves up to C$14M for Mactung - North of 60 Mining News Directory Photos Store About Contact Advertise Free Trial Subscribe Sign In The mining newspaper for Alaska and Canada's North Canada approves up to C$14M for Mactung North of 60 Mining News - November 17, 2026 A.J. Roan , Mining News | Last updated Nov 17, 2026 1:20pm 0 Share Fireweed Metals Corp. Fireweed expects to complete Mactung's updated feasibility study in early 2027 to support future mine licensing applications. Support targets engineering and processing studies for Yukon tungsten mine. Fireweed Metals Corp. Nov. 16 announced it has received conditional approval for up to C$14 million (US$9.8 million) in funding from Natural Resources Canada (NRCan) to advance its Mactung tungsten project in eastern Yukon toward a final investment decision. Situated approximately 200 kilometers (124 miles) northeast of Ross River near the Yukon-Northwest Territories border, Mactung covers roughly 38 square kilometers (15 square miles) and forms part of Fireweed's broader Macpass District, a 985-square-kilometer (380-square-mile) land package that also hosts the company's Macpass zinc-lead-silver project. Considered one of the world's largest undeveloped high-grade tungsten deposits, Mactung currently hosts 41.5 million metric tons of indicated resource averaging 0.73% (665 million pounds) tungsten trioxide (WO3), alongside 12.2 million metric tons of inferred resource averaging 0.59% (159 million lb) WO3, according to a 2023 calculation. Used extensively in defense, aerospace, advanced manufacturing, and other industrial applications, tungsten has not been produced from primary mines in North America since 2015, leaving the continent dependent on foreign supplies such as China, which accounts for roughly 80% of global primary production and has imposed restrictions on exports. Seeking to strengthen North American supplies of the metal, the U.S. Department of Defense in December 2024 awarded Fireweed $15.8 million (C$22.5 million) under Title III of the Defense Production Act to advance feasibility and technical studies at Mactung, supporting the company's efforts to move the deposit toward a potential mining operation. While that commitment focused on advancing Mactung itself, Fireweed's work across the district also includes planning for improvements to the North Canol corridor, which provides the primary overland access to Mactung and the neighboring Macpass project. Supporting preliminary engineering and planning for proposed road and power infrastructure upgrades along that route, NRCan in August 2025 finalized a C$12.9 million ($9.4 million) contribution through the Critical Minerals Infrastructure Fund, since renamed the First and Last Mile Fund. With those earlier commitments supporting its development plans, Fireweed launched an updated feasibility study at Mactung in March, followed by 2,100 meters of geotechnical and hydrogeological drilling during its 2026 field season, with the study targeting completion in early 2027 ahead of future mine licensing applications. Distinct from the earlier infrastructure contribution, the latest conditional funding comes through NRCan's Global Partnerships Initiative, a federal program supporting research, development, and investment in Canadian critical minerals projects as part of efforts to strengthen domestic and international supply chains. Subject to the completion of final due diligence, the contribution will support metallurgical testing and advancement of engineering designs to a tender-ready stage, providing additional technical and economic information needed for a final investment decision. In addition to those studies, Fireweed plans to assess the potential development of an ammonium paratungstate (APT) production facility, which would convert tungsten concentrate into an intermediate material used to manufacture tungsten metal and other products. "We are highly encouraged by NRCan's funding to support the advancement of Mactung," said Fireweed Metals President and CEO Ian Gibbs. "This investment underscores Canada's growing recognition that Mactung is a cornerstone asset within its critical minerals strategy and highlights the project's strategic importance in establishing a secure, reliable long-term source of tungsten." Speaking to the federal government's interest in advancing Canadian critical minerals production, Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Tim Hodgson pointed to Mactung's potential contribution to industries dependent on imported tungsten. "Today's investment in the Mactung Tungsten project will help advance one of the world's largest undeveloped high-grade tungsten deposits while strengthening supply chains for a mineral that is essential to defence, aerospace and advanced manufacturing," Hodgson said. Under the proposed funding arrangement, NRCan is not expected to impose commercial conditions restricting Fireweed's current business activities or potential future tungsten sales, while the company's management will oversee the supported work and provide periodic progress reports to federal program administrators. records.title: BioTech Social Welcomes Former Nasdaq Global Head of Listings Karen Snow to Advisory Board
records.excerpt:
BioTech Social Inc. (BSI), parent company of BioTech Funding Portal, today announced that Karen Snow, former Global Head of Listings at Nasdaq, has joined its Advisory Board.

Snow brings more than 30 years of experience across investment banking, capital markets, corporate strategy, governance, sales, and company growth. Her addition brings deep public- and private-market expertise to BSI as the company pursues its broader strategy of building financial infrastructure around life science innovation.

BioTech Funding Portal, BSI's SEC-registered and FINRA-member Regulation Crowdfunding portal, represents the company's first implementation of that strategy. The portal enables eligible life science companies to raise up to $5 million annually from retail investors under Regulation Crowdfunding. Over time, BSI intends to explore additional financial structures, tools, and vehicles designed around the distinctive capital needs of life science companies.

"Life science companies face a financing journey unlike almost any other industry," said Karen Snow. "They spend years advancing important science through research, clinical, and regulatory milestones before reaching traditional measures of commercial maturity. I'm excited to work with BioTech Social as it considers how new financing approaches can help promising companies access capital at different stages - ultimately positioning themselves for long-term success."

Snow currently provides strategic counsel to companies across the private and public markets. Previously, she held a series of senior leadership roles at Credit Suisse and Nasdaq, culminating as Global Head of Listings, where she led the exchange's global listings and capital markets business and advised public and private company executives and boards.

During her Nasdaq tenure, Snow led a business that oversaw more than 2,000 IPOs, supported more than 3,000 listed companies, and executed 185 exchange switches representing more than $1.5 trillion in market capitalization.

Before Nasdaq, Snow spent more than 18 years at Credit Suisse, where she held senior roles in investment banking and equities, including Managing Director and Head of New York Equity Sales. Earlier in her career, she worked in investment banking at Deutsche Bank. She holds an MBA from Georgetown University and a BS in Business from Babson College, where she currently serves on the Board of Trustees.

Building Financial Infrastructure Around the Science

BSI was formed around the premise that promising life science innovation can be constrained not only by translational uncertainty, but also by the availability and structure of capital.

That challenge is particularly evident in the life science "valley of death" - the period during which companies must continue funding research, clinical development, regulatory activities, and organizational growth, often before they generate meaningful commercial revenue or become candidates for traditional institutional financing.

"Karen understands the entire arc of company development and how capital needs change along the way," said Dr. Neva West, CEO and Co-Founder of BSI. "What matters is creating more opportunities for promising research to move forward so that its clinical potential can be validated. That is especially important for patients and communities waiting for new approaches to diseases where the unmet needs remain significant. Karen brings a perspective that can help us determine how the financial side of that journey can better support clinical development."

Snow's addition expands a multidisciplinary BSI Advisory Board whose members bring experience across biotechnology, healthcare, finance, technology, patient advocacy, communications, company building, and capital formation.

About BioTech Social Inc.

BioTech Social Inc. is building financial infrastructure around life science innovation. The company develops platforms, tools and financial structures intended to expand access to capital for biotechnology, pharmaceutical, medical technology, diagnostic, digital health and other life science companies. BioTech Social Inc. is the parent company of BioTech Funding Portal LLC. www.biotech.social

About BioTech Funding Portal

BioTech Funding Portal is an SEC-registered funding portal and FINRA member focused exclusively on life science companies raising capital under Regulation Crowdfunding. The portal enables eligible companies to raise up to $5 million in capital annually from individual investors while providing a broader population of investors access to private life science investment opportunities under Regulation Crowdfunding.

Investment opportunities offered through BioTech Funding Portal are speculative, illiquid and involve a high degree of risk, including the possible loss of the entire investment. This press release is for informational purposes only and does not constitute an offer to sell or solicitation of an offer to buy any security. Any securities offering conducted through BioTech Funding Portal is made only pursuant to applicable offering materials filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission. www.biotech.fund

leeann@biotech.social

records.title: Mexico Heavy Vehicle Sales Grow 26.8%, Light Vehicle Sales Rise 3...
records.excerpt: Mexico's heavy-vehicle wholesale sales and light-vehicle retail sales rose year over year in October. Mexico's heavy-vehicle wholesale sales and light-vehicle retail sales rose year over year in October. Written by Amir Richani for IIR News Intelligence (Sugar Land, Texas) Summary Mexico's heavy-vehicle wholesale sales and light-vehicle retail sales rose year over year in October. However, production and exports of light vehicles showed a mixed trend, while heavy vehicles continued to grow. According to Industrial Info Resources data, there are US$11.81 billion in potential automotive investments in Mexico. Wholesale, Retail Sales Up The Mexican government reported that wholesale sales of heavy vehicles reached 3,301 in October, a 26.8% increase from the same period last year. Meanwhile, retail sales of light vehicles reached 137,395 in October, 3.1% more than in the same month in 2025. Backing the strong sales of automobiles, Mexico's auto parts production reached a record US$85.82 billion from January through August 2026, up 8.31% from the same period in 2025. "There is very good economic news: the production of heavy vehicles and the sale of light vehicles in Mexico represent very good news for the country. We are closing September and October in a very good position," said Mexico President Claudia Sheinbaum. But Light Vehicle Production Down According to Mexico's statistics agency (INEGI), Mexico produced 302,803 light vehicles in October, 17.7% less than last year, while exports reached 258,137 light vehicles in October, a 17.9% drop compared to 2025. In terms of cumulative numbers, light vehicle production through October reached 3.25 million compared to 3.39 million during the same period in 2025. Exports also trended lower, with 2.79 million light vehicles exported through October, almost 95,000 fewer than during the same period last year. Even so, retail sales of light vehicles between January and October reached 1.29 million, 4.8% more than during the same period last year. From January to October, about 76.6% of light vehicles exports were destined to the U.S., followed by 12.1% to Canada and 2.7% to Germany, according to INEGI. Heavy Vehicle Production, Exports Grow Unlike light vehicles, heavy vehicle production and exports are both trending higher in 2026. In October, heavy vehicle production in Mexico reached 16,375 in 2026 compared to 7,131 vehicles in October 2025, according to INEGI. For exports, October's figure more than doubled that of 2025, at 13,518 this year compared to 5,221 last year. In terms of cumulative figures, Mexico produced almost 133,500 heavy vehicles in the first 10 months of the year compared to 113,299 in the same period of 2025. Total exports of heavy vehicles through October almost reached 112,000, a 20.2% increase compared to the same period in 2025. From January through October 2026, the United States received 93.0% of Mexico's heavy-vehicle exports, followed by Canada at 4.0% and Colombia at 1.9%. Mexico's Roles and Projects Mexico is one of the world's key car manufacturers. Its lower labor costs than those in the United States have made it attractive for North American companies to establish assets in Mexico, from where their products are exported to other countries. At the same time, Mexico's population of over 130 million also offers a significant domestic market. The automobile industry is expected to continue growing in Mexico, as Industrial Info Resources has mapped 407 projects , excluding maintenance, across the country representing US$11.81 billion. Of those projects tracked, 71 projects are ranked as high probability, 218 as medium probability and 115 as low probability. Key Takeaways Mexico's wholesale sales of heavy vehicles in October reached 3,301, a 26.8% y-o-y increase. Most Mexican exports of light and heavy vehicles were destined for the United States. Industrial Info Resources is tracking 404 automotive projects in Mexico representing US$11.81 billion in investments. About Industrial Info Resources

records.title: Canada real estate 2027: where selective investors will win
records.excerpt: Colliers flags industrial, multifamily and grocery retail as top bets as investors shift focus to income growth over yield compression Colliers flags industrial, multifamily and grocery retail as top bets as investors shift focus to income growth over yield compression By Steve Randall Nov 19, 2026 Share Canada enters 2027 with the foundations for a more active real estate investment market - but the recovery is conditional. Trade uncertainty with the United States, slower population growth following the pullback in immigration, and elevated financing costs remain real headwinds. Investors prepared to look through near-term noise are finding genuine opportunities, particularly in sectors where constrained supply, structural demand and income growth can deliver returns without relying on yield compression. According to the Colliers 2027 Global Investor Outlook - which draws on survey responses from more than 1,170 investors across 35 countries - Canada continues to attract international capital. American investment in Canadian commercial real estate remains strong, while some European and Middle Eastern investors are actively looking north for portfolio diversification . Industrial leads, retail defends, multifamily waits Industrial and logistics is the standout area of conviction. After two softer years, vacancy has begun to fall and larger leases are returning. Investor interest is broad: last-mile distribution leads preferences at 22%, followed by manufacturing and industrial parks at 20% and big-box and warehouse assets at 18%, according to Colliers' 2027 survey. Trade uncertainty remains a risk - particularly for automotive-dependent markets - but demand from precious metals, agriculture and energy is broadening the sector's growth base. Retail offers a particularly defensive income profile. Grocery-anchored formats dominate, accounting for 35% of retail selections among Canadian investors, with neighbourhood retail formats close behind at 32%, per the same survey. These assets combine strong leasing demand and limited new supply with relatively low exposure to trade disruption. Multifamily holds a firm second place in investor preferences, though the investment case is more nuanced. Slower population growth has weakened development underwriting, and Toronto's condo correction is adding shadow inventory that competes with purpose-built rental supply. Improving affordability and any normalisation of immigration flows would meaningfully strengthen the thesis but for now it remains a medium-term story rather than an immediate conviction play. Where the capital is going Canada's investor base is tilting decisively toward active strategies. Value-add accounts for 22% of deployment intentions and opportunistic strategies - including development - for 38%, according to Colliers. Combined, that is roughly 60% of investors positioned for hands-on value creation rather than stabilised core income. Flexible capital structures are gaining traction alongside direct equity, with real estate debt, joint ventures and recapitalisations all becoming more relevant as owners address refinancing needs. Gateway markets lead, but new corridors are emerging Investor interest remains concentrated in Toronto, Vancouver, Calgary and Montréal. But Colliers flags a set of emerging themes beyond those gateways. Defence and national security spending could channel capital toward Canada's Maritime provinces, where shipyards and naval bases are concentrated. Longer-term, major nation-building projects - pipelines, airport expansion and high-speed rail - could reshape economic activity and real estate demand well beyond 2027. For advisors and investors thinking about real assets on a 10-to-20-year horizon, these infrastructure corridors represent a structural tailwind worth factoring in. AI and infrastructure are reshaping what makes an asset investable Artificial intelligence is not only an occupier story - it is increasingly an infrastructure story. Access to power, fibre connectivity and planning approvals is now sitting alongside location and tenant profile as a determinant of where capital can be deployed. Colliers notes that data centre-adjacent uses accounted for approximately 15% of industrial leasing activity in the United States in 2026, and the spillover into Canadian industrial markets - particularly those with reliable power infrastructure - is a trend worth monitoring for advisors managing real asset allocations. The bottom line The 2027 opportunity in Canada is broader than a simple market rebound, but it is not a rising tide. As Reid Taylor, Head of Institutional Brokerage, Capital Markets at Colliers Canada, notes in the report: greater certainty around trade, population growth and financing could provide the catalyst for a broader recovery - but until it arrives, the market rewards discipline, selectivity and income focus. For advisors with client exposure to REITs, private real estate funds or alternative asset allocations, the Colliers findings point to three clear watchpoints: improving industrial fundamentals in Canada's major metros, defensive income from grocery-anchored retail, and the emerging infrastructure and defence investment thesis in markets beyond the traditional gateways. Source: Colliers 2027 Global Investor Outlook , based on a survey of more than 1,170 international investors across 35 countries. records.title: Nearly two years in: Canada auto plant the 'front line' in Trump's trade war
records.excerpt: Nearly two years into President Donald Trump's trade war with Canada, specific battlefields have emerged. One is an idle auto plant northwest of Toronto. The Brampton Assembly Plant produced Dodge models until 2023, when global auto giant Stellantis said the facility needed to be retooled for the electric vehicle future -- pausing work for nearly 3,000 employees with a pledge to resume production in 2025, making the Jeep Compass. Then Trump imposed tariffs to force companies to make vehicles exclusively in the United States. Stellantis said the Jeep Compass would instead be made in Illinois and, on November 9, announced it was selling the Brampton plant to Canadian defense company Roshel. On a cold, windy afternoon outside the nearly empty plant this week, furious Canadian autoworkers demanded action from Prime Minister Mark Carney. "We've given our lives to this company. There's nothing we haven't done," said Jason Watson, a skilled tradesman and union leader. "The federal government needs to step in and do everything they can to reverse this sale," he said, flanked by dozens of autoworkers who, he said, had passed up other opportunities because they believed the plant would re-open. The fight over the Stellantis plant has exposed trade war's intractable challenges. Carney has earned acclaim for standing firm against Trump, but experts say he has few options to defend an auto industry that developed in southern Ontario because of its proximity to the United States. If tariffs continue restricting Canada's access to the US market, more job losses could be coming. - 'They were not honest' - Carney says reliance on the United States has made Canada vulnerable and the country needs to diversify. A similar battle at a Hamilton, Ontario steel plant -- where the US-owner Cleveland Cliffs has threatened hundreds of job losses citing tariffs -- has further highlighted Canada's vulnerability. Carney is trying to expand overseas trade relations and supercharge domestic manufacturing, in part through a defense industrial strategy that envisions more than CAD$500 billion ($350 billion) in spending over the coming decade. Roshel makes armored vehicles and could profit from government contracts. But Ardis Snow, Unifor union chairperson at the plant, said Roshel cannot replace the jobs or wages provided by an auto giant, suggesting it would pay roughly half of Stellantis's CAD$45 per hour. "Mortgage companies aren't going to say, 'Hey, we know you just had your salary cut in half, so we're going to cut your mortgage in half,'" Snow told AFP. Snow, who began working at the plant nearly 40 years ago, said colleagues moved to cheaper parts of Canada during the retooling shutdown. They were preparing to return when Stellantis announced Jeep Compass production was moving to Illinois. "It felt like a gut punch," he told AFP. But Stellantis kept assuring the union it would assign a new model to Brampton. In August, it confirmed the sale talks with Roshel. "Not that you can always believe everything that a corporation ever says to you, but we didn't have reasons not to believe it," he said. "They were not honest." - 'The front line' - Ottawa's rhetoric towards Stellantis has been tough. Carney called the sale "a betrayal." But the company is giving no indication the sale could be reversed, suggesting it's focused on severance packages for workers through "a fair, negotiated resolution that supports affected employees and recognizes their years of service." Rallying with workers this week, the head of Canada's left-wing New Democratic Party, Avi Lewis, argued Carney should "compel" Stellantis to keep making cars in Brampton. "Once we lose this industrial capacity, it is gone," he said. Trump's "tariff war is an attack on Canada," Lewis added. "This is the front line in this fight." But University of Toronto industrial and labor policy expert Rafael Gomez stressed Ottawa's limited options. Stellantis was already struggling in a competitive global auto market. records.title: Anthropic tops $2t market cap after record-breaking IPO in its Nasdaq debut
records.excerpt: Title: Anthropic tops $2t market cap after record-breaking IPO in its Nasdaq debut URL Source: http://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202611/20/WS6aff9106e4b03ebf8519d921.html Final URL: https://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202611/20/WS6aff9106e4b03ebf8519d921.html Published Time: 2026-11-20T08:15:02+08:00 Markdown Content: ![Image 1](https://img2.chinadaily.com.cn/images/202611/20/6aff9caee4b03ebf746414cb.jpeg) People watch a screen showing the logo of Anthropic at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, the United States, Nov 19, 2026. [Photo/Xinhua] Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company and the maker of the Claude chatbot, made a stunning debut on the stock market on Thursday, becoming one of the world's most valuable public companies, with its market value briefly at $2 trillion in a record-breaking initial public offering that was the largest in history. The stock closed up 17 percent on its $83 IPO price at $97.17 per share on Thursday. The company opened on Nasdaq shortly after midday and traded under the ticker "Ant" at $111.50 per share. That price was 30.4 percent higher than the $83 per share that was set during its IPO on Wednesday, in a sign of widespread investor confidence, analysts said. Anthropic raised $81.3 billion in the IPO and sold 980 million shares at $83 each. It was also set to raise $26 billion, bringing its total to $107 billion. The five-year-old AI lab now ranks among the 10 companies with the largest market share, according to The New York Times. Its successful IPO saw its value double compared to what it was six months ago. After the opening, the stock swung up to $111.50 but slipped back down to $100 per share. The Nasdaq composite and S&P 500 also fell by 1 percent after a bullish start. At closing, Anthropic had a fully diluted market cap of approximately $1.8 trillion with over 846 million shares traded Thursday. It comes as a host of concerns had threatened to drag down the IPO, including the acceleration of the AI boom, data centers, speed of development and regulation. At Nasdaq, located in the heart of New York City's Times Square, Dario Amodei, co-founder and CEO, and his sister Daniela Amodei, co-founder and president, clapped and looked on as they rang the opening bell at 9:30 am EST. Dario Amodei, who had previously trained as a physicist, helped co-found the company in 2021 with a group of researchers who left OpenAI. Amodei used his speech at Nasdaq to address concerns about AI safety, vowing that his AI firm would "remain under human control". "There is much work still to be done, and the most difficult safety work lies ahead of us," he said. "The incredible talent of the company that has enabled us to build the most capable AI systems will need to be directed more so than it has already towards double and triple checking that those AI systems are safe and remain under human control. "And to state it unequivocally, we will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control," he added. Amodei's stance on AI regulation gained the support of industry stalwarts SpaceX's Elon Musk, OpenAI's CEO Sam Altman, and Google DeepMind chief Demis Hassabis, according to TechCrunch. The meteoric rise means that each of the seven founders has a stake in the company that could be worth up to an estimated $26.5 billion to $27 billion, according to The Times. Employees, who affectionately call themselves "Ants", could become decamillionaires and centimillionaires. Yet, as the IPO took place, a crowd of rowdy demonstrators from a few different human rights groups, including RAD collective, ACT UP and New York Communities for Change noisily protested outside with megaphones against AI. Ian Nielson, co-lead of RAD collective, held a protest sign that read "stop tech oligarchs". "I'm protesting here the concentration of power in the hands of very few tech oligarchs, and the fact that these companies are making extremely risky decisions about our future without our consent," Nielson told China Daily. "We can't just allow these companies to operate and develop these technologies completely independently with no oversight for any democratic institution," he said. Kenny Moll, a climate justice activist, was also protesting. He told China Daily: "So many people have so many concerns about AI, even the CEOs of these companies have expressed major concerns about this technology that I think there is such a shared understanding and connection and intertwinement of issues enveloped in this AI story that it just makes sense that a lot of people care about stopping it." Moll added: "There has not been enough regulations. … They're subsidized by our tax dollars. There needs to be a real set of restrictions and regulations made against these companies." Anthropic said in the nine months up to Sept 30 it had $33.24 billion in revenue against $2.545 in 2025, according to CNBC. Its net losses were $104 billion during that nine-month period. It had lost $25.1 billion over the same time in 2025, its prospectus said. Analysts said that the company's IPO could pave the way for others in AI, including its main rival OpenAI. Anthropic's Wall Street debut occurred just five months after SpaceX, Musk's company, went public in another record-setting IPO that raised $87.5 billion. Anthropic said it has always addressed safety concerns, even choosing not to make Claude available to the public over internal concerns about safety in 2022, launching it in March 2023. This led OpenAI to release ChatGPT earlier. Anthropic's co-founder Jack Clark said that the release date of superhuman AI researchers could be pushed up to 2027 as the development of AI continues at pace, The Times reported.

Despite Tether's assets exceeding liabilities, S&P warned that a market downturn could leave USDT undercollateralized. The agency also raised concerns about transparency, noting that despite a KPMG audit, detailed financial disclosures remain limited. Tether rejected S&P's assessment, criticizing the methodology and defending its reserve management. The stablecoin continues to maintain its dollar peg, supported by liquidity on exchanges, though direct redemptions are limited to large verified holders.
